body: Break forth into joy, sing together, ye waste places of Jerusalem: for the LORD hath comforted his people, he hath redeemed Jerusalem.
modernText: Break out into joy! Sing together, you waste places of Jerusalem; for Yahweh has comforted his people. He has redeemed Jerusalem.
message: Break forth into joy, like it can't be contained. A good day where the gladness kind of bursts out of you.

body: Arise, shine; for thy light is come, and the glory of the LORD is risen upon thee.
modernText: “Arise, shine; for your light has come, and Yahweh’s glory has risen on you.
message: Arise, shine, your light has come. A good day as that moment of the light actually arriving and you getting to stand in it.

body: For your shame ye shall have double; and for confusion they shall rejoice in their portion: therefore in their land they shall possess the double: everlasting joy shall be unto them.
modernText: Instead of your shame you will have double. Instead of dishonor, they will rejoice in their portion. Therefore in their land they will possess double. Everlasting joy will be to them.
message: Double for your trouble, everlasting joy. If today's good makes up for a hard stretch, this says that's the design.

body: The voice of joy, and the voice of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom, and the voice of the bride, the voice of them that shall say, Praise the LORD of hosts: for the LORD is good; for his mercy endureth for ever: and of them that shall bring the sacrifice of praise into the house of the LORD. For I will cause to return the captivity of the land, as at the first, saith the LORD.
modernText: the voice of joy and the voice of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride, the voice of those who say, ‘Give thanks to Yahweh of Armies, for Yahweh is good, for his loving kindness endures forever;’ who bring thanksgiving into Yahweh’s house. For I will cause the captivity of the land to be reversed as at the first,” says Yahweh.
message: Joy and gladness returning to a place that had gone quiet. A good day as the sound of life coming back.

body: And all the people went their way to eat, and to drink, and to send portions, and to make great mirth, because they had understood the words that were declared unto them.
modernText: All the people went their way to eat, to drink, to send portions, and to celebrate, because they had understood the words that were declared to them.
message: Great mirth, actual celebration, because they finally understood the good. A good day worth throwing a little party over.

body: Sing unto him, sing psalms unto him, talk ye of all his wondrous works.
modernText: Sing to him. Sing praises to him. Tell of all his marvelous works.
message: Sing, and talk about the good stuff. A good day as something worth bringing up, not just privately enjoying.

body: Glory ye in his holy name: let the heart of them rejoice that seek the LORD.
modernText: Glory in his holy name. Let the heart of those who seek Yahweh rejoice.
message: The heart rejoicing, not just the schedule going well. A good day that reaches the center of you, not just the surface.

body: Sing unto the LORD, all the earth; shew forth from day to day his salvation.
modernText: Sing to Yahweh, all the earth! Display his salvation from day to day.
message: Day to day, the good keeps arriving. Today is just the latest in a running series worth noticing.

body: Sing and rejoice, O daughter of Zion: for, lo, I come, and I will dwell in the midst of thee, saith the LORD.
modernText: Sing and rejoice, daughter of Zion; for, behold, I come, and I will dwell within you,’ says Yahweh.
message: Gladness because of a promised nearness. A good day as the warmth of knowing you won't be left alone in it.

body: And Mary said, My soul doth magnify the Lord,
modernText: Mary said, “My soul magnifies the Lord.
message: The soul magnifying, making the good bigger by paying attention to it. A good day gets even better when you actually savor it.

body: It was meet that we should make merry, and be glad: for this thy brother was dead, and is alive again; and was lost, and is found.
modernText: But it was appropriate to celebrate and be glad, for this, your brother, was dead, and is alive again. He was lost, and is found.’ ”
message: The father's line at the party: it was right to celebrate. A good day where the celebrating isn't excessive, it's exactly fitting.

body: And they, continuing daily with one accord in the temple, and breaking bread from house to house, did eat their meat with gladness and singleness of heart,
modernText: Day by day, continuing steadfastly with one accord in the temple, and breaking bread at home, they took their food with gladness and singleness of heart,
message: Ordinary meals eaten with gladness. A good day as the simple, uncomplicated joy of regular things done happily.

body: And when they were come up out of the water, the Spirit of the Lord caught away Philip, that the eunuch saw him no more: and he went on his way rejoicing.
modernText: When they came up out of the water, the Spirit of the Lord caught Philip away, and the eunuch didn’t see him any more, for he went on his way rejoicing.
message: Just going about the day, rejoicing. A good day as the quiet gladness that follows you down the road, no occasion needed.

body: And when he had brought them into his house, he set meat before them, and rejoiced, believing in God with all his house.
modernText: He brought them up into his house, and set food before them, and rejoiced greatly, with all his household, having believed in God.
message: A whole household glad together after a hard night. A good day shared with the people under your roof.

body: For the kingdom of God is not meat and drink; but righteousness, and peace, and joy in the Holy Ghost.
modernText: for God’s Kingdom is not eating and drinking, but righteousness, peace, and joy in the Holy Spirit.
message: Joy named as a core part of the whole thing, not an extra. A good day as a glimpse of what it's all actually about.

body: But thanks be to God, which giveth us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ.
modernText: But thanks be to God, who gives us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ.
message: Thanks for a victory already given. If today feels like a win, this says there's a bigger one underneath it.

body: Thanks be unto God for his unspeakable gift.
modernText: Now thanks be to God for his unspeakable gift!
message: A gift too good to fully put into words. A good day where the gratitude runs ahead of your ability to describe it.

body: Strengthened with all might, according to his glorious power, unto all patience and longsuffering with joyfulness;
modernText: strengthened with all power, according to the might of his glory, for all endurance and perseverance with joy,
message: Even endurance done with joyfulness. A good day where strength and gladness are quietly the same thing.

body: And every creature which is in heaven, and on the earth, and under the earth, and such as are in the sea, and all that are in them, heard I saying, Blessing, and honour, and glory, and power, be unto him that sitteth upon the throne, and unto the Lamb for ever and ever.
modernText: I heard every created thing which is in heaven, on the earth, under the earth, on the sea, and everything in them, saying, “To him who sits on the throne, and to the Lamb be the blessing, the honor, the glory, and the dominion, forever and ever! Amen!”
message: A picture of everything, everywhere, glad at once. Today's good mood as a small, early note in that enormous song.

body: Blessed is he whose transgression is forgiven, whose sin is covered.
modernText: Blessed is he whose disobedience is forgiven, whose sin is covered.
message: A lightness that comes from being forgiven, nothing hanging over you. A good day as the feeling of a clean slate.

body: Blessed is the man unto whom the LORD imputeth not iniquity, and in whose spirit there is no guile.
modernText: Blessed is the man to whom Yahweh doesn’t impute iniquity, in whose spirit there is no deceit.
message: Nothing held against you, the record clear. On a good day, this names the quiet relief of not being counted guilty.

body: Many, O LORD my God, are thy wonderful works which thou hast done, and thy thoughts which are to us-ward: they cannot be reckoned up in order unto thee: if I would declare and speak of them, they are more than can be numbered.
modernText: Many, Yahweh, my God, are the wonderful works which you have done, and your thoughts which are toward us. They can’t be declared back to you. If I would declare and speak of them, they are more than can be counted.
message: So many good things you couldn't count them all. A good day as just one you happened to catch out of an uncountable pile.

body: Blessed is he that considereth the poor: the LORD will deliver him in time of trouble.
modernText: Blessed is he who considers the poor. Yahweh will deliver him in the day of evil.
message: Gladness tied to caring for others. If today's good came from being kind to someone, this says that's a blessed way to live.

body: Come and see the works of God: he is terrible in his doing toward the children of men.
modernText: Come, and see God’s deeds— awesome work on behalf of the children of men.
message: An invitation to come look at the good up close. A good day as a reason to stop and actually notice what's happening.

body: O bless our God, ye people, and make the voice of his praise to be heard:
modernText: Praise our God, you peoples! Make the sound of his praise heard,
message: Praise meant to be heard, not muttered. On a good day, let the gladness be audible to someone.

body: But I will hope continually, and will yet praise thee more and more.
modernText: But I will always hope, and will add to all of your praise.
message: More and more praise, a gladness that keeps growing. A good day that adds to a running total instead of standing alone.

body: I will sing of the mercies of the LORD for ever: with my mouth will I make known thy faithfulness to all generations.
modernText: I will sing of the loving kindness of Yahweh forever. With my mouth, I will make known your faithfulness to all generations.
message: Mercies worth singing about forever. A good day as one verse in a very long, grateful song.

body: O come, let us worship and bow down: let us kneel before the LORD our maker.
modernText: Oh come, let’s worship and bow down. Let’s kneel before Yahweh, our Maker,
message: An invitation to pause and be grateful. A good day as a reason to stop rushing and just appreciate it for a second.

body: For the LORD is great, and greatly to be praised: he is to be feared above all gods.
modernText: For Yahweh is great, and greatly to be praised! He is to be feared above all gods.
message: Great things, greatly praised. On a good day, let the size of the response match the size of the good.

body: With trumpets and sound of cornet make a joyful noise before the LORD, the King.
modernText: With trumpets and sound of the ram’s horn, make a joyful noise before the King, Yahweh.
message: Joyful noise, trumpets and all. A good day where the gladness is allowed to be a little loud and unrefined.

body: Let the floods clap their hands: let the hills be joyful together
modernText: Let the rivers clap their hands. Let the mountains sing for joy together.
message: Even the rivers clapping, the hills singing. A good day where the whole landscape seems to be celebrating with you.

body: Know ye that the LORD he is God: it is he that hath made us, and not we ourselves; we are his people, and the sheep of his pasture.
modernText: Know that Yahweh, he is God. It is he who has made us, and we are his. We are his people, and the sheep of his pasture.
message: A good day grounded in belonging: you're known, you're cared for, you're part of a flock. Not alone in the gladness.

body: The LORD is merciful and gracious, slow to anger, and plenteous in mercy.
modernText: Yahweh is merciful and gracious, slow to anger, and abundant in loving kindness.
message: The character behind a good day: patient, kind, not quick to frustration. The gladness has a gentle source.

body: But the mercy of the LORD is from everlasting to everlasting upon them that fear him, and his righteousness unto children’s children;
modernText: But Yahweh’s loving kindness is from everlasting to everlasting with those who fear him, his righteousness to children’s children,
message: Mercy with no start date and no end date. A good day resting on something that was good long before you and will be after.

body: Bless the LORD, O my soul. O LORD my God, thou art very great; thou art clothed with honour and majesty.
modernText: Bless Yahweh, my soul. Yahweh, my God, you are very great. You are clothed with honor and majesty.
message: Talking to your own soul again: bless this, notice how great the good actually is. A good day worth stirring yourself to feel.

body: O god, my heart is fixed; I will sing and give praise, even with my glory.
modernText: My heart is steadfast, God. I will sing and I will make music with my soul.
message: A heart fixed, settled, ready to sing. A good day where the gladness feels steady, not fragile.

body: I will praise thee, O LORD, among the people: and I will sing praises unto thee among the nations.
modernText: I will give thanks to you, Yahweh, among the nations. I will sing praises to you among the peoples.
message: Gladness shared out loud, among people. A good day that doesn't stay private, it gets told.

body: His work is honourable and glorious: and his righteousness endureth for ever.
modernText: His work is honor and majesty. His righteousness endures forever.
message: The good work called honourable and glorious. A good day as evidence of something well-made on your behalf.

body: He hath made his wonderful works to be remembered: the LORD is gracious and full of compassion.
modernText: He has caused his wonderful works to be remembered. Yahweh is gracious and merciful.
message: Good things made to be remembered, not forgotten. A good day worth banking, so you can pull it back out later.

body: Praise ye the LORD. Praise, O ye servants of the LORD, praise the name of the LORD.
modernText: Praise Yah! Praise, you servants of Yahweh, praise Yahweh’s name.
message: An invitation to the ordinary, working people to be glad. A good day the regular folks get to fully enjoy.

body: O praise the LORD, all ye nations: praise him, all ye people.
modernText: Praise Yahweh, all you nations! Extol him, all you peoples!
message: The shortest psalm, one simple call: praise. A good day as the easy, uncomplicated gladness it describes.

body: The right hand of the LORD is exalted: the right hand of the LORD doeth valiantly.
modernText: The right hand of Yahweh is exalted! The right hand of Yahweh does valiantly!”
message: A victory line, the strong hand lifted high. If today feels like a win, this celebrates the strength behind it.

body: How sweet are thy words unto my taste! yea, sweeter than honey to my mouth!
modernText: How sweet are your promises to my taste, more than honey to my mouth!
message: Sweetness, actual pleasure, in the good. A good day as something to taste and enjoy, not just get through.

body: Then was our mouth filled with laughter, and our tongue with singing: then said they among the heathen, The LORD hath done great things for them.
modernText: Then our mouth was filled with laughter, and our tongue with singing. Then they said among the nations, “Yahweh has done great things for them.”
message: Laughter and singing, the sound of a genuinely good day. If today has some of that in it, let it fill your mouth.

body: Lift up your hands in the sanctuary, and bless the LORD.
modernText: Lift up your hands in the sanctuary. Praise Yahweh!
message: Hands lifted, an open posture. A good day as a reason to stop clenching and just receive it.

body: Praise ye the LORD. Praise ye the name of the LORD; praise him, O ye servants of the LORD.
modernText: Praise Yah! Praise Yahweh’s name! Praise him, you servants of Yahweh,
message: A straightforward call to be glad. On a good day, the simplest response is often the truest one.

body: O give thanks unto the God of heaven: for his mercy endureth for ever.
modernText: Oh give thanks to the God of heaven; for his loving kindness endures forever.
message: The last line of a psalm that repeats 'his mercy endures forever' twenty-six times. A good day drawing from a mercy that just keeps going.

body: How precious also are thy thoughts unto me, O God! how great is the sum of them!
modernText: How precious to me are your thoughts, God! How vast is their sum!
message: The thoughts toward you called precious, and too many to count. A good day as the warmth of being thought about kindly.

body: If I should count them, they are more in number than the sand: when I awake, I am still with thee.
modernText: If I would count them, they are more in number than the sand. When I wake up, I am still with you.
message: Woke up still accompanied, still thought of. A good day that starts with the quiet comfort of not being alone.

body: Great is our Lord, and of great power: his understanding is infinite.
modernText: Great is our Lord, and mighty in power. His understanding is infinite.
message: Great power behind a good day, more than the lucky timing it might seem like. The gladness has real weight under it.

body: Praise him with the sound of the trumpet: praise him with the psaltery and harp.
modernText: Praise him with the sounding of the trumpet! Praise him with harp and lyre!
message: The big finish of the Psalms: praise with everything you've got. A good day as a reason to pull out all the stops.

body: Praise him with the timbrel and dance: praise him with stringed instruments and organs.
modernText: Praise him with tambourine and dancing! Praise him with stringed instruments and flute!
message: Dancing, actual dancing. A good day where the gladness is allowed to move your whole body, not just your mood.

body: Praise him upon the loud cymbals: praise him upon the high sounding cymbals.
modernText: Praise him with loud cymbals! Praise him with resounding cymbals!
message: Loud cymbals, the opposite of restrained. A good day where quiet and polite isn't the only option for being glad.

body: And thou shalt rejoice in every good thing which the LORD thy God hath given unto thee, and unto thine house, thou, and the Levite, and the stranger that is among you.
modernText: You shall rejoice in all the good which Yahweh your God has given to you, and to your house, you, and the Levite, and the foreigner who is among you.
message: Rejoice in every good thing, not just the big ones. A good day as permission to count the small goods too.

body: And Hannah prayed, and said, My heart rejoiceth in the LORD, mine horn is exalted in the LORD: my mouth is enlarged over mine enemies; because I rejoice in thy salvation.
modernText: Hannah prayed, and said: “My heart exults in Yahweh! My horn is exalted in Yahweh. My mouth is enlarged over my enemies, because I rejoice in your salvation.
message: A song from someone who waited a long time for good news. If today's gladness came after a wait, you're in good company.

body: The LORD liveth; and blessed be my rock; and exalted be the God of the rock of my salvation.
modernText: Yahweh lives! Blessed be my rock! Exalted be God, the rock of my salvation,
message: A victory song after rescue. A good day as the exhale of 'it held, I'm okay, thank God.'

body: Even them will I bring to my holy mountain, and make them joyful in my house of prayer: their burnt offerings and their sacrifices shall be accepted upon mine altar; for mine house shall be called an house of prayer for all people.
modernText: I will bring these to my holy mountain, and make them joyful in my house of prayer. Their burnt offerings and their sacrifices will be accepted on my altar; for my house will be called a house of prayer for all peoples.”
message: Made joyful, not just allowed in. A good day where even the quiet, reverent moments are meant to be glad.

body: And the shepherds returned, glorifying and praising God for all the things that they had heard and seen, as it was told unto them.
modernText: The shepherds returned, glorifying and praising God for all the things that they had heard and seen, just as it was told them.
message: Ordinary workers going back to their jobs, but changed, glad. A good day that follows you back into the regular stuff.

body: And when he was come nigh, even now at the descent of the mount of Olives, the whole multitude of the disciples began to rejoice and praise God with a loud voice for all the mighty works that they had seen;
modernText: As he was now getting near, at the descent of the Mount of Olives, the whole multitude of the disciples began to rejoice and praise God with a loud voice for all the mighty works which they had seen,
message: A crowd that couldn't hold it in. A good day where the gladness is too big to keep to yourself.

body: But whosoever drinketh of the water that I shall give him shall never thirst; but the water that I shall give him shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life.
modernText: but whoever drinks of the water that I will give him will never thirst again; but the water that I will give him will become in him a well of water springing up to eternal life.”
message: A well inside you, springing up, not running dry. A good day as evidence of a source that keeps refilling.

body: Rooted and built up in him, and stablished in the faith, as ye have been taught, abounding therein with thanksgiving.
modernText: rooted and built up in him, and established in the faith, even as you were taught, abounding in it in thanksgiving.
message: Gratitude overflowing from somewhere deep and well-rooted. A good day where thankfulness is the natural overflow, not an effort.

body: Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly in all wisdom; teaching and admonishing one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing with grace in your hearts to the Lord.
modernText: Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly; in all wisdom teaching and admonishing one another with psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs, singing with grace in your heart to the Lord.
message: Singing in your heart, even quietly. A good day where there's a little background music to how you're feeling.

body: Continue in prayer, and watch in the same with thanksgiving;
modernText: Continue steadfastly in prayer, watching in it with thanksgiving,
message: Staying grateful, watchfully. A good day as a reminder to keep noticing the good instead of letting it slip by unthanked.

body: For what thanks can we render to God again for you, for all the joy wherewith we joy for your sakes before our God;
modernText: For what thanksgiving can we render again to God for you, for all the joy with which we rejoice for your sakes before our God,
message: So much joy you don't know how to thank enough. A good day where gratitude runs ahead of your ability to express it.

body: Wherein ye greatly rejoice, though now for a season, if need be, ye are in heaviness through manifold temptations:
modernText: Wherein you greatly rejoice, though now for a little while, if need be, you have been grieved in various trials,
message: Great rejoicing, even with hard things in the mix. A good day where the gladness is real and doesn't require everything to be perfect.

body: But rejoice, inasmuch as ye are partakers of Christ’s sufferings; that, when his glory shall be revealed, ye may be glad also with exceeding joy.
modernText: But because you are partakers of Christ’s sufferings, rejoice, that at the revelation of his glory you also may rejoice with exceeding joy.
message: Rejoicing now, with even more joy promised later. A good day as a down payment on gladness that keeps coming.

body: Saying, Amen: Blessing, and glory, and wisdom, and thanksgiving, and honour, and power, and might, be unto our God for ever and ever. Amen.
modernText: saying, “Amen! Blessing, glory, wisdom, thanksgiving, honor, power, and might, be to our God forever and ever! Amen.”
message: A pile-up of good words, a full-throated celebration. Today's gladness as a small echo of that enormous thanks.

body: O LORD, how great are thy works! and thy thoughts are very deep.
modernText: How great are your works, Yahweh! Your thoughts are very deep.
message: A spontaneous 'how great is this' moment. A good day as a reason to just marvel for a second at how good things can be.

body: O LORD, how manifold are thy works! in wisdom hast thou made them all: the earth is full of thy riches.
modernText: Yahweh, how many are your works! In wisdom, you have made them all. The earth is full of your riches.
message: So many good, wisely-made things, everywhere you look. A good day as one small, well-crafted piece of a very full world.

body: I will praise thee; for I am fearfully and wonderfully made: marvellous are thy works; and that my soul knoweth right well.
modernText: I will give thanks to you, for I am fearfully and wonderfully made. Your works are wonderful. My soul knows that very well.
message: Even on a day you feel completely average, this says you're not an accident. Wonderfully made still applies on the unremarkable Tuesdays.

body: For I know the thoughts that I think toward you, saith the LORD, thoughts of peace, and not of evil, to give you an expected end.
modernText: For I know the thoughts that I think toward you,” says Yahweh, “thoughts of peace, and not of evil, to give you hope and a future.
message: On a day with no clear plot, this quietly insists there's a direction to it. You don't have to see it to be in it.

body: Trust in the LORD with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding.
modernText: Trust in Yahweh with all your heart, and don’t lean on your own understanding.
message: For the in-between days when you can't quite read the situation. Permission to not have it figured out and be okay anyway.

body: In all thy ways acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy paths.
modernText: In all your ways acknowledge him, and he will make your paths straight.
message: You don't need the whole map on an ordinary day. Just the next ordinary step, and that's being quietly sorted out.

body: Not that I speak in respect of want: for I have learned, in whatsoever state I am, therewith to be content.
modernText: Not that I speak because of lack, for I have learned in whatever state I am, to be content in it.
message: Contentment learned, even in the plain, nothing-special state. A good verse for a day that's just... fine.

body: I know both how to be abased, and I know how to abound: every where and in all things I am instructed both to be full and to be hungry, both to abound and to suffer need.
modernText: I know how to be humbled, and I also know how to abound. In everything and in all things I have learned the secret both to be filled and to be hungry, both to abound and to be in need.
message: Steady in the highs and the lows and the flat middles. The skill of being okay in an unremarkable stretch.

body: And be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind, that ye may prove what is that good, and acceptable, and perfect, will of God.
modernText: Don’t be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind, so that you may prove what is the good, well-pleasing, and perfect will of God.
message: Even a plain day is quietly shaping you. Not every change is dramatic, some happen in the ordinary middle.

body: Therefore if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature: old things are passed away; behold, all things are become new.
modernText: Therefore if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old things have passed away. Behold, all things have become new.
message: On a day that feels like more of the same, this says something's actually being made new under the surface.

body: Thou wilt shew me the path of life: in thy presence is fulness of joy; at thy right hand there are pleasures for evermore.
modernText: You will show me the path of life. In your presence is fullness of joy. In your right hand there are pleasures forever more.
message: There's a path here, even when today feels like standing still. The ordinary ground you're on is still going somewhere.

body: Set your affection on things above, not on things on the earth.
modernText: Set your mind on the things that are above, not on the things that are on the earth.
message: For a day with nothing pulling your attention, a gentle nudge to point it somewhere worthwhile instead of just drifting.

body: And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose.
modernText: We know that all things work together for good for those who love God, for those who are called according to his purpose.
message: Even the unremarkable parts count toward something. The boring Tuesday is doing quiet work too.

body: Be still, and know that I am God: I will be exalted among the heathen, I will be exalted in the earth.
modernText: “Be still, and know that I am God. I will be exalted among the nations. I will be exalted in the earth.”
message: A verse built for a slow day. Being still isn't wasted time here, it's where the knowing happens.

body: For my thoughts are not your thoughts, neither are your ways my ways, saith the LORD.
modernText: “For my thoughts are not your thoughts, and your ways are not my ways,” says Yahweh.
message: On a day you can't make sense of where things are going, this says that's okay, the perspective you're missing isn't yours to have yet.

body: For as the heavens are higher than the earth, so are my ways higher than your ways, and my thoughts than your thoughts.
modernText: “For as the heavens are higher than the earth, so are my ways higher than your ways, and my thoughts than your thoughts.
message: The view from up there is wider than yours. A plain, confusing day looks different from a higher vantage you don't have access to.

body: A man’s heart deviseth his way: but the LORD directeth his steps.
modernText: A man’s heart plans his course, but Yahweh directs his steps.
message: You can plan the day all you want, and it'll still go how it goes. Oddly freeing on a day that didn't follow the plan.

body: The steps of a good man are ordered by the LORD: and he delighteth in his way.
modernText: A man’s steps are established by Yahweh. He delights in his way.
message: Even the unremarkable steps are ordered, not random. The ordinary walking is going somewhere on purpose.

body: To every thing there is a season, and a time to every purpose under the heaven:
modernText: For everything there is a season, and a time for every purpose under heaven:
message: A verse for the in-between season. Not every stretch is a highlight, and this says the quiet ones have their place too.

body: For we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus unto good works, which God hath before ordained that we should walk in them.
modernText: For we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus for good works, which God prepared before that we would walk in them.
message: On a day you feel kind of pointless, this says you were made with intention. The purpose doesn't clock out on slow days.

body: Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path.
modernText: Your word is a lamp to my feet, and a light for my path.
message: Just enough light for the next step, not the whole road. Which is usually all an ordinary day actually requires.

body: The thief cometh not, but for to steal, and to kill, and to destroy: I am come that they might have life, and that they might have it more abundantly.
modernText: The thief only comes to steal, kill, and destroy. I came that they may have life, and may have it abundantly.
message: Abundant life isn't only the big moments. It's also hidden in the plain, in-between days like this one.

body: He hath shewed thee, O man, what is good; and what doth the LORD require of thee, but to do justly, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy God?
modernText: He has shown you, O man, what is good. What does Yahweh require of you, but to act justly, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with your God?
message: A simple instruction for an ordinary day: be fair, be kind, stay humble. No grand gesture required.

body: And not only so, but we glory in tribulations also: knowing that tribulation worketh patience;
modernText: Not only this, but we also rejoice in our sufferings, knowing that suffering produces perseverance;
message: Even the flat, unremarkable patience of a slow day is building something. Nothing's wasted, even the dull stretches.

body: And patience, experience; and experience, hope:
modernText: and perseverance, proven character; and proven character, hope:
message: The ordinary days quietly stack into experience, and experience into hope. The boring middle is doing more than it seems.

body: If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally, and upbraideth not; and it shall be given him.
modernText: But if any of you lacks wisdom, let him ask of God, who gives to all liberally and without reproach, and it will be given to him.
message: For a day where you're not sure what to do with yourself, this says you can just ask for a little clarity. No shame in not knowing.

body: Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen.
modernText: Now faith is assurance of things hoped for, proof of things not seen.
message: On a day you can't see much happening, faith is holding the thing you can't see yet. The ordinary day still counts as part of the story.

body: But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you.
modernText: But seek first God’s Kingdom, and his righteousness; and all these things will be given to you as well.
message: One thing to orient around on an aimless day. When nothing feels urgent, this gives you a quiet north star.

body: Delight thyself also in the LORD: and he shall give thee the desires of thine heart.
modernText: Also delight yourself in Yahweh, and he will give you the desires of your heart.
message: Even a plain day has small delights in it. The verse just suggests you point your attention at them.

body: Commit thy way unto the LORD; trust also in him; and he shall bring it to pass.
modernText: Commit your way to Yahweh. Trust also in him, and he will do this:
message: Hand over the day, even the unremarkable one, and let it unfold. Less white-knuckling the ordinary.

body: Whether therefore ye eat, or drink, or whatsoever ye do, do all to the glory of God.
modernText: Whether therefore you eat, or drink, or whatever you do, do all to the glory of God.
message: Even the mundane stuff, eating, working, scrolling, can quietly mean something. The ordinary day gets to count.

body: And whatsoever ye do in word or deed, do all in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God and the Father by him.
modernText: Whatever you do, in word or in deed, do all in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God the Father, through him.
message: Permission for the regular, in-between day to matter. Nothing's too small or too plain to be part of something.

body: Being confident of this very thing, that he which hath begun a good work in you will perform it until the day of Jesus Christ:
modernText: being confident of this very thing, that he who began a good work in you will complete it until the day of Jesus Christ.
message: Even on a day where nothing visibly progresses, the work in you is still going. Slow is still moving.

body: But they that wait upon the LORD shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles; they shall run, and not be weary; and they shall walk, and not faint.
modernText: but those who wait for Yahweh will renew their strength. They will mount up with wings like eagles. They will run, and not be weary. They will walk, and not faint.
message: A verse for the waiting, in-between stretch. The flat days are where the strength quietly gets topped back up.

body: The LORD is good unto them that wait for him, to the soul that seeketh him.
modernText: Yahweh is good to those who wait for him, to the soul who seeks him.
message: Good even to those just waiting, not achieving. An ordinary day of holding steady still counts for something.

body: Surely goodness and mercy shall follow me all the days of my life: and I will dwell in the house of the LORD for ever.
modernText: Surely goodness and loving kindness shall follow me all the days of my life, and I will dwell in Yahweh’s house forever.
message: All the days, including the forgettable ones. Goodness is trailing you even on the days nothing happens.

body: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith,
modernText: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faith,
message: The good stuff grows slowly, in ordinary soil. A plain day is exactly where that quiet fruit is forming.

body: Meekness, temperance: against such there is no law.
modernText: gentleness, and self-control. Against such things there is no law.
message: Steadiness, gentleness, self-control, the unglamorous virtues. A regular day is where they actually get practiced.

body: The secret things belong unto the LORD our God: but those things which are revealed belong unto us and to our children for ever, that we may do all the words of this law.
modernText: The secret things belong to Yahweh our God; but the things that are revealed belong to us and to our children forever, that we may do all the words of this law.
message: On a day you can't figure out the bigger picture, this says some of it just isn't yours to know yet. You can let that be okay.

body: So teach us to number our days, that we may apply our hearts unto wisdom.
modernText: So teach us to count our days, that we may gain a heart of wisdom.
message: Even the ordinary days are worth counting, not wasting. A quiet reminder that a plain day is still one of your days.

body: Ye are the light of the world. A city that is set on an hill cannot be hid.
modernText: You are the light of the world. A city located on a hill can’t be hidden.
message: On a day you feel unremarkable, this says you're still giving off light. You don't have to feel bright to be it.

body: Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven.
modernText: Even so, let your light shine before men; that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father who is in heaven.
message: Even the small, ordinary good you do is seen. The regular day isn't invisible, it's quietly counting.

body: Behold, I will do a new thing; now it shall spring forth; shall ye not know it? I will even make a way in the wilderness, and rivers in the desert.
modernText: Behold, I will do a new thing. It springs out now. Don’t you know it? I will even make a way in the wilderness, and rivers in the desert.
message: Something new might already be starting, even on a day that feels like the same old thing. You might just not see it yet.

body: Shew me thy ways, O LORD; teach me thy paths.
modernText: Show me your ways, Yahweh. Teach me your paths.
message: A simple ask for a day without direction: just show me the next bit. You don't have to request the whole route.

body: Lead me in thy truth, and teach me: for thou art the God of my salvation; on thee do I wait all the day.
modernText: Guide me in your truth, and teach me, For you are the God of my salvation, I wait for you all day long.
message: Waiting all day, which is sometimes exactly what an ordinary day is. The waiting itself is a kind of trust.

body: Abide in me, and I in you. As the branch cannot bear fruit of itself, except it abide in the vine; no more can ye, except ye abide in me.
modernText: Remain in me, and I in you. As the branch can’t bear fruit by itself unless it remains in the vine, so neither can you, unless you remain in me.
message: On a day with nothing to strive for, this just says stay. Abiding isn't achieving, and it's enough.

body: I am the vine, ye are the branches: He that abideth in me, and I in him, the same bringeth forth much fruit: for without me ye can do nothing.
modernText: I am the vine. You are the branches. He who remains in me and I in him bears much fruit, for apart from me you can do nothing.
message: A strangely restful line for a low-output day. The results were never fully on you anyway.

body: For a day in thy courts is better than a thousand. I had rather be a doorkeeper in the house of my God, than to dwell in the tents of wickedness.
modernText: For a day in your courts is better than a thousand. I would rather be a doorkeeper in the house of my God, than to dwell in the tents of wickedness.
message: Even one ordinary day in a good place beats a thousand elsewhere. The plain day you're in might be worth more than it feels.

body: The LORD bless thee, and keep thee:
modernText: ‘Yahweh bless you, and keep you.
message: An old blessing that applies to the unremarkable days too. Blessed and kept, even on a Tuesday.

body: The LORD make his face shine upon thee, and be gracious unto thee:
modernText: Yahweh make his face to shine on you, and be gracious to you.
message: A face turned toward you with warmth, even when nothing special is happening. The ordinary day is still watched over kindly.

body: The LORD lift up his countenance upon thee, and give thee peace.
modernText: Yahweh lift up his face toward you, and give you peace.’
message: Peace offered on a plain day, not just a hard one. Sometimes the gift of an ordinary day is just that it's quiet.

body: But godliness with contentment is great gain.
modernText: But godliness with contentment is great gain.
message: Contentment called great gain, the quiet kind of rich. An ordinary, content day might be worth more than an exciting, restless one.

body: Boast not thyself of to morrow; for thou knowest not what a day may bring forth.
modernText: Don’t boast about tomorrow; for you don’t know what a day may bring.
message: On a day you can't see much coming, this says don't bother pretending you can. You only actually have today, which is fine.

body: He hath made every thing beautiful in his time: also he hath set the world in their heart, so that no man can find out the work that God maketh from the beginning to the end.
modernText: He has made everything beautiful in its time. He has also set eternity in their hearts, yet so that man can’t find out the work that God has done from the beginning even to the end.
message: Even the in-between, unfinished-feeling day has its time. Beautiful isn't always now, and that's allowed.

body: Whatsoever thy hand findeth to do, do it with thy might; for there is no work, nor device, nor knowledge, nor wisdom, in the grave, whither thou goest.
modernText: Whatever your hand finds to do, do it with your might; for there is no work, nor plan, nor knowledge, nor wisdom, in Sheol, where you are going.
message: Whatever the ordinary day hands you, just do that. No need for it to be meaningful, just done.

body: In the morning sow thy seed, and in the evening withhold not thine hand: for thou knowest not whether shall prosper, either this or that, or whether they both shall be alike good.
modernText: In the morning sow your seed, and in the evening don’t withhold your hand; for you don’t know which will prosper, whether this or that, or whether they both will be equally good.
message: Keep planting the small ordinary things, you don't know which will take. A low-stakes nudge to just keep showing up.

body: And whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord, and not unto men;
modernText: And whatever you do, work heartily, as for the Lord, and not for men,
message: Even the mundane task gets to be done with a little heart. Not because it's exciting, just because it's yours to do.

body: And that ye study to be quiet, and to do your own business, and to work with your own hands, as we commanded you;
modernText: and that you make it your ambition to lead a quiet life, and to do your own business, and to work with your own hands, even as we instructed you;
message: An underrated goal: a quiet, ordinary life, minding your own stuff. A plain day is basically this verse in action.

body: Let thine eyes look right on, and let thine eyelids look straight before thee.
modernText: Let your eyes look straight ahead. Fix your gaze directly before you.
message: On an aimless day, just look straight ahead at the next thing. You don't have to solve the whole horizon.

body: Ponder the path of thy feet, and let all thy ways be established.
modernText: Make the path of your feet level. Let all of your ways be established.
message: Pay attention to where your actual feet are going today. The small, ordinary steps are worth a glance.

body: There are many devices in a man’s heart; nevertheless the counsel of the LORD, that shall stand.
modernText: There are many plans in a man’s heart, but Yahweh’s counsel will prevail.
message: You had plans, the day had other ideas. This says the underlying thread holds even when your version doesn't.

body: The thoughts of the diligent tend only to plenteousness; but of every one that is hasty only to want.
modernText: The plans of the diligent surely lead to profit; and everyone who is hasty surely rushes to poverty.
message: The slow, steady, unglamorous effort is quietly adding up. A plain day of just doing the work counts.

body: Order my steps in thy word: and let not any iniquity have dominion over me.
modernText: Establish my footsteps in your word. Don’t let any iniquity have dominion over me.
message: A small ask for an ordinary day: just keep my steps straight. Not greatness, just not getting lost.

body: And thine ears shall hear a word behind thee, saying, This is the way, walk ye in it, when ye turn to the right hand, and when ye turn to the left.
modernText: and when you turn to the right hand, and when you turn to the left, your ears will hear a voice behind you, saying, “This is the way. Walk in it.”
message: On a day you're unsure which way to go, this promises a nudge when you need it. You'll hear it at the turn, not before.

body: Thus saith the LORD, Stand ye in the ways, and see, and ask for the old paths, where is the good way, and walk therein, and ye shall find rest for your souls. But they said, We will not walk therein.
modernText: Yahweh says, “Stand in the ways and see, and ask for the old paths, ‘Where is the good way?’ and walk in it, and you will find rest for your souls. But they said, ‘We will not walk in it.’
message: When a day feels directionless, sometimes the move is the tried-and-true path, not a new one. Rest in the familiar.

body: This book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth; but thou shalt meditate therein day and night, that thou mayest observe to do according to all that is written therein: for then thou shalt make thy way prosperous, and then thou shalt have good success.
modernText: This book of the law shall not depart from your mouth, but you shall meditate on it day and night, that you may observe to do according to all that is written in it; for then you shall make your way prosperous, and then you shall have good success.
message: The ordinary, repeated, daily practice is the point. Not a dramatic breakthrough, just steady attention over time.

body: And he humbled thee, and suffered thee to hunger, and fed thee with manna, which thou knewest not, neither did thy fathers know; that he might make thee know that man doth not live by bread only, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of the LORD doth man live.
modernText: He humbled you, allowed you to be hungry, and fed you with manna, which you didn’t know, neither did your fathers know, that he might teach you that man does not live by bread only, but man lives by every word that proceeds out of Yahweh’s mouth.
message: There's more to an ordinary day than its literal tasks. Something's feeding you underneath the to-do list.

body: But grow in grace, and in the knowledge of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ. To him be glory both now and for ever. Amen.
modernText: But grow in the grace and knowledge of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ. To him be the glory both now and forever. Amen.
message: Growth that happens slowly, on normal days, not just in big moments. A plain day is where most of it quietly occurs.

body: And beside this, giving all diligence, add to your faith virtue; and to virtue knowledge;
modernText: Yes, and for this very cause adding on your part all diligence, in your faith supply moral excellence; and in moral excellence, knowledge;
message: Character built by adding, bit by bit, on ordinary days. Nobody becomes anything in one dramatic leap.

body: And to knowledge temperance; and to temperance patience; and to patience godliness;
modernText: and in knowledge, self-control; and in self-control perseverance; and in perseverance godliness;
message: The unflashy virtues, patience, self-control, get built on unremarkable days. This is the gym where they're trained.

body: Do all things without murmurings and disputings:
modernText: Do all things without complaining and arguing,
message: A quiet challenge for a meh day: just do the stuff without complaining about it. Harder and better than it sounds.

body: Brethren, I count not myself to have apprehended: but this one thing I do, forgetting those things which are behind, and reaching forth unto those things which are before,
modernText: Brothers, I don’t regard myself as yet having taken hold, but one thing I do: forgetting the things which are behind, and stretching forward to the things which are before,
message: On an in-between day, permission to stop replaying the past and just face forward. The old stuff doesn't have to come along.

body: I press toward the mark for the prize of the high calling of God in Christ Jesus.
modernText: I press on toward the goal for the prize of the high calling of God in Christ Jesus.
message: Even a slow day is still pressing forward, however slightly. Progress doesn't require drama, just direction.

body: Therefore, my beloved brethren, be ye stedfast, unmoveable, always abounding in the work of the Lord, forasmuch as ye know that your labour is not in vain in the Lord.
modernText: Therefore, my beloved brothers, be steadfast, immovable, always abounding in the Lord’s work, because you know that your labor is not in vain in the Lord.
message: Steady, unmoved, keeping at it, the verse says. On an ordinary day, steadiness itself is the accomplishment.

body: But let every man prove his own work, and then shall he have rejoicing in himself alone, and not in another.
modernText: But let each man examine his own work, and then he will have reason to boast in himself, and not in someone else.
message: Just tend to your own stuff today, not the comparison game. A quiet day is a good day to stop measuring against everyone else.

body: For every man shall bear his own burden.
modernText: For each man will bear his own burden.
message: Carry your own ordinary load, no more and no less. A plain day where you just handle your part is enough.

body: For ye have need of patience, that, after ye have done the will of God, ye might receive the promise.
modernText: For you need endurance so that, having done the will of God, you may receive the promise.
message: Sometimes an ordinary day is just a patience day. Nothing happens, and the holding-on is the whole task.

body: Jesus Christ the same yesterday, and to day, and for ever.
modernText: Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever.
message: On a day where everything feels samey, there's something that's steadily, reliably the same, and that's actually a comfort.

body: Go to now, ye that say, To day or to morrow we will go into such a city, and continue there a year, and buy and sell, and get gain:
modernText: Come now, you who say, “Today or tomorrow let’s go into this city, and spend a year there, trade, and make a profit.”
message: A gentle poke at over-planning. You can map the week, but today is the only part you're actually living.

body: Whereas ye know not what shall be on the morrow. For what is your life? It is even a vapour, that appeareth for a little time, and then vanisheth away.
modernText: Whereas you don’t know what your life will be like tomorrow. For what is your life? For you are a vapor that appears for a little time, and then vanishes away.
message: Life called a vapour, here and gone. Oddly freeing on a plain day, nothing's that heavy if it's all this brief.

body: For that ye ought to say, If the Lord will, we shall live, and do this, or that.
modernText: For you ought to say, “If the Lord wills, we will both live, and do this or that.”
message: A humble way to hold your plans loosely. On an ordinary day, 'we'll see' is a perfectly fine posture.

body: Not slothful in business; fervent in spirit; serving the Lord;
modernText: not lagging in diligence; fervent in spirit; serving the Lord;
message: Keep a little fire going even in the routine. The ordinary work doesn't have to be done half-asleep.

body: One man esteemeth one day above another: another esteemeth every day alike. Let every man be fully persuaded in his own mind.
modernText: One man esteems one day as more important. Another esteems every day alike. Let each man be fully assured in his own mind.
message: Permission to just be settled in your own take on an ordinary day. You don't owe anyone a performance of certainty.

body: Except the LORD build the house, they labour in vain that build it: except the LORD keep the city, the watchman waketh but in vain.
modernText: Unless Yahweh builds the house, they who build it labor in vain. Unless Yahweh watches over the city, the watchman guards it in vain.
message: A reminder that the outcome was never fully on your shoulders. Takes some pressure off a normal working day.

body: Prepare thy work without, and make it fit for thyself in the field; and afterwards build thine house.
modernText: Prepare your work outside, and get your fields ready. Afterwards, build your house.
message: Just get the ordinary groundwork done, in order. A plain day is often exactly the day for the unglamorous prep.

body: Better is the end of a thing than the beginning thereof: and the patient in spirit is better than the proud in spirit.
modernText: Better is the end of a thing than its beginning. The patient in spirit is better than the proud in spirit.
message: Middles are awkward, ends are better. If today feels like an unremarkable middle, this says keep going, it improves.

body: Say not thou, What is the cause that the former days were better than these? for thou dost not enquire wisely concerning this.
modernText: Don’t say, “Why were the former days better than these?” For you do not ask wisely about this.
message: A nudge against romanticizing the past on a flat day. Today isn't worse, it's just today, and it counts.

body: They shall still bring forth fruit in old age; they shall be fat and flourishing;
modernText: They will still produce fruit in old age. They will be full of sap and green,
message: Fruit still coming, even in the later, quieter seasons. An ordinary stretch isn't a dead one, things are still growing.

body: Better is little with the fear of the LORD than great treasure and trouble therewith.
modernText: Better is little, with the fear of Yahweh, than great treasure with trouble.
message: Small and peaceful beats big and stressful. A plain, quiet day might be the better deal you don't always notice.

body: Better is a dry morsel, and quietness therewith, than an house full of sacrifices with strife.
modernText: Better is a dry morsel with quietness, than a house full of feasting with strife.
message: A dry crust in peace beats a feast in chaos. On an uneventful day, the quiet itself is the luxury.

body: Remove far from me vanity and lies: give me neither poverty nor riches; feed me with food convenient for me:
modernText: Remove far from me falsehood and lies. Give me neither poverty nor riches. Feed me with the food that is needful for me,
message: A prayer for just enough, nothing dramatic. The underrated goal of an ordinary, sufficient day.

body: For we brought nothing into this world, and it is certain we can carry nothing out.
modernText: For we brought nothing into the world, and we certainly can’t carry anything out.
message: A little perspective for a plain day: you came with nothing, you'll leave with nothing. Lightens the grip on all of it.

body: And having food and raiment let us be therewith content.
modernText: But having food and clothing, we will be content with that.
message: Food, clothes, enough. The verse sets a low, honest bar for contentment that an ordinary day usually clears.

body: Let your moderation be known unto all men. The Lord is at hand.
modernText: Let your gentleness be known to all men. The Lord is at hand.
message: Moderation, evenness, not too high or low. A good description of a steady, unremarkable day, and that's a fine way to be.

body: Give us this day our daily bread.
modernText: Give us today our daily bread.
message: Just today's bread, not the whole pantry. A small, grounding prayer for an ordinary day: enough for now is enough.

body: The LORD is my portion, saith my soul; therefore will I hope in him.
modernText: “Yahweh is my portion,” says my soul. “Therefore I will hope in him.”
message: On a day without much to show for it, this names a portion you still have. Your share isn't tied to how eventful today was.

body: Lord, my heart is not haughty, nor mine eyes lofty: neither do I exercise myself in great matters, or in things too high for me.
modernText: Yahweh, my heart isn’t arrogant, nor my eyes lofty; nor do I concern myself with great matters, or things too wonderful for me.
message: A refreshing verse for a small day: not everything has to be big. Permission to not engage with the great matters today.

body: Let Israel hope in the LORD from henceforth and for ever.
modernText: Israel, hope in Yahweh, from this time forward and forever more.
message: After all the calming down, just, keep hoping. On an ordinary day, quiet hope is enough to carry.

body: Rejoice not against me, O mine enemy: when I fall, I shall arise; when I sit in darkness, the LORD shall be a light unto me.
modernText: Don’t rejoice against me, my enemy. When I fall, I will arise. When I sit in darkness, Yahweh will be a light to me.
message: Not a dramatic rescue, just, you'll get back up, the light will come. Steady reassurance for an unremarkable low.

body: The sleep of a labouring man is sweet, whether he eat little or much: but the abundance of the rich will not suffer him to sleep.
modernText: The sleep of a laboring man is sweet, whether he eats little or much; but the abundance of the rich will not allow him to sleep.
message: An honest, earthy good: a solid day's work earns a good night's sleep. Simple, ordinary, and worth something.

body: That ye might walk worthy of the Lord unto all pleasing, being fruitful in every good work, and increasing in the knowledge of God;
modernText: that you may walk worthily of the Lord, to please him in all respects, bearing fruit in every good work and increasing in the knowledge of God,
message: Fruitful in the ordinary, everyday good work. A plain day of small right things is its own kind of fruitful.

body: But ye, brethren, be not weary in well doing.
modernText: But you, brothers, don’t be weary in doing what is right.
message: A quiet encouragement for the long, unremarkable middle: don't get tired of doing the small good things. They count.

body: For the LORD giveth wisdom: out of his mouth cometh knowledge and understanding.
modernText: For Yahweh gives wisdom. Out of his mouth comes knowledge and understanding.
message: On a day you're not sure how to handle something ordinary, this says wisdom is available for the asking. You don't have to already know.

body: Without counsel purposes are disappointed: but in the multitude of counsellors they are established.
modernText: Where there is no counsel, plans fail; but in a multitude of counselors they are established.
message: For a fuzzy decision on a plain day: you don't have to figure it out solo. Running it by a few people isn't weakness, it's wisdom.

body: Where no counsel is, the people fall: but in the multitude of counsellors there is safety.
modernText: Where there is no wise guidance, the nation falls, but in the multitude of counselors there is victory.
message: A quiet case for asking around before you decide. On an ordinary day, a second opinion can save a lot of trouble.

body: Commit thy works unto the LORD, and thy thoughts shall be established.
modernText: Commit your deeds to Yahweh, and your plans shall succeed.
message: Hand the ordinary work over and watch your scattered thoughts settle. A plain day runs smoother when you're not gripping the outcome.

body: Man’s goings are of the LORD; how can a man then understand his own way?
modernText: A man’s steps are from Yahweh; how then can man understand his way?
message: On a day you can't quite see where your life is going, this says that's normal. The path makes sense from somewhere you're not standing.

body: Be not wise in thine own eyes: fear the LORD, and depart from evil.
modernText: Don’t be wise in your own eyes. Fear Yahweh, and depart from evil.
message: A little humility for an ordinary day: you don't have to have the final take on everything. Permission to not know.

body: He that tilleth his land shall be satisfied with bread: but he that followeth vain persons is void of understanding.
modernText: He who tills his land shall have plenty of bread, but he who chases fantasies is void of understanding.
message: Do the plain, unglamorous work of your own patch, and you'll be fed. An honest verse for the ordinary grind.

body: Wealth gotten by vanity shall be diminished: but he that gathereth by labour shall increase.
modernText: Wealth gained dishonestly dwindles away, but he who gathers by hand makes it grow.
message: The slow way, bit by bit, is the one that actually lasts. A plain day of small steady effort is quietly building something.

body: In all labour there is profit: but the talk of the lips tendeth only to penury.
modernText: In all hard work there is profit, but the talk of the lips leads only to poverty.
message: Even the unexciting work has something to show for it. A reminder that the ordinary day's effort isn't wasted.

body: Seest thou a man diligent in his business? he shall stand before kings; he shall not stand before mean men.
modernText: Do you see a man skilled in his work? He will serve kings. He won’t serve obscure men.
message: The ordinary skill you quietly keep sharpening takes you further than you'd think. Diligence on plain days adds up.

body: He that tilleth his land shall have plenty of bread: but he that followeth after vain persons shall have poverty enough.
modernText: One who works his land will have an abundance of food; but one who chases fantasies will have his fill of poverty.
message: Tend your actual, ordinary responsibilities and there's enough. Less chasing the shiny thing, more working the ground you've got.

body: And also that every man should eat and drink, and enjoy the good of all his labour, it is the gift of God.
modernText: Also that every man should eat and drink, and enjoy good in all his labor, is the gift of God.
message: Even on a plain day, you're allowed to enjoy the fruits of ordinary work. Taking a little pleasure in it is the gift.

body: Wherefore I perceive that there is nothing better, than that a man should rejoice in his own works; for that is his portion: for who shall bring him to see what shall be after him?
modernText: Therefore I saw that there is nothing better than that a man should rejoice in his works; for that is his portion: for who can bring him to see what will be after him?
message: The realist's conclusion: enjoy what you do. On an unremarkable day, taking some satisfaction in your own work is the win.

body: Two are better than one; because they have a good reward for their labour.
modernText: Two are better than one, because they have a good reward for their labor.
message: A plain-day reminder that you don't have to do life solo. Ordinary days are better with someone in them.

body: For if they fall, the one will lift up his fellow: but woe to him that is alone when he falleth; for he hath not another to help him up.
modernText: For if they fall, the one will lift up his fellow; but woe to him who is alone when he falls, and doesn’t have another to lift him up.
message: The practical case for not isolating: someone to help you up when you stumble. Even a low-key day is steadier with company.

body: Then I commended mirth, because a man hath no better thing under the sun, than to eat, and to drink, and to be merry: for that shall abide with him of his labour the days of his life, which God giveth him under the sun.
modernText: Then I commended mirth, because a man has no better thing under the sun, than to eat, and to drink, and to be joyful: for that will accompany him in his labor all the days of his life which God has given him under the sun.
message: Even the skeptic lands on: enjoy the ordinary pleasures. A plain day is a fine day to eat something good and not overthink it.

body: I returned, and saw under the sun, that the race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong, neither yet bread to the wise, nor yet riches to men of understanding, nor yet favour to men of skill; but time and chance happeneth to them all.
modernText: I returned and saw under the sun that the race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong, neither yet bread to the wise, nor yet riches to men of understanding, nor yet favor to men of skill; but time and chance happen to them all.
message: A comforting leveler for an average day. It's not all about being the fastest or strongest; timing and chance play their part too.

body: Let us hear the conclusion of the whole matter: Fear God, and keep his commandments: for this is the whole duty of man.
modernText: This is the end of the matter. All has been heard. Fear God and keep his commandments; for this is the whole duty of man.
message: After all the searching, the conclusion is refreshingly simple. On an ordinary day, you don't need a grand philosophy, just the basics.

body: Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor standeth in the way of sinners, nor sitteth in the seat of the scornful.
modernText: Blessed is the man who doesn’t walk in the counsel of the wicked, nor stand on the path of sinners, nor sit in the seat of scoffers;
message: A plain day is a good day to notice whose advice you're taking. The quiet choices of who you listen to shape more than you'd think.

body: And he shall be like a tree planted by the rivers of water, that bringeth forth his fruit in his season; his leaf also shall not wither; and whatsoever he doeth shall prosper.
modernText: He will be like a tree planted by the streams of water, that produces its fruit in its season, whose leaf also does not wither. Whatever he does shall prosper.
message: Steady, rooted, fruitful in season, not every day. An ordinary day is just part of a slow, deep kind of growth.

body: He that walketh uprightly, and worketh righteousness, and speaketh the truth in his heart.
modernText: He who walks blamelessly and does what is right, and speaks truth in his heart;
message: The unflashy virtues, honesty, integrity, doing right. A plain day is exactly where those get quietly practiced.

body: Let the words of my mouth, and the meditation of my heart, be acceptable in thy sight, O LORD, my strength, and my redeemer.
modernText: Let the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart be acceptable in your sight, Yahweh, my rock, and my redeemer.
message: A small, grounding prayer for an ordinary day: let what I say and think be decent. A low-key aim that quietly shapes everything.

body: Examine me, O LORD, and prove me; try my reins and my heart.
modernText: Examine me, Yahweh, and prove me. Try my heart and my mind.
message: An honest, unglamorous ask: take a look at me, I'm open. A plain day is a fine time for a little self-honesty.

body: Teach me thy way, O LORD, and lead me in a plain path, because of mine enemies.
modernText: Teach me your way, Yahweh. Lead me in a straight path, because of my enemies.
message: Literally asking for a plain path. On an ordinary day, uneventful and straightforward is exactly what you want.

body: Thou shalt guide me with thy counsel, and afterward receive me to glory.
modernText: You will guide me with your counsel, and afterward receive me to glory.
message: On a day you can't see far ahead, this promises guidance as you go. You don't need the whole plan, just the next bit of counsel.

body: Teach me thy way, O LORD; I will walk in thy truth: unite my heart to fear thy name.
modernText: Teach me your way, Yahweh. I will walk in your truth. Make my heart undivided to fear your name.
message: A steady, ordinary request: just teach me, and I'll walk it. The quiet, daily kind of learning, not a dramatic revelation.

body: Lord, thou hast been our dwelling place in all generations.
modernText: Lord, you have been our dwelling place for all generations.
message: Something constant behind all the ordinary, forgettable days. A steady home that doesn't change with how eventful life is.

body: Before the mountains were brought forth, or ever thou hadst formed the earth and the world, even from everlasting to everlasting, thou art God.
modernText: Before the mountains were born, before you had formed the earth and the world, even from everlasting to everlasting, you are God.
message: On a day that feels small and passing, this points to something that doesn't. A little perspective, quietly steadying.

body: As for man, his days are as grass: as a flower of the field, so he flourisheth.
modernText: As for man, his days are like grass. As a flower of the field, so he flourishes.
message: A gentle reminder that life's brief, which somehow makes the plain days feel less like something to rush through.

body: Man goeth forth unto his work and to his labour until the evening.
modernText: Man goes out to his work, to his labor until the evening.
message: The whole ordinary rhythm of a day, out to work and back, in one line. Scripture noticing the plain daily grind, and giving it dignity.

body: A good man sheweth favour, and lendeth: he will guide his affairs with discretion.
modernText: It is well with the man who deals graciously and lends. He will maintain his cause in judgment.
message: Just handling your ordinary business with good sense. A plain day well-managed is its own quiet accomplishment.

body: Unto thee lift I up mine eyes, O thou that dwellest in the heavens.
modernText: I lift up my eyes to you, you who sit in the heavens.
message: On a day with your head down in the usual stuff, a small nudge to look up for a second. A quiet reset for an ordinary afternoon.

body: The eyes of all wait upon thee; and thou givest them their meat in due season.
modernText: The eyes of all wait for you. You give them their food in due season.
message: Provision that arrives on time, in due season, not early, not late. A plain day as part of a quietly reliable supply.

body: The way of the just is uprightness: thou, most upright, dost weigh the path of the just.
modernText: The way of the just is uprightness. You who are upright make the path of the righteous level.
message: The straightforward, level path of just doing right. On an ordinary day, uprightness looks a lot like the unremarkable next right thing.

body: This also cometh forth from the LORD of hosts, which is wonderful in counsel, and excellent in working.
modernText: This also comes out from Yahweh of Armies, who is wonderful in counsel, and excellent in wisdom.
message: Good counsel behind even the ordinary workings of things. A plain day is quietly being guided, not just drifting.

body: Thus saith the LORD, thy Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel; I am the LORD thy God which teacheth thee to profit, which leadeth thee by the way that thou shouldest go.
modernText: Yahweh, your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel says: “I am Yahweh your God, who teaches you to profit, who leads you by the way that you should go.
message: Led in the way you should go, even on an aimless day. The direction isn't all on you to figure out.

body: O LORD, I know that the way of man is not in himself: it is not in man that walketh to direct his steps.
modernText: Yahweh, I know that the way of man is not in himself. It is not in man who walks to direct his steps.
message: A relief on a day you feel directionless: steering your whole life was never fully your job. You can loosen the grip.

body: I the LORD search the heart, I try the reins, even to give every man according to his ways, and according to the fruit of his doings.
modernText: “I, Yahweh, search the mind. I try the heart, even to give every man according to his ways, according to the fruit of his doings.”
message: On a day no one really sees what's going on with you, this says someone does, all the way down. Known, even on the invisible days.

body: The light of the body is the eye: if therefore thine eye be single, thy whole body shall be full of light.
modernText: “The lamp of the body is the eye. If therefore your eye is sound, your whole body will be full of light.
message: What you fix your attention on shapes the whole ordinary day. A quiet suggestion to watch where your eyes keep landing.

body: Therefore whosoever heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them, I will liken him unto a wise man, which built his house upon a rock:
modernText: “Everyone therefore who hears these words of mine, and does them, I will liken him to a wise man, who built his house on a rock.
message: The wise life is built in ordinary, repeated actions, not dramatic ones. A plain day is where the foundation actually gets laid.

body: He that is faithful in that which is least is faithful also in much: and he that is unjust in the least is unjust also in much.
modernText: He who is faithful in a very little is faithful also in much. He who is dishonest in a very little is also dishonest in much.
message: The small, unremarkable faithfulness matters more than it looks. How you handle a plain day says a lot.

body: If ye know these things, happy are ye if ye do them.
modernText: If you know these things, blessed are you if you do them.
message: Knowing the good thing isn't enough, the happiness is in actually doing it. A plain day is a fine day to just do the small right thing.

body: For I say, through the grace given unto me, to every man that is among you, not to think of himself more highly than he ought to think; but to think soberly, according as God hath dealt to every man the measure of faith.
modernText: For I say through the grace that was given me, to every man who is among you, not to think of himself more highly than he ought to think; but to think reasonably, as God has apportioned to each person a measure of faith.
message: A grounding verse for an ordinary day: just have an honest, even read of yourself. No inflation, no deflation, just sober.

body: Moreover it is required in stewards, that a man be found faithful.
modernText: Here, moreover, it is required of stewards that they be found faithful.
message: The main ask isn't brilliance, it's faithfulness. On a plain day, just reliably handling what's yours is the whole assignment.

body: Let all things be done decently and in order.
modernText: Let all things be done decently and in order.
message: A quietly satisfying verse for an ordinary day: just do things decently, in order. Sometimes tidy and steady is the goal.

body: (For we walk by faith, not by sight:)
modernText: for we walk by faith, not by sight.
message: For a day you can't see where any of it's headed, this says that's the normal mode. Walking without the full view is just how it works.

body: See then that ye walk circumspectly, not as fools, but as wise,
modernText: Therefore watch carefully how you walk, not as unwise, but as wise,
message: Just move through the ordinary day with a little care and attention. Not dramatic wisdom, just not sleepwalking through it.

body: Redeeming the time, because the days are evil.
modernText: redeeming the time, because the days are evil.
message: Making something of the ordinary hours, not wasting them. A gentle nudge that even a plain day has time worth using.

body: Walk in wisdom toward them that are without, redeeming the time.
modernText: Walk in wisdom toward those who are outside, redeeming the time.
message: Wisdom in how you spend an ordinary day, in how you treat people. The unremarkable hours are still worth tending well.

body: Teaching us that, denying ungodliness and worldly lusts, we should live soberly, righteously, and godly, in this present world;
modernText: instructing us to the intent that, denying ungodliness and worldly lusts, we would live soberly, righteously, and godly in this present age;
message: A plain, steady way to live, soberly, decently, in the here and now. An ordinary day is exactly where this gets lived out.

body: The meek will he guide in judgment: and the meek will he teach his way.
modernText: He will guide the humble in justice. He will teach the humble his way.
message: Guidance offered to the humble, the ones not insisting they know. On a plain day, not having it figured out is actually the opening for direction.

body: All the paths of the LORD are mercy and truth unto such as keep his covenant and his testimonies.
modernText: All the paths of Yahweh are loving kindness and truth to such as keep his covenant and his testimonies.
message: Even the unremarkable path you're on is paved with mercy and truth. The ordinary road isn't a random one.

body: What man is he that feareth the LORD? him shall he teach in the way that he shall choose.
modernText: What man is he who fears Yahweh? He shall instruct him in the way that he shall choose.
message: On a day you're unsure of your next move, this says there's teaching available. You don't have to self-navigate every ordinary choice.

body: The secret of the LORD is with them that fear him; and he will shew them his covenant.
modernText: The friendship of Yahweh is with those who fear him. He will show them his covenant.
message: A quiet closeness offered on an ordinary day. Not fireworks, just the steady intimacy of being let in on something.

body: The counsel of the LORD standeth for ever, the thoughts of his heart to all generations.
modernText: The counsel of Yahweh stands fast forever, the thoughts of his heart to all generations.
message: Plans shift, days blur, but something underneath stays fixed. A steadying thought for a day that feels aimless.

body: Depart from evil, and do good; seek peace, and pursue it.
modernText: Depart from evil, and do good. Seek peace, and pursue it.
message: A simple, ordinary-day assignment: avoid the bad, do a little good, chase some peace. No heroics required.

body: I delight to do thy will, O my God: yea, thy law is within my heart.
modernText: I delight to do your will, my God. Yes, your law is within my heart.”
