message: Even the ordinary doing of the right thing can carry a quiet delight. A plain day where the small good feels less like a chore.

body: I will behave myself wisely in a perfect way. O when wilt thou come unto me? I will walk within my house with a perfect heart.
modernText: I will be careful to live a blameless life. When will you come to me? I will walk within my house with a blameless heart.
message: Just conducting yourself decently in the ordinary stuff, even when no one's watching. A plain day well-lived at home counts.

body: The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom: a good understanding have all they that do his commandments: his praise endureth for ever.
modernText: The fear of Yahweh is the beginning of wisdom. All those who do his work have a good understanding. His praise endures forever!
message: Wisdom starts somewhere humble, not with having all the answers. An ordinary day is a fine place to begin again.

body: I have chosen the way of truth: thy judgments have I laid before me.
modernText: I have chosen the way of truth. I have set your ordinances before me.
message: A quiet, repeated choice, not a dramatic one. On a plain day, just picking the honest path again is the whole move.

body: Make me to go in the path of thy commandments; for therein do I delight.
modernText: Direct me in the path of your commandments, for I delight in them.
message: An ask to be kept on a good, ordinary path. Not asking for excitement, just for the steady right direction.

body: I thought on my ways, and turned my feet unto thy testimonies.
modernText: I considered my ways, and turned my steps to your statutes.
message: A plain day is a good day to pause and consider where you're actually headed, then adjust. Small course corrections count.

body: Teach me good judgment and knowledge: for I have believed thy commandments.
modernText: Teach me good judgment and knowledge, for I believe in your commandments.
message: A humble ask for an ordinary day: just a little better judgment. You don't have to be wise, just teachable.

body: I remember the days of old; I meditate on all thy works; I muse on the work of thy hands.
modernText: I remember the days of old. I meditate on all your doings. I contemplate the work of your hands.
message: On a slow day, a gentle practice: look back and notice what's already been done. The quiet review is its own kind of steadying.

body: A wise man will hear, and will increase learning; and a man of understanding shall attain unto wise counsels:
modernText: that the wise man may hear, and increase in learning; that the man of understanding may attain to sound counsel:
message: The wise keep learning, even on ordinary days, even past the point they could coast. A plain day is a fine day to stay curious.

body: Happy is the man that findeth wisdom, and the man that getteth understanding.
modernText: Happy is the man who finds wisdom, the man who gets understanding.
message: Happiness tied not to excitement but to wisdom. A quiet, ordinary day is often where the steady kind of contentment lives.

body: Wisdom is the principal thing; therefore get wisdom: and with all thy getting get understanding.
modernText: Wisdom is supreme. Get wisdom. Yes, though it costs all your possessions, get understanding.
message: The main thing to get, over all the flashier pursuits. A plain day is a reminder that the steady, wise stuff matters most.

body: Keep thy heart with all diligence; for out of it are the issues of life.
modernText: Keep your heart with all diligence, for out of it is the wellspring of life.
message: Even on an uneventful day, your inner life is worth tending. Quietly guarding your heart is ordinary, important work.

body: Blessed is the man that heareth me, watching daily at my gates, waiting at the posts of my doors.
modernText: Blessed is the man who hears me, watching daily at my gates, waiting at my door posts.
message: Blessing tied to a daily, ordinary showing-up. Not a big moment, just the steady habit of paying attention.

body: The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom: and the knowledge of the holy is understanding.
modernText: The fear of Yahweh is the beginning of wisdom. The knowledge of the Holy One is understanding.
message: Wisdom begins with a little humility, available any ordinary day. You don't need a crisis to start getting wiser.

body: He that walketh uprightly walketh surely: but he that perverteth his ways shall be known.
modernText: He who walks blamelessly walks surely, but he who perverts his ways will be found out.
message: The plain, honest path is also the steady one. On an ordinary day, just doing right keeps your footing sure.

body: When pride cometh, then cometh shame: but with the lowly is wisdom.
modernText: When pride comes, then comes shame, but with humility comes wisdom.
message: Wisdom keeps company with the humble, not the loud. A quiet, unremarkable day is where it tends to show up.

body: He that walketh with wise men shall be wise: but a companion of fools shall be destroyed.
modernText: One who walks with wise men grows wise, but a companion of fools suffers harm.
message: Who you spend ordinary days around rubs off on you. A quiet reminder that the steady company you keep shapes you.

body: The simple believeth every word: but the prudent man looketh well to his going.
modernText: A simple man believes everything, but the prudent man carefully considers his ways.
message: Just paying a little attention to where you're headed. A plain day is a good day to look before you step.

body: The fear of the LORD is the instruction of wisdom; and before honour is humility.
modernText: The fear of Yahweh teaches wisdom. Before honor is humility.
message: Wisdom learned the humble way, in ordinary lessons. The quiet, un-glamorous order of growth: humility first.

body: He that is slow to anger is better than the mighty; and he that ruleth his spirit than he that taketh a city.
modernText: One who is slow to anger is better than the mighty; one who rules his spirit, than he who takes a city.
message: Self-control quietly outranks raw strength. On an ordinary day, keeping your cool is a bigger win than it looks.

body: The heart of the prudent getteth knowledge; and the ear of the wise seeketh knowledge.
modernText: The heart of the discerning gets knowledge. The ear of the wise seeks knowledge.
message: The wise keep quietly collecting knowledge, even on plain days. Learning as an ordinary, ongoing habit.

body: Hear counsel, and receive instruction, that thou mayest be wise in thy latter end.
modernText: Listen to counsel and receive instruction, that you may be wise in your latter end.
message: Just stay teachable, the verse says. On an ordinary day, being willing to take advice is the quiet path to wiser.

body: Apply thine heart unto instruction, and thine ears to the words of knowledge.
modernText: Apply your heart to instruction, and your ears to the words of knowledge.
message: Lean in and learn, even on an unremarkable day. The steady application, not the dramatic breakthrough, is what builds you.

body: Through wisdom is an house builded; and by understanding it is established:
modernText: Through wisdom a house is built; by understanding it is established;
message: Good things get built slowly, with wisdom, on ordinary days. A plain day is one more brick in something solid.

body: So shall the knowledge of wisdom be unto thy soul: when thou hast found it, then there shall be a reward, and thy expectation shall not be cut off.
modernText: so you shall know wisdom to be to your soul. If you have found it, then there will be a reward: Your hope will not be cut off.
message: Wisdom described as sweet to the soul, like honey. An ordinary day of quiet learning is nourishing in a way you don't always notice.

body: He that hath no rule over his own spirit is like a city that is broken down, and without walls.
modernText: Like a city that is broken down and without walls is a man whose spirit is without restraint.
message: Self-control as the walls that keep you steady. On a plain day, just keeping your own spirit in check is quiet strength.

body: Iron sharpeneth iron; so a man sharpeneth the countenance of his friend.
modernText: Iron sharpens iron; so a man sharpens his friend’s countenance.
message: A good conversation on an ordinary day can sharpen you. The quiet value of just talking things through with someone.

body: Where there is no vision, the people perish: but he that keepeth the law, happy is he.
modernText: Where there is no revelation, the people cast off restraint; but one who keeps the law is blessed.
message: Even a plain day benefits from a little sense of direction. A quiet nudge to keep some north star in view.

body: For God giveth to a man that is good in his sight wisdom, and knowledge, and joy: but to the sinner he giveth travail, to gather and to heap up, that he may give to him that is good before God. This also is vanity and vexation of spirit.
modernText: For to the man who pleases him, God gives wisdom, knowledge, and joy; but to the sinner he gives travail, to gather and to heap up, that he may give to him who pleases God. This also is vanity and a chasing after wind.
message: Wisdom, knowledge, and joy bundled together as gifts. A plain day is a fine time to receive the quieter ones.

body: For wisdom is a defence, and money is a defence: but the excellency of knowledge is, that wisdom giveth life to them that have it.
modernText: For wisdom is a defense, even as money is a defense; but the excellency of knowledge is that wisdom preserves the life of him who has it.
message: Wisdom as a kind of shelter, quietly protecting you. On an ordinary day, the steady, wise choices are guarding more than you see.

body: If the iron be blunt, and he do not whet the edge, then must he put to more strength: but wisdom is profitable to direct.
modernText: If the ax is blunt, and one doesn’t sharpen the edge, then he must use more strength; but skill brings success.
message: A practical note: a little wisdom makes the ordinary work go easier. Sharpening your approach beats just grinding harder.

body: The Lord GOD hath given me the tongue of the learned, that I should know how to speak a word in season to him that is weary: he wakeneth morning by morning, he wakeneth mine ear to hear as the learned.
modernText: The Lord Yahweh has given me the tongue of those who are taught, that I may know how to sustain with words him who is weary. He awakens morning by morning, he awakens my ear to hear as those who are taught.
message: Learning that happens morning by morning, ordinary and repeated. A plain day is just one more in a quiet, steady education.

body: For the vision is yet for an appointed time, but at the end it shall speak, and not lie: though it tarry, wait for it; because it will surely come, it will not tarry.
modernText: For the vision is yet for the appointed time, and it hurries toward the end, and won’t prove false. Though it takes time, wait for it; because it will surely come. It won’t delay.
message: If nothing seems to be happening, this says the timing isn't yours to rush. The ordinary waiting is part of the plan, not a delay in it.

body: For who hath despised the day of small things? for they shall rejoice, and shall see the plummet in the hand of Zerubbabel with those seven; they are the eyes of the LORD, which run to and fro through the whole earth.
modernText: Indeed, who despises the day of small things? For these seven shall rejoice, and shall see the plumb line in the hand of Zerubbabel. These are Yahweh’s eyes, which run back and forth through the whole earth.”
message: A verse that honors the unremarkable. Don't write off a plain day, the small-things days are where most of life actually happens.

body: It is good for a man that he bear the yoke of his youth.
modernText: It is good for a man that he bear the yoke in his youth.
message: The ordinary discipline of steady responsibility shapes you well. A plain day of just carrying your part is quietly forming something.

body: And Jesus increased in wisdom and stature, and in favour with God and man.
modernText: And Jesus increased in wisdom and stature, and in favor with God and men.
message: Even he grew up slowly, ordinary day by ordinary day. Steady, unremarkable growth is the normal, good way it happens.

body: Then spake Jesus again unto them, saying, I am the light of the world: he that followeth me shall not walk in darkness, but shall have the light of life.
modernText: Again, therefore, Jesus spoke to them, saying, “I am the light of the world. He who follows me will not walk in the darkness, but will have the light of life.”
message: Enough light to see by, even on an aimless day. You don't get floodlights, just enough to take the next ordinary step.

body: For as many as are led by the Spirit of God, they are the sons of God.
modernText: For as many as are led by the Spirit of God, these are children of God.
message: Led, quietly, even on a day you feel like you're just wandering. The guidance is often too subtle to notice until later.

body: Watch ye, stand fast in the faith, quit you like men, be strong.
modernText: Watch! Stand firm in the faith! Be courageous! Be strong!
message: A short, steadying charge for an ordinary day: stay alert, stand firm, keep your feet. No drama, just hold steady.

body: Study to shew thyself approved unto God, a workman that needeth not to be ashamed, rightly dividing the word of truth.
modernText: Give diligence to present yourself approved by God, a workman who doesn’t need to be ashamed, properly handling the Word of Truth.
message: Just do your ordinary work well enough to stand behind it. A plain day of honest, careful effort is the whole aim.

body: Wherefore, my beloved brethren, let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath:
modernText: So, then, my beloved brothers, let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, and slow to anger;
message: Three ordinary-day habits worth more than they look: listen more, talk less, cool down slower. Quietly life-improving.

body: But the wisdom that is from above is first pure, then peaceable, gentle, and easy to be intreated, full of mercy and good fruits, without partiality, and without hypocrisy.
modernText: But the wisdom that is from above is first pure, then peaceful, gentle, reasonable, full of mercy and good fruits, without partiality, and without hypocrisy.
message: A description of the good, quiet kind of wisdom: peaceable, gentle, reasonable. A steadying aim for an ordinary day's interactions.

body: As ye have therefore received Christ Jesus the Lord, so walk ye in him:
modernText: As therefore you received Christ Jesus, the Lord, walk in him,
message: Just keep walking the same steady way you started. On a plain day, consistency is the whole instruction.

body: Wait on the LORD, and keep his way, and he shall exalt thee to inherit the land: when the wicked are cut off, thou shalt see it.
modernText: Wait for Yahweh, and keep his way, and he will exalt you to inherit the land. When the wicked are cut off, you shall see it.
message: Wait, and keep walking the ordinary path, the verse says. On a slow day, steady patience is its own quiet accomplishment.

body: Lead me, O LORD, in thy righteousness because of mine enemies; make thy way straight before my face.
modernText: Lead me, Yahweh, in your righteousness because of my enemies. Make your way straight before my face.
message: A simple ask for an ordinary day: just keep the path clear and straight ahead. No need for a grand route, only a clear next step.

body: As for God, his way is perfect: the word of the LORD is tried: he is a buckler to all those that trust in him.
modernText: As for God, his way is perfect. Yahweh’s word is tried. He is a shield to all those who take refuge in him.
message: Even when your own day feels messy and unremarkable, the larger way you're on is sound. The plan holds even when the plot is dull.

body: He restoreth my soul: he leadeth me in the paths of righteousness for his name’s sake.
modernText: He restores my soul. He guides me in the paths of righteousness for his name’s sake.
message: Quiet restoration on an ordinary day, and a nudge back onto a good path. Nothing dramatic, just being gently set right.

body: Create in me a clean heart, O God; and renew a right spirit within me.
modernText: Create in me a clean heart, O God. Renew a right spirit within me.
message: A plain day is a fine day for a quiet reset. Not a big transformation, just asking to start fresh from here.

body: Behold, thou desirest truth in the inward parts: and in the hidden part thou shalt make me to know wisdom.
modernText: Behold, you desire truth in the inward parts. You teach me wisdom in the inmost place.
message: Honesty on the inside, where no one sees. A plain day is a good time to be real with yourself about how things actually are.

body: When I remember thee upon my bed, and meditate on thee in the night watches.
modernText: when I remember you on my bed, and think about you in the night watches.
message: The quiet thinking that happens at the end of an ordinary day. The plain, unremarkable moments are where a lot of the real reflection lives.

body: For thou art my hope, O Lord GOD: thou art my trust from my youth.
modernText: For you are my hope, Lord Yahweh, my confidence from my youth.
message: A long, steady trust, built over ordinary years, not one big moment. The quiet kind of hope that's just always been there.

body: I will meditate also of all thy work, and talk of thy doings.
modernText: I will also meditate on all your work, and consider your doings.
message: On a slow day, a gentle practice: turn things over, notice what's been done. Ordinary reflection as its own quiet work.

body: That they might set their hope in God, and not forget the works of God, but keep his commandments:
modernText: that they might set their hope in God, and not forget God’s deeds, but keep his commandments,
message: Just keeping your hope pointed somewhere steady, even on a plain day. A quiet anchor for the unremarkable stretch.

body: Thy word have I hid in mine heart, that I might not sin against thee.
modernText: I have hidden your word in my heart, that I might not sin against you.
message: The good you quietly store up on ordinary days is what you draw on later. A plain day is a fine time to stock the shelves.

body: I will meditate in thy precepts, and have respect unto thy ways.
modernText: I will meditate on your precepts, and consider your ways.
message: Ordinary, unhurried reflection, not a dramatic epiphany. The slow turning-over of good things on a quiet day.

body: Give me understanding, and I shall keep thy law; yea, I shall observe it with my whole heart.
modernText: Give me understanding, and I will keep your law. Yes, I will obey it with my whole heart.
message: A humble ask for a little more understanding. On an ordinary day, just getting it a bit more clearly is enough.

body: Turn away mine eyes from beholding vanity; and quicken thou me in thy way.
modernText: Turn my eyes away from looking at worthless things. Revive me in your ways.
message: A quiet ask to stop staring at the empty stuff. A plain day is a good day to notice where your attention's been leaking.

body: It is good for me that I have been afflicted; that I might learn thy statutes.
modernText: It is good for me that I have been afflicted, that I may learn your statutes.
message: An unexpected angle: even the hard stretches taught you something. A plain day of integrating those lessons counts.

body: The entrance of thy words giveth light; it giveth understanding unto the simple.
modernText: The entrance of your words gives light. It gives understanding to the simple.
message: Just a little light, enough to make the ordinary clearer. Not a spotlight, just enough to see the next plain step.

body: Set a watch, O LORD, before my mouth; keep the door of my lips.
modernText: Set a watch, Yahweh, before my mouth. Keep the door of my lips.
message: An ordinary-day prayer worth praying: help me not say the dumb thing. Quiet restraint is its own small victory.

body: Honour the LORD with thy substance, and with the firstfruits of all thine increase:
modernText: Honor Yahweh with your substance, with the first fruits of all your increase:
message: Even the ordinary handling of your money and stuff can mean something. A plain day where the small, practical choices count.

body: Her ways are ways of pleasantness, and all her paths are peace.
modernText: Her ways are ways of pleasantness. All her paths are peace.
message: Wisdom's ordinary ways are pleasant and peaceful, not dramatic. A plain, peaceable day is wisdom quietly at work.

body: Then shalt thou walk in thy way safely, and thy foot shall not stumble.
modernText: Then you shall walk in your way securely. Your foot won’t stumble.
message: Walk your ordinary way safely, steadily, without stumbling. A plain day where just keeping your footing is the whole thing.

body: Go to the ant, thou sluggard; consider her ways, and be wise:
modernText: Go to the ant, you sluggard. Consider her ways, and be wise;
message: The humble ant, just quietly doing its work. A plain day as a chance to admire, and copy, unglamorous steady effort.

body: In the multitude of words there wanteth not sin: but he that refraineth his lips is wise.
modernText: In the multitude of words there is no lack of disobedience, but he who restrains his lips does wisely.
message: Sometimes the wise move on an ordinary day is just saying less. Quiet restraint, underrated and easy to practice today.

body: The way of a fool is right in his own eyes: but he that hearkeneth unto counsel is wise.
modernText: The way of a fool is right in his own eyes, but he who is wise listens to counsel.
message: Being willing to take advice, even on small ordinary decisions. A plain day is a low-stakes place to practice listening.

body: The soul of the sluggard desireth, and hath nothing: but the soul of the diligent shall be made fat.
modernText: The soul of the sluggard desires, and has nothing, but the desire of the diligent shall be fully satisfied.
message: The steady, diligent approach quietly pays off. A plain day of just keeping at it is doing more than it seems.

body: A wise man feareth, and departeth from evil: but the fool rageth, and is confident.
modernText: A wise man fears and shuns evil, but the fool is hot headed and reckless.
message: A little healthy caution on an ordinary day. Wisdom often looks like simply steering clear of the obvious trouble.

body: A soft answer turneth away wrath: but grievous words stir up anger.
modernText: A gentle answer turns away wrath, but a harsh word stirs up anger.
message: One of the most practical verses for any ordinary day: answer gently, and watch tension drop. Small choice, big effect.

body: A man hath joy by the answer of his mouth: and a word spoken in due season, how good is it!
modernText: Joy comes to a man with the reply of his mouth. How good is a word at the right time!
message: The right thing said at the right ordinary moment. A plain day as a chance to offer someone a well-timed, good word.

body: Pride goeth before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall.
modernText: Pride goes before destruction, and an arrogant spirit before a fall.
message: A quiet check for an ordinary day: keep the ego in proportion. Staying humble on the plain days prevents trouble on the bigger ones.

body: He that hath knowledge spareth his words: and a man of understanding is of an excellent spirit.
modernText: He who spares his words has knowledge. He who is even tempered is a man of understanding.
message: Knowing when to hold back is its own kind of wisdom. An ordinary day is a fine place to practice the measured response.

body: He that getteth wisdom loveth his own soul: he that keepeth understanding shall find good.
modernText: He who gets wisdom loves his own soul. He who keeps understanding shall find good.
message: Getting a little wiser is a way of being good to yourself. A plain day of quiet learning is self-care that doesn't look like it.

body: He that followeth after righteousness and mercy findeth life, righteousness, and honour.
modernText: He who follows after righteousness and kindness finds life, righteousness, and honor.
message: Just keep doing right and being kind, ordinary day after ordinary day. The verse promises that steady path leads somewhere good.

body: A prudent man foreseeth the evil, and hideth himself: but the simple pass on, and are punished.
modernText: A prudent man sees danger and hides himself; but the simple pass on, and suffer for it.
message: A little foresight on a plain day, seeing the small problem before it grows. Quiet, unglamorous wisdom that saves a lot of grief.

body: A word fitly spoken is like apples of gold in pictures of silver.
modernText: A word fitly spoken is like apples of gold in settings of silver.
message: The right words at the right time, beautiful and valuable. A plain day as a chance to say something good to someone.

body: He that trusteth in his own heart is a fool: but whoso walketh wisely, he shall be delivered.
modernText: One who trusts in himself is a fool; but one who walks in wisdom is kept safe.
message: Trusting your own gut isn't always wise, but walking wisely is. A plain day is a good day to lean on good counsel over your hunches.

body: And now, Israel, what doth the LORD thy God require of thee, but to fear the LORD thy God, to walk in all his ways, and to love him, and to serve the LORD thy God with all thy heart and with all thy soul,
modernText: Now, Israel, what does Yahweh your God require of you, but to fear Yahweh your God, to walk in all his ways, to love him, and to serve Yahweh your God with all your heart and with all your soul,
message: A refreshingly simple summary for an ordinary day: just walk the good way, with a little reverence and love. No grand feat required.

body: Learn to do well; seek judgment, relieve the oppressed, judge the fatherless, plead for the widow.
modernText: Learn to do well. Seek justice. Relieve the oppressed. Defend the fatherless. Plead for the widow.”
message: Learn to do good, the verse says, like it's a skill you practice. An ordinary day is exactly the classroom for it.

body: And many people shall go and say, Come ye, and let us go up to the mountain of the LORD, to the house of the God of Jacob; and he will teach us of his ways, and we will walk in his paths: for out of Zion shall go forth the law, and the word of the LORD from Jerusalem.
modernText: Many peoples shall go and say, “Come, let’s go up to the mountain of Yahweh, to the house of the God of Jacob; and he will teach us of his ways, and we will walk in his paths.” For the law shall go out of Zion, and Yahweh’s word from Jerusalem.
message: Being taught the way, then just walking it, steadily. A plain day as one more step along a well-worn, good path.

body: Call unto me, and I will answer thee, and shew thee great and mighty things, which thou knowest not.
modernText: ‘Call to me, and I will answer you, and will show you great and difficult things, which you don’t know.’
message: Even on an unremarkable day, there's an open invitation to ask and be shown something. The ordinary moment can still hold a question worth asking.

body: Blessed are they which do hunger and thirst after righteousness: for they shall be filled.
modernText: Blessed are those who hunger and thirst after righteousness, for they shall be filled.
message: Just wanting to be good, to do right, counts and gets filled. On a plain day, that quiet hunger is enough to be blessed.

body: Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you:
modernText: “Ask, and it will be given you. Seek, and you will find. Knock, and it will be opened for you.
message: A simple, steady invitation: just keep asking, keep looking. An ordinary day is a fine day to quietly keep seeking.

body: But he said, Yea rather, blessed are they that hear the word of God, and keep it.
modernText: But he said, “On the contrary, blessed are those who hear the word of God, and keep it.”
message: Blessing tied to the ordinary act of hearing and doing. Not a dramatic calling, just quietly keeping the good you know.

body: If any man will do his will, he shall know of the doctrine, whether it be of God, or whether I speak of myself.
modernText: If anyone desires to do his will, he will know about the teaching, whether it is from God, or if I am speaking from myself.
message: Understanding comes through doing, not just thinking. On a plain day, the next small act is how the clarity actually arrives.

body: For in him we live, and move, and have our being; as certain also of your own poets have said, For we are also his offspring.
modernText: ‘For in him we live, move, and have our being.’ As some of your own poets have said, ‘For we are also his offspring.’
message: Even the ordinary, unremarkable living and moving happens inside something larger. A plain day is still held, breath by breath.

body: O the depth of the riches both of the wisdom and knowledge of God! how unsearchable are his judgments, and his ways past finding out!
modernText: Oh the depth of the riches both of the wisdom and the knowledge of God! How unsearchable are his judgments, and his ways past tracing out!
message: On a day you can't make sense of how things fit, this says the full picture is deeper than you can see. Permission to not have it all mapped.

body: Wherefore let him that thinketh he standeth take heed lest he fall.
modernText: Therefore let him who thinks he stands be careful that he doesn’t fall.
message: A quiet check for a day that's going fine: stay humble, stay careful. Ordinary steadiness includes not getting cocky.

body: I therefore, the prisoner of the Lord, beseech you that ye walk worthy of the vocation wherewith ye are called,
modernText: I therefore, the prisoner in the Lord, beg you to walk worthily of the calling with which you were called,
message: Just live in a way that fits who you are, on the ordinary days too. A plain day is where that worthy walk actually happens.

body: Let nothing be done through strife or vainglory; but in lowliness of mind let each esteem other better than themselves.
modernText: doing nothing through rivalry or through conceit, but in humility, each counting others better than himself;
message: An ordinary-day practice: quietly putting others a little ahead of yourself. Small, humble, and quietly transformative.

body: Those things, which ye have both learned, and received, and heard, and seen in me, do: and the God of peace shall be with you.
modernText: The things which you learned, received, heard, and saw in me: do these things, and the God of peace will be with you.
message: Just do the good things you already know, the verse says, and peace follows. On a plain day, that's the whole simple formula.

body: Put on therefore, as the elect of God, holy and beloved, bowels of mercies, kindness, humbleness of mind, meekness, longsuffering;
modernText: Put on therefore, as God’s chosen ones, holy and beloved, a heart of compassion, kindness, lowliness, humility, and perseverance;
message: Getting dressed, in a sense, for an ordinary day: kindness, humility, patience. The quiet virtues worn like clothes.

body: Prove all things; hold fast that which is good.
modernText: Test all things, and hold firmly that which is good.
message: A level-headed ordinary-day practice: weigh things, keep what's good, drop the rest. Quiet, steady discernment.

body: But be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving your own selves.
modernText: But be doers of the word, and not only hearers, deluding your own selves.
message: The nudge to actually do the small good thing, not just nod at it. An ordinary day is where the doing, or not, actually happens.

body: But I trusted in thee, O LORD: I said, Thou art my God.
modernText: But I trust in you, Yahweh. I said, “You are my God.”
message: A plain, steady declaration for an ordinary day. Not dramatic faith, just quietly deciding again where your trust sits.

body: A little that a righteous man hath is better than the riches of many wicked.
modernText: Better is a little that the righteous has, than the abundance of many wicked.
message: Better to have a little and be at peace. A plain, modest day might be richer than it looks.

body: I have been young, and now am old; yet have I not seen the righteous forsaken, nor his seed begging bread.
modernText: I have been young, and now am old, yet I have not seen the righteous forsaken, nor his children begging for bread.
message: A long look back from someone who's seen a lot of ordinary days. The quiet testimony: you don't get left to fend alone.

body: Mark the perfect man, and behold the upright: for the end of that man is peace.
modernText: Mark the perfect man, and see the upright, for there is a future for the man of peace.
message: The steady, upright life quietly leads to peace. An ordinary day of just doing right is pointed somewhere good.

body: O God, thou art my God; early will I seek thee: my soul thirsteth for thee, my flesh longeth for thee in a dry and thirsty land, where no water is;
modernText: God, you are my God. I will earnestly seek you. My soul thirsts for you. My flesh longs for you, in a dry and weary land, where there is no water.
message: A simple morning habit for an ordinary day: reach out first, before the noise. Quiet, steady, grounding.

body: For a thousand years in thy sight are but as yesterday when it is past, and as a watch in the night.
modernText: For a thousand years in your sight are just like yesterday when it is past, like a watch in the night.
message: A little perspective for a plain day: from far enough back, even the big stuff is small. Oddly freeing on an unremarkable afternoon.

body: For he is our God; and we are the people of his pasture, and the sheep of his hand. To day if ye will hear his voice,
modernText: for he is our God. We are the people of his pasture, and the sheep in his care. Today, oh that you would hear his voice!
message: A quiet sense of belonging for an ordinary day. Not alone, not unclaimed, just tended, even on the forgettable days.

body: Blessed are the undefiled in the way, who walk in the law of the LORD.
modernText: Blessed are those whose ways are blameless, who walk according to Yahweh’s law.
message: Blessing tied to just walking a clean, ordinary path. Nothing flashy, the quiet integrity of the regular day.

body: Blessed are they that keep his testimonies, and that seek him with the whole heart.
modernText: Blessed are those who keep his statutes, who seek him with their whole heart.
message: Blessing in the steady seeking, not a one-time find. An ordinary day of just keeping at it counts.

body: Wherewithal shall a young man cleanse his way? by taking heed thereto according to thy word.
modernText: How can a young man keep his way pure? By living according to your word.
message: The ordinary, unglamorous answer: just pay attention to how you live. A plain day is where that cleansing actually happens.

body: Thy testimonies also are my delight and my counsellors.
modernText: Indeed your statutes are my delight, and my counselors.
message: Good counsel to lean on for an ordinary decision. You don't have to figure the plain day out entirely alone.

body: And I will walk at liberty: for I seek thy precepts.
modernText: I will walk in liberty, for I have sought your precepts.
message: A surprising pairing: freedom found in a steady, ordinary way of living. The plain, good path turns out to be the open one.

body: O lord, thou hast searched me, and known me.
modernText: Yahweh, you have searched me, and you know me.
message: Fully known, even on a day no one's really looking. The plain, invisible version of you is still completely seen.

body: Thou compassest my path and my lying down, and art acquainted with all my ways.
modernText: You search out my path and my lying down, and are acquainted with all my ways.
message: Even your ordinary routine, your walking and resting, is known and accompanied. The unremarkable day isn't unwatched.

body: Then shalt thou understand righteousness, and judgment, and equity; yea, every good path.
modernText: Then you will understand righteousness and justice, equity and every good path.
message: Clarity about the plain, everyday right thing. An ordinary day's small discernments quietly add up to real understanding.

body: My son, forget not my law; but let thine heart keep my commandments:
modernText: My son, don’t forget my teaching; but let your heart keep my commandments:
message: Just don't forget the good you already know. On an ordinary day, remembering the basics is most of the assignment.

body: So shalt thou find favour and good understanding in the sight of God and man.
modernText: So you will find favor, and good understanding in the sight of God and man.
message: Favour and good sense, the quiet rewards of a steadily lived life. A plain day of doing right builds toward them.

body: The liberal soul shall be made fat: and he that watereth shall be watered also himself.
modernText: The liberal soul shall be made fat. He who waters shall be watered also himself.
message: A gentle law of ordinary days: give, and you get refreshed too. Small generosity comes back around.

body: The hand of the diligent shall bear rule: but the slothful shall be under tribute.
modernText: The hands of the diligent ones shall rule, but laziness ends in slave labor.
message: The steady, diligent approach quietly earns responsibility. A plain day of just keeping at it is building something.

body: Hope deferred maketh the heart sick: but when the desire cometh, it is a tree of life.
modernText: Hope deferred makes the heart sick, but when longing is fulfilled, it is a tree of life.
message: An honest verse for a day of still-waiting. It names how long waits wear on you, and promises the arrival is worth it.

body: He that is slow to wrath is of great understanding: but he that is hasty of spirit exalteth folly.
modernText: He who is slow to anger has great understanding, but he who has a quick temper displays folly.
message: Patience reframed as intelligence. On an ordinary day, keeping your temper is quietly one of the smarter things you can do.

body: A man that hath friends must shew himself friendly: and there is a friend that sticketh closer than a brother.
modernText: A man of many companions may be ruined, but there is a friend who sticks closer than a brother.
message: The quiet value of a steady friend, worth more than many acquaintances. A plain day is a good day to appreciate the ones who stick around.

body: Even a child is known by his doings, whether his work be pure, and whether it be right.
modernText: Even a child makes himself known by his doings, whether his work is pure, and whether it is right.
message: You're known by the small, ordinary things you actually do. A plain day's quiet actions say more than you'd think.

body: To do justice and judgment is more acceptable to the LORD than sacrifice.
modernText: To do righteousness and justice is more acceptable to Yahweh than sacrifice.
message: The everyday doing of what's right matters more than grand gestures. An ordinary day of plain fairness counts for a lot.

body: A good name is rather to be chosen than great riches, and loving favour rather than silver and gold.
modernText: A good name is more desirable than great riches, and loving favor is better than silver and gold.
message: A good reputation, quietly built over ordinary days, is worth more than money. The plain, honest days are what earn it.

body: Let not thine heart envy sinners: but be thou in the fear of the LORD all the day long.
modernText: Don’t let your heart envy sinners, but rather fear Yahweh all day long.
message: Steady reverence through a whole ordinary day, not just the big moments. A quiet, all-day orientation.

body: A faithful man shall abound with blessings: but he that maketh haste to be rich shall not be innocent.
modernText: A faithful man is rich with blessings; but one who is eager to be rich will not go unpunished.
message: The quietly faithful life, lived out in ordinary days, accumulates good. Steadiness pays, even when it's boring.

body: Then I saw that wisdom excelleth folly, as far as light excelleth darkness.
modernText: Then I saw that wisdom excels folly, as far as light excels darkness.
message: Even the realist admits wisdom beats foolishness, plainly. On an ordinary day, the small wise choice is still the better-lit path.

body: I know that, whatsoever God doeth, it shall be for ever: nothing can be put to it, nor any thing taken from it: and God doeth it, that men should fear before him.
modernText: I know that whatever God does, it shall be forever. Nothing can be added to it, nor anything taken from it; and God has done it, that men should fear before him.
message: Something lasting under all the passing, ordinary days. A quiet reassurance that not everything is as fleeting as a plain Tuesday feels.

body: In the day of prosperity be joyful, but in the day of adversity consider: God also hath set the one over against the other, to the end that man should find nothing after him.
modernText: In the day of prosperity be joyful, and in the day of adversity consider; yes, God has made the one side by side with the other, to the end that man should not find out anything after him.
message: A balanced take for an ordinary day: enjoy the good when it's good, reflect when it's not. Steady either way.

body: The grass withereth, the flower fadeth: but the word of our God shall stand for ever.
modernText: The grass withers, the flower fades; but the word of our God stands forever.”
message: Something that outlasts every ordinary, forgettable day. A steadying thought: not everything fades as fast as today seems to.

body: So shall my word be that goeth forth out of my mouth: it shall not return unto me void, but it shall accomplish that which I please, and it shall prosper in the thing whereto I sent it.
modernText: so is my word that goes out of my mouth: it will not return to me void, but it will accomplish that which I please, and it will prosper in the thing I sent it to do.
message: Even on a day nothing seems productive, this says the good at work doesn't come back empty. Quiet, invisible fruitfulness.

body: The LORD hath appeared of old unto me, saying, Yea, I have loved thee with an everlasting love: therefore with lovingkindness have I drawn thee.
modernText: Yahweh appeared of old to me, saying, “Yes, I have loved you with an everlasting love. Therefore I have drawn you with loving kindness.
message: A steady, unchanging love under all the ordinary days. Not dependent on how eventful or impressive today was.

body: Let us search and try our ways, and turn again to the LORD.
modernText: Let us search and try our ways, and turn again to Yahweh.
message: A plain day is a fine day for a quiet honest look at how you're living, and a small course correction.

body: Then shall we know, if we follow on to know the LORD: his going forth is prepared as the morning; and he shall come unto us as the rain, as the latter and former rain unto the earth.
modernText: Let’s acknowledge Yahweh. Let’s press on to know Yahweh. As surely as the sun rises, Yahweh will appear. He will come to us like the rain, like the spring rain that waters the earth.”
message: Knowing comes by following on, steadily, not in a flash. A plain day is just one more step in that ongoing pursuit.

body: But he answered and said, It is written, Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God.
modernText: But he answered, “It is written, ‘Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceeds out of God’s mouth.’ ”
message: There's more feeding you than the literal tasks of an ordinary day. Something nourishes you under the surface of the routine.

body: For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.
modernText: for where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.
message: A quiet prompt for an ordinary day: notice what you actually treasure, because your heart's already following it.

body: And as ye would that men should do to you, do ye also to them likewise.
modernText: “As you would like people to do to you, do exactly so to them.
message: The golden rule, perfect for ordinary interactions. A plain day is full of small chances to just treat people the way you'd want.

body: And he said unto them, Take heed, and beware of covetousness: for a man’s life consisteth not in the abundance of the things which he possesseth.
modernText: He said to them, “Beware! Keep yourselves from covetousness, for a man’s life doesn’t consist of the abundance of the things which he possesses.”
message: A grounding reminder for a plain day: your life isn't the sum of your stuff. The ordinary, un-acquisitive day might be closer to the point.

body: Jesus answered and said unto him, If a man love me, he will keep my words: and my Father will love him, and we will come unto him, and make our abode with him.
modernText: Jesus answered him, “If a man loves me, he will keep my word. My Father will love him, and we will come to him, and make our home with him.
message: Love shown in the ordinary keeping of small things. Not grand declarations, just the quiet daily follow-through.

body: I beseech you therefore, brethren, by the mercies of God, that ye present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable unto God, which is your reasonable service.
modernText: Therefore I urge you, brothers, by the mercies of God, to present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable to God, which is your spiritual service.
message: Even the ordinary, physical living of a plain day can be an offering. The regular stuff gets to mean something.

body: Be kindly affectioned one to another with brotherly love; in honour preferring one another;
modernText: In love of the brothers be tenderly affectionate to one another; in honor preferring one another;
message: An ordinary-day practice: just be warm to people, put them a little first. Small, steady kindness.

body: If we live in the Spirit, let us also walk in the Spirit.
modernText: If we live by the Spirit, let’s also walk by the Spirit.
message: Just keep your ordinary walking in step with what you believe. A plain day of quiet consistency.

body: Be not deceived; God is not mocked: for whatsoever a man soweth, that shall he also reap.
modernText: Don’t be deceived. God is not mocked, for whatever a man sows, that he will also reap.
message: The small, ordinary things you plant today quietly grow. A plain day is still a day of sowing something.

body: And be ye kind one to another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, even as God for Christ’s sake hath forgiven you.
modernText: And be kind to one another, tender hearted, forgiving each other, just as God also in Christ forgave you.
message: Three ordinary-day habits: be kind, be soft, let things go. Quietly, they change everything.

body: For it is God which worketh in you both to will and to do of his good pleasure.
modernText: For it is God who works in you both to will and to work, for his good pleasure.
message: Even on a day you don't feel like you're accomplishing much, something's quietly at work in you. The ordinary day isn't idle.

body: Follow peace with all men, and holiness, without which no man shall see the Lord:
modernText: Follow after peace with all men, and the sanctification without which no man will see the Lord,
message: Just pursue peace, steadily, with the people around you. A plain day is full of small chances to keep the peace.

body: Humble yourselves in the sight of the Lord, and he shall lift you up.
modernText: Humble yourselves in the sight of the Lord, and he will exalt you.
message: A quiet, ordinary posture: stay low, and trust you'll be raised when it's time. No need to self-promote on a plain day.

body: Likewise, ye younger, submit yourselves unto the elder. Yea, all of you be subject one to another, and be clothed with humility: for God resisteth the proud, and giveth grace to the humble.
modernText: Likewise, you younger ones, be subject to the elder. Yes, all of you clothe yourselves with humility, to subject yourselves to one another; for “God resists the proud, but gives grace to the humble.”
message: Humility worn like clothing, every ordinary day. The quiet, steady virtue that makes the plain days go smoother.

body: My little children, let us not love in word, neither in tongue; but in deed and in truth.
modernText: My little children, let’s not love in word only, or with the tongue only, but in deed and truth.
message: Love shown in small, ordinary actions, not just said. A plain day is full of chances to make it real instead of just nice.

body: But they that wait upon the LORD shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles; they shall run, and not be weary; and they shall walk, and not faint.
modernText: but those who wait for Yahweh will renew their strength. They will mount up with wings like eagles. They will run, and not be weary. They will walk, and not faint.
message: The renewing isn't something you manufacture, it comes to the ones who wait. On an empty day, resting is the strategy, not quitting.

body: Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.
modernText: “Come to me, all you who labor and are heavily burdened, and I will give you rest.
message: You don't have to clean up or catch up first. The invitation is to come tired, exactly as worn out as you are, and set it down.

body: Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls.
modernText: Take my yoke upon you, and learn from me, for I am gentle and humble in heart; and you will find rest for your souls.
message: Not just a break for your body, rest for your soul, the part of you that's been quietly running on empty.

body: The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want.
modernText: Yahweh is my shepherd: I shall lack nothing.
message: On a day you feel depleted, this says you're being tended. You don't have to shepherd yourself through the tired.

body: He maketh me to lie down in green pastures: he leadeth me beside the still waters.
modernText: He makes me lie down in green pastures. He leads me beside still waters.
message: Made to lie down, the verse says, like rest is something you're gently led into, not something you have to earn.

body: He restoreth my soul: he leadeth me in the paths of righteousness for his name’s sake.
modernText: He restores my soul. He guides me in the paths of righteousness for his name’s sake.
message: Soul-level restoration, the quiet refilling of what the day drained. You don't have to do the restoring yourself.

body: I will lift up mine eyes unto the hills, from whence cometh my help.
modernText: I will lift up my eyes to the hills. Where does my help come from?
message: Even lifting your eyes feels like effort when you're this tired. The verse just points you toward where help comes from, no striving required.

body: My help cometh from the LORD, which made heaven and earth.
modernText: My help comes from Yahweh, who made heaven and earth.
message: Help from outside yourself, which is good news when there's nothing left inside. You don't have to be your own source today.

body: He will not suffer thy foot to be moved: he that keepeth thee will not slumber.
modernText: He will not allow your foot to be moved. He who keeps you will not slumber.
message: While you finally rest, someone stays awake. You can let your guard all the way down, the watch doesn't stop when you do.

body: And let us not be weary in well doing: for in due season we shall reap, if we faint not.
modernText: Let’s not be weary in doing good, for we will reap in due season, if we don’t give up.
message: An honest nod to the tired that comes from doing good with no payoff yet. A gentle 'the harvest is coming,' no pressure to feel it now.

body: For which cause we faint not; but though our outward man perish, yet the inward man is renewed day by day.
modernText: Therefore we don’t faint, but though our outward man is decaying, yet our inward man is renewed day by day.
message: The outside is worn down, and that's allowed. Something inside is being quietly refilled, even on the days you can't feel it.

body: For our light affliction, which is but for a moment, worketh for us a far more exceeding and eternal weight of glory;
modernText: For our light affliction, which is for the moment, works for us more and more exceedingly an eternal weight of glory,
message: The weight feels anything but light right now. The verse just whispers that it's doing something, even when it only feels heavy.

body: Hast thou not known? hast thou not heard, that the everlasting God, the LORD, the Creator of the ends of the earth, fainteth not, neither is weary? there is no searching of his understanding.
modernText: Haven’t you known? Haven’t you heard? The everlasting God, Yahweh, the Creator of the ends of the earth, doesn’t faint. He isn’t weary. His understanding is unsearchable.
message: You're tired because you're human and finite. The one holding it all isn't, and doesn't run down when you do.

body: He giveth power to the faint; and to them that have no might he increaseth strength.
modernText: He gives power to the weak. He increases the strength of him who has no might.
message: Specifically for the faint, the ones with no might left. Strength offered to the exact empty version of you, no qualifying required.

body: I will both lay me down in peace, and sleep: for thou, LORD, only makest me dwell in safety.
modernText: In peace I will both lay myself down and sleep, for you, Yahweh alone, make me live in safety.
message: Permission to just lie down and sleep, held while you do. The tired day gets to end in actual rest, not just collapse.

body: When thou liest down, thou shalt not be afraid: yea, thou shalt lie down, and thy sleep shall be sweet.
modernText: When you lie down, you will not be afraid. Yes, you will lie down, and your sleep will be sweet.
message: A gentle promise for a worn-out night: you'll lie down, and the rest will be sweet. Sleep as a gift, not just a shutdown.

body: It is vain for you to rise up early, to sit up late, to eat the bread of sorrows: for so he giveth his beloved sleep.
modernText: It is vain for you to rise up early, to stay up late, eating the bread of toil, for he gives sleep to his loved ones.
message: The staying-up, the grinding, isn't what holds it together. Rest is actually given to you, as the beloved, not earned by exhaustion.

body: For consider him that endured such contradiction of sinners against himself, lest ye be wearied and faint in your minds.
modernText: For consider him who has endured such contradiction of sinners against himself, that you don’t grow weary, fainting in your souls.
message: It names the specific kind of tired that's in the mind, not just the body. A soft acknowledgment that mental weariness is real.

body: Likewise the Spirit also helpeth our infirmities: for we know not what we should pray for as we ought: but the Spirit itself maketh intercession for us with groanings which cannot be uttered.
modernText: In the same way, the Spirit also helps our weaknesses, for we don’t know how to pray as we ought. But the Spirit himself makes intercession for us with groanings which can’t be uttered.
message: When you're too tired even to pray, this says it gets done for you. You don't have to find the words, or the energy.

body: My flesh and my heart faileth: but God is the strength of my heart, and my portion for ever.
modernText: My flesh and my heart fails, but God is the strength of my heart and my portion forever.
message: Honest about the failing, the body and nerve giving out. And steady about a strength that isn't yours to run out of.

body: And he said unto them, Come ye yourselves apart into a desert place, and rest a while: for there were many coming and going, and they had no leisure so much as to eat.
modernText: He said to them, “You come apart into a deserted place, and rest awhile.” For there were many coming and going, and they had no leisure so much as to eat.
message: Even he told tired people to come away and rest. Permission, straight from the source, to step back and recover for a bit.

body: And he said, My presence shall go with thee, and I will give thee rest.
modernText: He said, “My presence will go with you, and I will give you rest.”
message: Not a to-do list, just presence, and rest. On an empty day, the promise is company and a place to set it down.

body: It is of the LORD’s mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not.
modernText: It is because of Yahweh’s loving kindnesses that we are not consumed, because his compassion doesn’t fail.
message: On a day you feel used up, the compassion toward you isn't. You haven't exhausted the supply, even now.

body: They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness.
modernText: They are new every morning. Great is your faithfulness.
message: Whatever today drained, the mercy resets overnight. You get to start tomorrow refilled, not in the red.

body: And God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes; and there shall be no more death, neither sorrow, nor crying, neither shall there be any more pain: for the former things are passed away.
modernText: He will wipe away every tear from their eyes. Death will be no more; neither will there be mourning, nor crying, nor pain, any more. The first things have passed away.”
message: A glimpse of a future with no more exhaustion, no more weariness. For a tired day, a quiet reminder that this isn't the end state.

body: The LORD thy God in the midst of thee is mighty; he will save, he will rejoice over thee with joy; he will rest in his love, he will joy over thee with singing.
modernText: Yahweh, your God, is among you, a mighty one who will save. He will rejoice over you with joy. He will calm you in his love. He will rejoice over you with singing.
message: Even the one holding you rests in love. A picture of being so settled with you that there's nothing frantic about it.

body: Be still, and know that I am God: I will be exalted among the heathen, I will be exalted in the earth.
modernText: “Be still, and know that I am God. I will be exalted among the nations. I will be exalted in the earth.”
message: Be still, the verse says, which a tired body is more than ready to do. The stillness isn't laziness here, it's where you're met.

body: For thus saith the Lord GOD, the Holy One of Israel; In returning and rest shall ye be saved; in quietness and in confidence shall be your strength: and ye would not.
modernText: For thus said the Lord Yahweh, the Holy One of Israel, “You will be saved in returning and rest. Your strength will be in quietness and in confidence.” You refused,
message: Strength found in quietness, not in pushing harder. For a tired day, this flips the script: rest is where the strength actually is.

body: Let us choose to us judgment: let us know among ourselves what is good.
modernText: Let us choose for us that which is right. Let us know among ourselves what is good.
message: A quiet invitation to just sort out together what's good and right, at a pace you can manage. No rushing the worn-out mind.

body: For I have satiated the weary soul, and I have replenished every sorrowful soul.
modernText: For I have satiated the weary soul, and I have replenished every sorrowful soul.”
message: The weary soul satisfied, the sorrowful replenished. The verse promises the empty part of you gets filled, not just propped up.

body: Return unto thy rest, O my soul; for the LORD hath dealt bountifully with thee.
modernText: Return to your rest, my soul, for Yahweh has dealt bountifully with you.
message: Talking to your own tired soul like a friend: come back, you can rest now. Sometimes you have to give yourself the permission.

body: Truly my soul waiteth upon God: from him cometh my salvation.
modernText: My soul rests in God alone. My salvation is from him.
message: The soul quietly waiting, not striving. On a tired day, just waiting, leaning, is enough.

body: My soul, wait thou only upon God; for my expectation is from him.
modernText: My soul, wait in silence for God alone, for my expectation is from him.
message: Resting your expectation on something outside your own depleted self. You don't have to generate the hope today.

body: Rest in the LORD, and wait patiently for him: fret not thyself because of him who prospereth in his way, because of the man who bringeth wicked devices to pass.
modernText: Rest in Yahweh, and wait patiently for him. Don’t fret because of him who prospers in his way, because of the man who makes wicked plots happen.
message: Rest and wait, two things a tired soul is actually suited for. For once, the instruction matches exactly where you are.

body: There remaineth therefore a rest to the people of God.
modernText: There remains therefore a Sabbath rest for the people of God.
message: A rest still waiting for you, held in reserve. On a tired day, the promise that real rest is a real thing, not a fantasy.

body: For he that is entered into his rest, he also hath ceased from his own works, as God did from his.
modernText: For he who has entered into his rest has himself also rested from his works, as God did from his.
message: Permission to cease, to stop working for a bit. The rest here is about laying your own efforts down, not just sleeping.

body: But whosoever drinketh of the water that I shall give him shall never thirst; but the water that I shall give him shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life.
modernText: but whoever drinks of the water that I will give him will never thirst again; but the water that I will give him will become in him a well of water springing up to eternal life.”
message: A well inside you that doesn't run dry, even when you feel completely tapped out. A source that refills on its own.

body: For the LORD God is a sun and shield: the LORD will give grace and glory: no good thing will he withhold from them that walk uprightly.
modernText: For Yahweh God is a sun and a shield. Yahweh will give grace and glory. He withholds no good thing from those who walk blamelessly.
message: Warmth and cover both, on a day you have nothing left to give. Nothing good held back from the tired, depleted you.

body: And the LORD shall guide thee continually, and satisfy thy soul in drought, and make fat thy bones: and thou shalt be like a watered garden, and like a spring of water, whose waters fail not.
modernText: and Yahweh will guide you continually, satisfy your soul in dry places, and make your bones strong. You will be like a watered garden, and like a spring of water whose waters don’t fail.
message: Satisfied even in the drought, the dry, empty stretch. The verse meets you exactly in the running-on-fumes feeling.

body: The LORD upholdeth all that fall, and raiseth up all those that be bowed down.
modernText: Yahweh upholds all who fall, and raises up all those who are bowed down.
message: For everyone bent under the weight today. Upheld and raised, gently, specifically the ones who feel like they're going down.

body: I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me.
modernText: I can do all things through Christ, who strengthens me.
message: Not a demand to push harder, but a quiet 'you're not drawing on your own empty tank for this.' Strength from somewhere else.

body: But if the Spirit of him that raised up Jesus from the dead dwell in you, he that raised up Christ from the dead shall also quicken your mortal bodies by his Spirit that dwelleth in you.
modernText: But if the Spirit of him who raised up Jesus from the dead dwells in you, he who raised up Christ Jesus from the dead will also give life to your mortal bodies through his Spirit who dwells in you.
message: Even your tired, mortal body is promised a kind of coming-back-to-life. The weariness isn't the final word on your energy.

body: That he would grant you, according to the riches of his glory, to be strengthened with might by his Spirit in the inner man;
modernText: that he would grant you, according to the riches of his glory, that you may be strengthened with power through his Spirit in the inner person,
message: Strength on the inside, where the tired lives. Not just powering through, being quietly reinforced underneath.

body: Therefore, my beloved brethren, be ye stedfast, unmoveable, always abounding in the work of the Lord, forasmuch as ye know that your labour is not in vain in the Lord.
modernText: Therefore, my beloved brothers, be steadfast, immovable, always abounding in the Lord’s work, because you know that your labor is not in vain in the Lord.
message: On a day your effort feels pointless, this says it isn't wasted. The tiring work is counting, even when you can't see it.

body: And the LORD said unto Moses, Is the LORD’s hand waxed short? thou shalt see now whether my word shall come to pass unto thee or not.
modernText: Yahweh said to Moses, “Has Yahweh’s hand grown short? Now you will see whether my word will happen to you or not.”
message: A gentle question for a depleted day: is help really as limited as it feels? The reach is longer than your tired eyes can see.

body: Be of good courage, and he shall strengthen your heart, all ye that hope in the LORD.
modernText: Be strong, and let your heart take courage, all you who hope in Yahweh.
message: Addressed to everyone still hoping, even faintly, even tiredly. Strength offered to the ones just barely hanging on.

body: Repent ye therefore, and be converted, that your sins may be blotted out, when the times of refreshing shall come from the presence of the Lord.
modernText: “Repent therefore, and turn again, that your sins may be blotted out, so that there may come times of refreshing from the presence of the Lord,
message: Refreshing, the exact word for what a tired soul needs. And it comes from presence, from being with, not from doing more.

body: Strengthen ye the weak hands, and confirm the feeble knees.
modernText: Strengthen the weak hands, and make the feeble knees firm.
message: A tender verse for shaky hands and worn-out knees. It doesn't scold the weakness, it just gently steadies it.

body: Say to them that are of a fearful heart, Be strong, fear not: behold, your God will come with vengeance, even God with a recompence; he will come and save you.
modernText: Tell those who have a fearful heart, “Be strong! Don’t be afraid! Behold, your God will come with vengeance, God’s retribution. He will come and save you.
message: Spoken softly to the fearful, tired heart. Not a demand to toughen up, a gentle 'you're not alone in this, hold on.'

body: And he said unto me, My grace is sufficient for thee: for my strength is made perfect in weakness. Most gladly therefore will I rather glory in my infirmities, that the power of Christ may rest upon me.
modernText: He has said to me, “My grace is sufficient for you, for my power is made perfect in weakness.” Most gladly therefore I will rather glory in my weaknesses, that the power of Christ may rest on me.
message: The grace shows up in the weakness, not after you fix it. On an empty day, your depletion is exactly where the strength arrives.

body: I laid me down and slept; I awaked; for the LORD sustained me.
modernText: I laid myself down and slept. I awakened; for Yahweh sustains me.
message: You made it through the night and woke up, not because you held yourself together, but because something steadier kept you while you slept.

body: Therefore my heart is glad, and my glory rejoiceth: my flesh also shall rest in hope.
modernText: Therefore my heart is glad, and my tongue rejoices. My body shall also dwell in safety.
message: Even your body gets to rest, in hope, not just collapse. The tired is allowed to lay down into something gentle.

body: Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil: for thou art with me; thy rod and thy staff they comfort me.
modernText: Even though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for you are with me. Your rod and your staff, they comfort me.
message: Even dragging through the low, tired valley, you're not walking it alone. The presence matters more than the pace.

body: Thou preparest a table before me in the presence of mine enemies: thou anointest my head with oil; my cup runneth over.
modernText: You prepare a table before me in the presence of my enemies. You anoint my head with oil. My cup runs over.
message: Tended to, filled past the brim, even on an empty day. Someone pouring into you when you've got nothing left to pour.

body: I had fainted, unless I had believed to see the goodness of the LORD in the land of the living.
modernText: I am still confident of this: I will see the goodness of Yahweh in the land of the living.
message: An honest admission from a tired person: I'd have given out, if I hadn't held onto the hope of good still coming. The believing kept you upright.

body: The LORD will give strength unto his people; the LORD will bless his people with peace.
modernText: Yahweh will give strength to his people. Yahweh will bless his people with peace.
message: Strength first, then peace, both given, not generated. On a tired day, you get to receive instead of produce.

body: Cast thy burden upon the LORD, and he shall sustain thee: he shall never suffer the righteous to be moved.
modernText: Cast your burden on Yahweh and he will sustain you. He will never allow the righteous to be moved.
message: Burden is the right word for the tired, and this doesn't tell you to carry it better. It tells you where to set it down, and promises to hold you up.

body: Blessed be the Lord, who daily loadeth us with benefits, even the God of our salvation. Selah.
modernText: Blessed be the Lord, who daily bears our burdens, even the God who is our salvation.
message: On a day you feel loaded down, this flips it: you're also being loaded with good, daily, even when you're too tired to notice.

body: O God, thou art terrible out of thy holy places: the God of Israel is he that giveth strength and power unto his people. Blessed be God.
modernText: You are awesome, God, in your sanctuaries. The God of Israel gives strength and power to his people. Praise be to God!
message: Strength handed out, not demanded. For the empty, depleted day, the supply is somewhere other than your own reserves.

body: He that dwelleth in the secret place of the most High shall abide under the shadow of the Almighty.
modernText: He who dwells in the secret place of the Most High will rest in the shadow of the Almighty.
message: A quiet, shaded place to rest in. Not a fix for the tiredness, a shelter to sit in while it passes.

body: In the multitude of my thoughts within me thy comforts delight my soul.
modernText: In the multitude of my thoughts within me, your comforts delight my soul.
message: When the tired mind won't quiet down, this is the comfort that shows up in the middle of the noise, soothing the worn-out soul.

body: Who satisfieth thy mouth with good things; so that thy youth is renewed like the eagle’s.
modernText: who satisfies your desire with good things, so that your youth is renewed like the eagle’s.
message: Renewed like an eagle, filled back up. On a day you feel ancient with tiredness, a promise of being refreshed.

body: The LORD is my strength and song, and is become my salvation.
modernText: Yah is my strength and song. He has become my salvation.
message: Strength and song in one breath. For the tired, sometimes relief sounds like finally being able to exhale.

body: My soul melteth for heaviness: strengthen thou me according unto thy word.
modernText: My soul is weary with sorrow: strengthen me according to your word.
message: It names the exact feeling, a soul melting under the weight, and just asks for strength. No pretending you're fine required.

body: This is my comfort in my affliction: for thy word hath quickened me.
modernText: This is my comfort in my affliction, for your word has revived me.
message: Comfort found right inside the tired, hard stretch, not after it ends. Something that revives you while you're still worn down.

body: Let, I pray thee, thy merciful kindness be for my comfort, according to thy word unto thy servant.
modernText: Please let your loving kindness be for my comfort, according to your word to your servant.
message: A simple ask for a tired day: let the kindness be what comforts me. Permission to want to be comforted, and to ask for it plainly.

body: Surely I have behaved and quieted myself, as a child that is weaned of his mother: my soul is even as a weaned child.
modernText: Surely I have stilled and quieted my soul, like a weaned child with his mother, like a weaned child is my soul within me.
message: A soul calmed like a sleepy kid resting against someone. Not fixed, not energized, just quiet and held.

body: In the day when I cried thou answeredst me, and strengthenedst me with strength in my soul.
modernText: In the day that I called, you answered me. You encouraged me with strength in my soul.
message: Strengthened in the soul, the exact place the tired lives. The strength came in the crying, not after you pulled it together.

body: For thou hast been a strength to the poor, a strength to the needy in his distress, a refuge from the storm, a shadow from the heat, when the blast of the terrible ones is as a storm against the wall.
modernText: For you have been a stronghold to the poor, a stronghold to the needy in his distress, a refuge from the storm, a shade from the heat, when the blast of the dreaded ones is like a storm against the wall.
message: A shelter for the ones with nothing left, shade from the relentless heat. Rest built for exactly the empty, worn-down day.

body: And my people shall dwell in a peaceable habitation, and in sure dwellings, and in quiet resting places;
modernText: My people will live in a peaceful habitation, in safe dwellings, and in quiet resting places,
message: Quiet resting places, promised. On a tired day, a picture of somewhere to finally just settle and be still.

body: Fear thou not; for I am with thee: be not dismayed; for I am thy God: I will strengthen thee; yea, I will help thee; yea, I will uphold thee with the right hand of my righteousness.
modernText: Don’t you be afraid, for I am with you. Don’t be dismayed, for I am your God. I will strengthen you. Yes, I will help you. Yes, I will uphold you with the right hand of my righteousness.
message: When you feel like you're sagging, this is a hand under your arm. Upheld, not lectured about standing up straighter.

body: And even to your old age I am he; and even to hoar hairs will I carry you: I have made, and I will bear; even I will carry, and will deliver you.
modernText: Even to old age I am he, and even to gray hairs I will carry you. I have made, and I will bear. Yes, I will carry, and will deliver.
message: Carried the whole way, even to gray hair. On a day you feel like you're dragging yourself along, this says you're being carried.

body: Sing, O heavens; and be joyful, O earth; and break forth into singing, O mountains: for the LORD hath comforted his people, and will have mercy upon his afflicted.
modernText: Sing, heavens, and be joyful, earth! Break out into singing, mountains, for Yahweh has comforted his people, and will have compassion on his afflicted.
message: Comfort and mercy for the afflicted, worn-down ones. The tired and the heavy are exactly who this is aimed at.

body: For thus saith the high and lofty One that inhabiteth eternity, whose name is Holy; I dwell in the high and holy place, with him also that is of a contrite and humble spirit, to revive the spirit of the humble, and to revive the heart of the contrite ones.
modernText: For the high and lofty One who inhabits eternity, whose name is Holy, says: “I dwell in the high and holy place, with him also who is of a contrite and humble spirit, to revive the spirit of the humble, and to revive the heart of the contrite.
message: Reviving the low, the depleted spirit. The verse goes looking specifically for the ones who feel at the bottom, to bring them back.

body: I have seen his ways, and will heal him: I will lead him also, and restore comforts unto him and to his mourners.
modernText: I have seen his ways, and will heal him. I will lead him also, and restore comforts to him and to his mourners.
message: Seen, healed, led gently, comforts restored. A quiet, tender itinerary for someone worn all the way out.

body: In all their affliction he was afflicted, and the angel of his presence saved them: in his love and in his pity he redeemed them; and he bare them, and carried them all the days of old.
modernText: In all their affliction he was afflicted, and the angel of his presence saved them. In his love and in his pity he redeemed them. He bore them, and carried them all the days of old.
message: Bore them, carried them, all the days. On a tired day, a picture of being lifted and carried through, not left to trudge alone.

body: As one whom his mother comforteth, so will I comfort you; and ye shall be comforted in Jerusalem.
modernText: As one whom his mother comforts, so I will comfort you. You will be comforted in Jerusalem.”
message: The gentlest image in the Bible for a tired, worn day: comforted the way a mother comforts a tired child. Soft, close, no conditions.

body: Thus saith the LORD, Stand ye in the ways, and see, and ask for the old paths, where is the good way, and walk therein, and ye shall find rest for your souls. But they said, We will not walk therein.
modernText: Yahweh says, “Stand in the ways and see, and ask for the old paths, ‘Where is the good way?’ and walk in it, and you will find rest for your souls. But they said, ‘We will not walk in it.’
message: Rest for your souls, the oldest promise. When you're worn out, sometimes the way forward is the quiet, well-worn path, not a new push.

body: For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.
modernText: For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.”
message: Not a promise of no load, a lighter one, shared. The weight redistributed so it stops flattening you.

body: And of Benjamin he said, The beloved of the LORD shall dwell in safety by him; and the Lord shall cover him all the day long, and he shall dwell between his shoulders.
modernText: About Benjamin he said, “The beloved of Yahweh will dwell in safety by him. He covers him all day long. He dwells between his shoulders.”
message: Resting between the shoulders, tucked in close and safe. On a tired day, a picture of being carried like someone beloved.

body: The eternal God is thy refuge, and underneath are the everlasting arms: and he shall thrust out the enemy from before thee; and shall say, Destroy them.
modernText: The eternal God is your dwelling place. Underneath are the everlasting arms. He thrust out the enemy from before you, and said, ‘Destroy!’
message: However far you feel like you're sinking into the tiredness, there's a floor, and it's arms. Underneath, holding, always.

body: Thou, O God, didst send a plentiful rain, whereby thou didst confirm thine inheritance, when it was weary.
