modernText: You, God, sent a plentiful rain. You confirmed your inheritance when it was weary.
message: Rain sent on the weary ground to revive it. A picture of being watered, refreshed, exactly when you'd gone dry.

body: And as he lay and slept under a juniper tree, behold, then an angel touched him, and said unto him, Arise and eat.
modernText: He lay down and slept under a juniper tree; and behold, an angel touched him, and said to him, “Arise and eat!”
message: When Elijah was too exhausted to go on, the first thing offered wasn't a pep talk, it was food and rest. Sometimes the holy thing is a nap and a meal.

body: And the angel of the LORD came again the second time, and touched him, and said, Arise and eat; because the journey is too great for thee.
modernText: Yahweh’s angel came again the second time, and touched him, and said, “Arise and eat, because the journey is too great for you.”
message: An honest acknowledgment: the journey is too great for you right now. So first, eat, rest. Strength for the road comes after, not before.

body: As the hart panteth after the water brooks, so panteth my soul after thee, O God.
modernText: As the deer pants for the water brooks, so my soul pants after you, God.
message: A worn-out, thirsty kind of longing. The verse doesn't rush you out of it, it just names the deep tiredness and the ache for refreshing.

body: My soul thirsteth for God, for the living God: when shall I come and appear before God?
modernText: My soul thirsts for God, for the living God. When shall I come and appear before God?
message: A tired soul reaching for something living, refilling. On an empty day, the longing itself is honest and allowed.

body: I stretch forth my hands unto thee: my soul thirsteth after thee, as a thirsty land. Selah.
modernText: I spread out my hands to you. My soul thirsts for you, like a parched land.
message: Dry as cracked ground, the verse says, and just reaching for water. A picture of tiredness that doesn't pretend to be anything else.

body: In the last day, that great day of the feast, Jesus stood and cried, saying, If any man thirst, let him come unto me, and drink.
modernText: Now on the last and greatest day of the feast, Jesus stood and cried out, “If anyone is thirsty, let him come to me and drink!
message: A simple invitation for the depleted: just come, and drink. No qualification, no catching up first, only come thirsty and be filled.

body: Now the Lord of peace himself give you peace always by all means. The Lord be with you all.
modernText: Now may the Lord of peace himself give you peace at all times in all ways. The Lord be with you all.
message: Peace at all times and in every way, which includes this tired, worn-down way. Nothing about your exhaustion disqualifies you from it.

body: Let your conversation be without covetousness; and be content with such things as ye have: for he hath said, I will never leave thee, nor forsake thee.
modernText: Be free from the love of money, content with such things as you have, for he has said, “I will in no way leave you, neither will I in any way forsake you.”
message: On a day you feel like everyone needs something and no one's holding you, this says someone is, and isn't going anywhere.

body: And let the beauty of the LORD our God be upon us: and establish thou the work of our hands upon us; yea, the work of our hands establish thou it.
modernText: Let the favor of the Lord our God be on us. Establish the work of our hands for us. Yes, establish the work of our hands.
message: A prayer for the tiring work to hold, to mean something. The effort you're pouring out while depleted, asked to be made to stick.

body: Cast me not off in the time of old age; forsake me not when my strength faileth.
modernText: Don’t reject me in my old age. Don’t forsake me when my strength fails.
message: An honest prayer for when your strength is failing: don't let go of me now. And the quiet answer underneath: you won't be cast off.

body: The Lord GOD hath given me the tongue of the learned, that I should know how to speak a word in season to him that is weary: he wakeneth morning by morning, he wakeneth mine ear to hear as the learned.
modernText: The Lord Yahweh has given me the tongue of those who are taught, that I may know how to sustain with words him who is weary. He awakens morning by morning, he awakens my ear to hear as those who are taught.
message: A word, specifically for the weary, delivered morning by morning. The verse knows exactly who needs the gentle thing, and when.

body: Watch and pray, that ye enter not into temptation: the spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak.
modernText: Watch and pray, that you don’t enter into temptation. The spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak.”
message: Said with understanding, not scolding. Your spirit wants to, but the body is worn out, and even he acknowledged that's just how it is sometimes.

body: Bear ye one another’s burdens, and so fulfil the law of Christ.
modernText: Bear one another’s burdens, and so fulfill the law of Christ.
message: A reminder that the tired load isn't meant to be carried solo. Letting someone help carry it is the design, not a failure.

body: Be merciful unto me, O God, be merciful unto me: for my soul trusteth in thee: yea, in the shadow of thy wings will I make my refuge, until these calamities be overpast.
modernText: Be merciful to me, God, be merciful to me, for my soul takes refuge in you. Yes, in the shadow of your wings, I will take refuge, until disaster has passed.
message: Shelter under a wing until the hard stretch passes. Not a demand to push through, a place to wait it out and rest.

body: From the end of the earth will I cry unto thee, when my heart is overwhelmed: lead me to the rock that is higher than I.
modernText: From the end of the earth, I will call to you when my heart is overwhelmed. Lead me to the rock that is higher than I.
message: When your heart is overwhelmed and worn out, this just asks to be led somewhere higher and steadier. You don't have to climb it alone.

body: In the day of my trouble I will call upon thee: for thou wilt answer me.
modernText: In the day of my trouble I will call on you, for you will answer me.
message: For the specific tired, heavy day, not trouble in general. This one, the one you're in, is the one it says will be answered.

body: The LORD is good, a strong hold in the day of trouble; and he knoweth them that trust in him.
modernText: Yahweh is good, a stronghold in the day of trouble; and he knows those who take refuge in him.
message: On a worn-out day, a reminder that you're known, not just by the tiredness, but by someone who holds you in it.

body: Why art thou cast down, O my soul? and why art thou disquieted in me? hope thou in God: for I shall yet praise him for the help of his countenance.
modernText: Why are you in despair, my soul? Why are you disturbed within me? Hope in God! For I shall still praise him for the saving help of his presence.
message: Talking gently to your own worn-down soul: why so heavy? And then pointing it, softly, back toward hope. A conversation worth having when you're tired.

body: Keep me as the apple of the eye, hide me under the shadow of thy wings,
modernText: Keep me as the apple of your eye. Hide me under the shadow of your wings,
message: Kept close and tucked under a wing, for a day you have nothing left to protect yourself with. Sheltered, precious, no effort required.

body: He sent from above, he took me, he drew me out of many waters.
modernText: He sent from on high. He took me. He drew me out of many waters.
message: Reached down and pulled you out of the deep when you were going under. A rescue image for the days the tiredness feels like drowning.

body: For his anger endureth but a moment; in his favour is life: weeping may endure for a night, but joy cometh in the morning.
modernText: For his anger is but for a moment. His favor is for a lifetime. Weeping may stay for the night, but joy comes in the morning.
message: It doesn't deny the long, heavy night. It just quietly promises the morning is coming, and the weight won't stay forever.

body: How excellent is thy lovingkindness, O God! therefore the children of men put their trust under the shadow of thy wings.
modernText: How precious is your loving kindness, God! The children of men take refuge under the shadow of your wings.
message: Somewhere small and covered to rest under. On a tired day, a place to just be sheltered while you have nothing to give.

body: I waited patiently for the LORD; and he inclined unto me, and heard my cry.
modernText: I waited patiently for Yahweh. He turned to me, and heard my cry.
message: Waiting, worn out, and being heard anyway. The patience of a tired soul isn't wasted, something is leaning in to listen.

body: He brought me up also out of an horrible pit, out of the miry clay, and set my feet upon a rock, and established my goings.
modernText: He brought me up also out of a horrible pit, out of the miry clay. He set my feet on a rock, and gave me a firm place to stand.
message: Lifted out of the sinking, miry place and set on something solid. The after-picture for a day that feels like quicksand.

body: God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble.
modernText: God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble.
message: A refuge and a help that's present right now, not later. On a tired day, somewhere to sink into that's already here.

body: Because thou hast been my help, therefore in the shadow of thy wings will I rejoice.
modernText: For you have been my help. I will rejoice in the shadow of your wings.
message: Even from under the wing, worn out and sheltering, there's room for a little gladness. Rest that doesn't have to be joyless.

body: My soul followeth hard after thee: thy right hand upholdeth me.
modernText: My soul stays close to you. Your right hand holds me up.
message: Even when your following feels like dragging, a hand is upholding you. You're held even when you can barely keep up.

body: Which holdeth our soul in life, and suffereth not our feet to be moved.
modernText: who preserves our life among the living, and doesn’t allow our feet to be moved.
message: Held in life, kept steady, a behind-the-scenes holding you don't notice until you're too tired to hold yourself.

body: Be thou my strong habitation, whereunto I may continually resort: thou hast given commandment to save me; for thou art my rock and my fortress.
modernText: Be to me a rock of refuge to which I may always go. Give the command to save me, for you are my rock and my fortress.
message: A place to go back to, again and again, as often as you need. Not a one-time rescue, a standing door for the worn-out.

body: O turn unto me, and have mercy upon me; give thy strength unto thy servant, and save the son of thine handmaid.
modernText: Turn to me, and have mercy on me! Give your strength to your servant. Save the son of your servant.
message: A plain, tired ask: just give me some strength. You don't have to generate it, only request it, and receive.

body: I watch, and am as a sparrow alone upon the house top.
modernText: I watch, and have become like a sparrow that is alone on the housetop.
message: The verse knows the lonely, worn-out kind of tired, a sparrow alone on a roof. It doesn't fix it, it just sees it honestly.

body: Seek the LORD, and his strength: seek his face evermore.
modernText: Seek Yahweh and his strength. Seek his face forever more.
message: Seek the strength, not just the solution. On an empty day, the resource you're low on is available, if you just turn toward it.

body: For he satisfieth the longing soul, and filleth the hungry soul with goodness.
modernText: For he satisfies the longing soul. He fills the hungry soul with good.
message: The longing soul satisfied, the hungry soul filled with goodness. A promise for the exact depleted, running-on-empty feeling.

body: The LORD preserveth the simple: I was brought low, and he helped me.
modernText: Yahweh preserves the simple. I was brought low, and he saved me.
message: Brought low, and then helped. The verse names the going-down and the being-caught in the same quiet breath.

body: My soul fainteth for thy salvation: but I hope in thy word.
modernText: My soul faints for your salvation. I hope in your word.
message: An honest line for a fainting, worn-out soul, still quietly hoping. The tiredness and the hope allowed to exist together.

body: Mine eyes fail for thy word, saying, When wilt thou comfort me?
modernText: My eyes fail for your word. I say, “When will you comfort me?”
message: Eyes failing from waiting, asking plainly: when will the comfort come? The verse sits in the tired longing without rushing it.

body: Uphold me according unto thy word, that I may live: and let me not be ashamed of my hope.
modernText: Uphold me according to your word, that I may live. Let me not be ashamed of my hope.
message: Just, hold me up enough to keep going. A small, tired prayer for the days you only have strength to ask to be held.

body: Hold thou me up, and I shall be safe: and I will have respect unto thy statutes continually.
modernText: Hold me up, and I will be safe, and will have respect for your statutes continually.
message: Held up, and therefore safe. On a tired day, you don't have to keep yourself steady, you just have to let yourself be held.

body: Behold, he that keepeth Israel shall neither slumber nor sleep.
modernText: Behold, he who keeps Israel will neither slumber nor sleep.
message: While you finally sleep, the one keeping you doesn't. You can rest all the way, because the watch never clocks out.

body: The LORD is thy keeper: the LORD is thy shade upon thy right hand.
modernText: Yahweh is your keeper. Yahweh is your shade on your right hand.
message: A keeper and a shade, right beside you. Shelter from the glare on a day you have no energy to shield yourself.

body: The sun shall not smite thee by day, nor the moon by night.
modernText: The sun will not harm you by day, nor the moon by night.
message: Protected through the whole exhausting cycle, day and night. The worn-out hours, all of them, watched over.

body: The LORD shall preserve thee from all evil: he shall preserve thy soul.
modernText: Yahweh will keep you from all evil. He will keep your soul.
message: Preserved, kept, your very soul guarded while you're too tired to guard it. Steady words for a depleted day.

body: When my spirit was overwhelmed within me, then thou knewest my path. In the way wherein I walked have they privily laid a snare for me.
modernText: When my spirit was overwhelmed within me, you knew my route. On the path in which I walk, they have hidden a snare for me.
message: Right when your spirit is overwhelmed and worn out, the path is still known, by someone who isn't overwhelmed with you.

body: O LORD, be gracious unto us; we have waited for thee: be thou their arm every morning, our salvation also in the time of trouble.
modernText: Yahweh, be gracious to us. We have waited for you. Be our strength every morning, our salvation also in the time of trouble.
message: A morning ask for strength that isn't yours: be our arm today. Borrowed strength, requested fresh each tired day.

body: He shall feed his flock like a shepherd: he shall gather the lambs with his arm, and carry them in his bosom, and shall gently lead those that are with young.
modernText: He will feed his flock like a shepherd. He will gather the lambs in his arm, and carry them in his bosom. He will gently lead those who have their young.
message: The gentlest shepherd image: carrying the lambs, gently leading the ones too worn to keep pace. Tenderness for the tired.

body: A bruised reed shall he not break, and the smoking flax shall he not quench: he shall bring forth judgment unto truth.
modernText: He won’t break a bruised reed. He won’t quench a dimly burning wick. He will faithfully bring justice.
message: The gentlest verse for the most depleted day. Already bent, barely flickering, and the response isn't to snap you, it's to handle you with care.

body: But now thus saith the LORD that created thee, O Jacob, and he that formed thee, O Israel, Fear not: for I have redeemed thee, I have called thee by thy name; thou art mine.
modernText: But now Yahweh who created you, Jacob, and he who formed you, Israel, says: “Don’t be afraid, for I have redeemed you. I have called you by your name. You are mine.
message: Called by name, claimed, on a day you feel like a worn-out nobody. You're known and belong, even this depleted.

body: For I will pour water upon him that is thirsty, and floods upon the dry ground: I will pour my spirit upon thy seed, and my blessing upon thine offspring:
modernText: For I will pour water on him who is thirsty, and streams on the dry ground. I will pour my Spirit on your descendants, and my blessing on your offspring:
message: Water poured on the thirsty, floods on the dry ground. A picture of being drenched and revived exactly when you'd gone parched.

body: For the LORD shall comfort Zion: he will comfort all her waste places; and he will make her wilderness like Eden, and her desert like the garden of the LORD; joy and gladness shall be found therein, thanksgiving, and the voice of melody.
modernText: For Yahweh has comforted Zion. He has comforted all her waste places, and has made her wilderness like Eden, and her desert like the garden of Yahweh. Joy and gladness will be found in them, thanksgiving, and the voice of melody.
message: Comfort that turns a wasteland back into a garden. For a tired, dried-out stretch, a promise of being made lush again.

body: Ho, every one that thirsteth, come ye to the waters, and he that hath no money; come ye, buy, and eat; yea, come, buy wine and milk without money and without price.
modernText: “Hey! Come, everyone who thirsts, to the waters! Come, he who has no money, buy, and eat! Yes, come, buy wine and milk without money and without price.
message: An open call for the depleted and dry: just come, no money, no merit. Come empty and be filled.

body: Wherefore do ye spend money for that which is not bread? and your labour for that which satisfieth not? hearken diligently unto me, and eat ye that which is good, and let your soul delight itself in fatness.
modernText: Why do you spend money for that which is not bread, and your labor for that which doesn’t satisfy? Listen diligently to me, and eat that which is good, and let your soul delight itself in richness.
message: Stop spending yourself on what doesn't fill. Come eat what's actually good, and let your worn-out soul be satisfied.

body: To appoint unto them that mourn in Zion, to give unto them beauty for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning, the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness; that they might be called trees of righteousness, the planting of the LORD, that he might be glorified.
modernText: to provide for those who mourn in Zion, to give to them a garland for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning, the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness, that they may be called trees of righteousness, the planting of Yahweh, that he may be glorified.
message: An exchange, not an erasure. The ashes of a burned-out stretch traded for something beautiful, the heaviness for a lighter oil.

body: Fear not, little flock; for it is your Father’s good pleasure to give you the kingdom.
modernText: Don’t be afraid, little flock, for it is your Father’s good pleasure to give you the Kingdom.
message: Called little flock, tenderly, on a day you feel small and spent. Spoken to gently, with the whole kingdom behind it.

body: Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you: not as the world giveth, give I unto you. Let not your heart be troubled, neither let it be afraid.
modernText: Peace I leave with you. My peace I give to you; not as the world gives, I give to you. Don’t let your heart be troubled, neither let it be fearful.
message: A peace that isn't the world's kind, left with you like a gift. For a weary heart, permission to stop being troubled and just receive it.

body: Who comforteth us in all our tribulation, that we may be able to comfort them which are in any trouble, by the comfort wherewith we ourselves are comforted of God.
modernText: who comforts us in all our affliction, that we may be able to comfort those who are in any affliction, through the comfort with which we ourselves are comforted by God.
message: Comfort in all of it, no kind of worn-out too small or too big to qualify. The tired day is squarely inside the 'all.'

body: Nevertheless God, that comforteth those that are cast down, comforted us by the coming of Titus;
modernText: Nevertheless, he who comforts the lowly, God, comforted us by the coming of Titus,
message: Comfort aimed specifically at the cast-down, the depleted. Not the thriving, the ones at the bottom are exactly who it finds.

body: And the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.
modernText: And the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, will guard your hearts and your thoughts in Christ Jesus.
message: A peace that stands guard over your worn-out heart and mind. You don't have to defend yourself today, the peace does it.

body: But my God shall supply all your need according to his riches in glory by Christ Jesus.
modernText: My God will supply every need of yours according to his riches in glory in Christ Jesus.
message: Need, not every want, and all of it supplied. On an empty day, a promise sized to exactly what you actually require, no more.

body: Casting all your care upon him; for he careth for you.
modernText: casting all your worries on him, because he cares for you.
message: All the care, handed over, because you're cared for. On a tired day, permission to set the whole load down with someone who's got you.

body: But the God of all grace, who hath called us unto his eternal glory by Christ Jesus, after that ye have suffered a while, make you perfect, stablish, strengthen, settle you.
modernText: But may the God of all grace, who called you to his eternal glory by Christ Jesus, after you have suffered a little while, perfect, establish, strengthen, and settle you.
message: After the hard, draining stretch, not a vague 'it gets better,' but settled, strengthened, steadied. The after is part of the promise.

body: Let us therefore come boldly unto the throne of grace, that we may obtain mercy, and find grace to help in time of need.
modernText: Let’s therefore draw near with boldness to the throne of grace, that we may receive mercy and may find grace for help in time of need.
message: Come boldly, even worn out and empty-handed. Grace to help, available in the exact time of need, no appointment required.

body: Which hope we have as an anchor of the soul, both sure and stedfast, and which entereth into that within the veil;
modernText: This hope we have as an anchor of the soul, a hope both sure and steadfast and entering into that which is within the veil;
message: An anchor for the part of you that's drifting in the tiredness. Something holding steady below the surface while the top goes slack.

body: Now unto him that is able to keep you from falling, and to present you faultless before the presence of his glory with exceeding joy,
modernText: Now to him who is able to keep them from stumbling, and to present you faultless before the presence of his glory in great joy,
message: Kept from falling, not by your own grip, but by someone able to hold you. On a tired day, the staying-upright isn't all on you.

body: But I will sing of thy power; yea, I will sing aloud of thy mercy in the morning: for thou hast been my defence and refuge in the day of my trouble.
modernText: But I will sing of your strength. Yes, I will sing aloud of your loving kindness in the morning. For you have been my high tower, a refuge in the day of my distress.
message: A defence and refuge, proven in past tired days. Something worth leaning on again, because it held before.

body: Thou shalt increase my greatness, and comfort me on every side.
modernText: Increase my honor and comfort me again.
message: Comforted on every side, surrounded by it. For a depleted day, a picture of being held and tended from all directions at once.

body: When I said, My foot slippeth; thy mercy, O LORD, held me up.
modernText: When I said, “My foot is slipping!” Your loving kindness, Yahweh, held me up.
message: That moment you felt yourself giving out, and something caught you. Mercy showing up right at the slip, holding the tired upright.

body: When the poor and needy seek water, and there is none, and their tongue faileth for thirst, I the LORD will hear them, I the God of Israel will not forsake them.
modernText: The poor and needy seek water, and there is none. Their tongue fails for thirst. I, Yahweh, will answer them. I, the God of Israel, will not forsake them.
message: For the parched, worn-out, searching feeling, this promises the thirst gets heard, not ignored. The tired and empty aren't forsaken.

body: Surely goodness and mercy shall follow me all the days of my life: and I will dwell in the house of the LORD for ever.
modernText: Surely goodness and loving kindness shall follow me all the days of my life, and I will dwell in Yahweh’s house forever.
message: Goodness and mercy trailing you, all the days, including the worn-out ones. Even when you're too tired to notice, they're keeping up.

body: Have mercy upon me, O LORD; for I am weak: O LORD, heal me; for my bones are vexed.
modernText: Have mercy on me, Yahweh, for I am faint. Yahweh, heal me, for my bones are troubled.
message: A plain, tired prayer: have mercy, I'm weak. No dressing it up, no pretending. Sometimes 'I'm weak' is the whole honest thing to say.

body: Consider and hear me, O LORD my God: lighten mine eyes, lest I sleep the sleep of death;
modernText: Behold, and answer me, Yahweh, my God. Give light to my eyes, lest I sleep in death;
message: An ask to have your eyes lightened when they're heavy with exhaustion. The verse knows the kind of tired that feels like fading, and prays against it.

body: I will love thee, O LORD, my strength.
modernText: I love you, Yahweh, my strength.
message: Leaning your whole tired weight on a strength that isn't yours. On an empty day, calling something else your strength is permission to stop being it.

body: For thou wilt light my candle: the LORD my God will enlighten my darkness.
modernText: For you will light my lamp, Yahweh. My God will light up my darkness.
message: Even a small candle, lit for you, when you have no light left to make. A little glow in a worn-out, dim stretch.

body: It is God that girdeth me with strength, and maketh my way perfect.
modernText: the God who arms me with strength, and makes my way perfect?
message: Strength strapped on from outside, the path smoothed. For a tired day, equipped by something other than your own reserves.

body: Send thee help from the sanctuary, and strengthen thee out of Zion;
modernText: send you help from the sanctuary, grant you support from Zion,
message: Help and strength sent to you, from somewhere steadier than yourself. On an empty day, you're the one being resupplied.

body: Turn thee unto me, and have mercy upon me; for I am desolate and afflicted.
modernText: Turn to me, and have mercy on me, for I am desolate and afflicted.
message: It uses the word desolate, and doesn't flinch. For a lonely, worn-out day, a verse that just names it honestly and asks to be turned toward.

body: Look upon mine affliction and my pain; and forgive all my sins.
modernText: Consider my affliction and my travail. Forgive all my sins.
message: A simple ask to just be seen in the tiredness and ache. Sometimes you don't need it fixed, you need it looked at and not dismissed.

body: Hide not thy face far from me; put not thy servant away in anger: thou hast been my help; leave me not, neither forsake me, O God of my salvation.
modernText: Don’t hide your face from me. Don’t put your servant away in anger. You have been my help. Don’t abandon me, neither forsake me, God of my salvation.
message: A worn-out plea not to be left alone, grounded in the fact that help has come before. On a tired day, remembering it held last time.

body: The LORD is their strength, and he is the saving strength of his anointed.
modernText: Yahweh is their strength. He is a stronghold of salvation to his anointed.
message: Strength as something that saves, not just sustains. For the depleted, a source that doesn't just keep you going but actually rescues.

body: Save thy people, and bless thine inheritance: feed them also, and lift them up for ever.
modernText: Save your people, and bless your inheritance. Be their shepherd also, and bear them up forever.
message: Fed and lifted up, carried, like a shepherd with worn-out sheep. A gentle picture for a day you need to be tended, not driven.

body: Have mercy upon me, O LORD, for I am in trouble: mine eye is consumed with grief, yea, my soul and my belly.
modernText: Have mercy on me, Yahweh, for I am in distress. My eye, my soul, and my body waste away with grief.
message: The verse describes exhaustion that's reached the whole body, eyes, soul, gut. It doesn't tidy it up, it just says it plainly.

body: Our soul waiteth for the LORD: he is our help and our shield.
modernText: Our soul has waited for Yahweh. He is our help and our shield.
message: Waiting, worn out, watching for someone who's actually coming. Help and cover on the way, so you can rest in the meantime.

body: I sought the LORD, and he heard me, and delivered me from all my fears.
modernText: I sought Yahweh, and he answered me, and delivered me from all my fears.
message: The seeking got heard and answered, all the fears included. On a tired day, the reaching counts, even when it's faint.

body: Though he fall, he shall not be utterly cast down: for the LORD upholdeth him with his hand.
modernText: Though he stumble, he shall not fall, for Yahweh holds him up with his hand.
message: It allows for falling, for the tired stumble. It just says the fall isn't final, because of whose hand is under you.

body: Lord, all my desire is before thee; and my groaning is not hid from thee.
modernText: Lord, all my desire is before you. My groaning is not hidden from you.
message: Even the wordless groaning of a worn-out day is heard, not hidden. You don't have to explain the tiredness for it to be known.

body: Why art thou cast down, O my soul? and why art thou disquieted within me? hope in God: for I shall yet praise him, who is the health of my countenance, and my God.
modernText: Why are you in despair, my soul? Why are you disturbed within me? Hope in God! For I shall still praise him: my Savior, my helper, and my God.
message: Talking gently to your own worn-down soul: why so heavy? And pointing it, softly, back toward hope. A kind conversation for a tired day.

body: Arise for our help, and redeem us for thy mercies’ sake.
modernText: Rise up to help us. Redeem us for your loving kindness’ sake.
message: A short, tired cry: just get up and help us. On an empty day, you're allowed to ask plainly for rescue, on the basis of mercy, not merit.

body: Behold, God is mine helper: the Lord is with them that uphold my soul.
modernText: Behold, God is my helper. The Lord is the one who sustains my soul.
message: Four plain words for a day you feel unsupported and worn out: God is mine helper. Said flatly, like a fact to lean on.

body: For thou hast been a shelter for me, and a strong tower from the enemy.
modernText: For you have been a refuge for me, a strong tower from the enemy.
message: Already proven, past tense: thou hast been a shelter. On a tired day, a track record of being sheltered you can lean on again.

body: Save me, O God; for the waters are come in unto my soul.
modernText: Save me, God, for the waters have come up to my neck!
message: An honest image of tiredness that's reached the soul, water up to the neck. The verse doesn't rush you out of it, it cries out from inside it.

body: But I am poor and sorrowful: let thy salvation, O God, set me up on high.
modernText: But I am in pain and distress. Let your salvation, God, protect me.
message: Poor and sorrowful, worn down, and asking to be lifted up high. The verse holds the low honestly and still reaches for the lift.

body: He shall spare the poor and needy, and shall save the souls of the needy.
modernText: He will have pity on the poor and needy. He will save the souls of the needy.
message: The needy, the depleted, specifically spared and saved. On an empty day, having nothing to offer is exactly the qualification.

body: Nevertheless I am continually with thee: thou hast holden me by my right hand.
modernText: Nevertheless, I am continually with you. You have held my right hand.
message: Held by the hand, continually, even when you feel like you're barely holding on. The grip is the other way around.

body: Bow down thine ear, O LORD, hear me: for I am poor and needy.
modernText: Hear, Yahweh, and answer me, for I am poor and needy.
message: A tired, honest prayer: bend down and listen, because I'm empty and need help. No posturing, just a plain cry to be heard.

body: For I am poor and needy, and my heart is wounded within me.
modernText: for I am poor and needy. My heart is wounded within me.
message: It names a wounded heart alongside the exhaustion. For a day you're both tired and hurting, a verse that holds both without tidying them.

body: I love the LORD, because he hath heard my voice and my supplications.
modernText: I love Yahweh, because he listens to my voice, and my cries for mercy.
message: Love that grew out of being heard. For a worn-out day, the quiet gratitude that your cry actually landed somewhere.

body: For thou hast delivered my soul from death, mine eyes from tears, and my feet from falling.
modernText: For you have delivered my soul from death, my eyes from tears, and my feet from falling.
message: Soul, eyes, feet, the whole worn-out self delivered. A verse that takes inventory of the tiredness and answers every part of it.

body: I called upon the LORD in distress: the LORD answered me, and set me in a large place.
modernText: Out of my distress, I called on Yah. Yah answered me with freedom.
message: Called out from the tight, pressed-in place and given room to breathe. Sometimes the answer to the tired is just space.

body: Though I walk in the midst of trouble, thou wilt revive me: thou shalt stretch forth thine hand against the wrath of mine enemies, and thy right hand shall save me.
modernText: Though I walk in the middle of trouble, you will revive me. You will stretch out your hand against the wrath of my enemies. Your right hand will save me.
message: Not lifted out of the trouble, revived in the middle of walking through it. Kept going when you thought you were out of gas.

body: The LORD lifteth up the meek: he casteth the wicked down to the ground.
modernText: Yahweh upholds the humble. He brings the wicked down to the ground.
message: The lowly, the worn-down, specifically lifted up. On a tired day, being at the bottom is exactly who gets raised.

body: The LORD taketh pleasure in them that fear him, in those that hope in his mercy.
modernText: Yahweh takes pleasure in those who fear him, in those who hope in his loving kindness.
message: Pleasure taken not in your output, but in your hoping. On an empty day, just quietly hoping is enough to be delighted in.

body: LORD, thou wilt ordain peace for us: for thou also hast wrought all our works in us.
modernText: Yahweh, you will ordain peace for us, for you have also done all our work for us.
message: Peace as something ordained, arranged for you on purpose. On a tired day, rest isn't a fluke you have to hope for, it's set up for you.

body: The meek also shall increase their joy in the LORD, and the poor among men shall rejoice in the Holy One of Israel.
modernText: The humble also will increase their joy in Yahweh, and the poor among men will rejoice in the Holy One of Israel.
message: Increasing joy for the meek, the quiet, the worn-down. The verse promises the gladness grows, even from a low, tired place.

body: And the ransomed of the LORD shall return, and come to Zion with songs and everlasting joy upon their heads: they shall obtain joy and gladness, and sorrow and sighing shall flee away.
modernText: Then Yahweh’s ransomed ones will return, and come with singing to Zion; and everlasting joy will be on their heads. They will obtain gladness and joy, and sorrow and sighing will flee away.”
message: A picture of a day when the sighing finally leaves. For a tired stretch, a reminder that this isn't the permanent weather.

body: Comfort ye, comfort ye my people, saith your God.
modernText: “Comfort, comfort my people,” says your God.
message: Comfort, said twice, like it couldn't wait to be repeated. On a worn-out day, the double insistence that comfort is for you.

body: For the mountains shall depart, and the hills be removed; but my kindness shall not depart from thee, neither shall the covenant of my peace be removed, saith the LORD that hath mercy on thee.
modernText: For the mountains may depart, and the hills be removed; but my loving kindness will not depart from you, and my covenant of peace will not be removed,” says Yahweh who has mercy on you.
message: Even if the solid things shift, the kindness doesn't. Something that outlasts the tired, unsteady stretch you're in.

body: These things I have spoken unto you, that in me ye might have peace. In the world ye shall have tribulation: but be of good cheer; I have overcome the world.
modernText: I have told you these things, that in me you may have peace. In the world you have trouble; but cheer up! I have overcome the world.”
message: Good cheer with a backbone, for a worn-out heart. Not 'try harder,' just 'the hard part is already beaten, you can lean on that.'

body: Now the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing, that ye may abound in hope, through the power of the Holy Ghost.
modernText: Now may the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing, that you may abound in hope, in the power of the Holy Spirit.
message: Filled, not drained, with joy and peace. On an empty day, a prayer that you'd be topped back up from a source outside yourself.

body: Persecuted, but not forsaken; cast down, but not destroyed;
modernText: pursued, yet not forsaken; struck down, yet not destroyed;
message: Cast down, worn out, but not destroyed. The verse admits the knocked-down part and insists it isn't the end of you.

body: Finally, brethren, farewell. Be perfect, be of good comfort, be of one mind, live in peace; and the God of love and peace shall be with you.
modernText: Finally, brothers, rejoice! Be perfected. Be comforted. Be of the same mind. Live in peace, and the God of love and peace will be with you.
message: A gentle sign-off: be comforted, and know love and peace are with you. For a tired day, a soft blessing to rest under.

body: Strengthened with all might, according to his glorious power, unto all patience and longsuffering with joyfulness;
modernText: strengthened with all power, according to the might of his glory, for all endurance and perseverance with joy,
message: Strengthened specifically for the long, draining haul, and somehow with joy in it. Endurance that isn't white-knuckled.

body: Notwithstanding the Lord stood with me, and strengthened me; that by me the preaching might be fully known, and that all the Gentiles might hear: and I was delivered out of the mouth of the lion.
modernText: But the Lord stood by me and strengthened me, that through me the message might be fully proclaimed, and that all the Gentiles might hear. So I was delivered out of the mouth of the lion.
message: On a day you felt abandoned and spent, this says someone stood with you and gave you strength. Company and a refill, right when you were alone.

body: Wherefore lift up the hands which hang down, and the feeble knees;
modernText: Therefore lift up the hands that hang down and the feeble knees,
message: A verse for literal exhaustion: drooping hands, shaky knees. It doesn't scold the weakness, it just gently helps you lift them.

body: God is in the midst of her; she shall not be moved: God shall help her, and that right early.
modernText: God is within her. She shall not be moved. God will help her at dawn.
message: The steadiness isn't out at the edges, it's right in the middle of you, and help comes early. For a tired day, held from the center.

body: Yet the LORD will command his lovingkindness in the day time, and in the night his song shall be with me, and my prayer unto the God of my life.
modernText: Yahweh will command his loving kindness in the daytime. In the night his song shall be with me: a prayer to the God of my life.
message: A kindness for the day and a song for the night. Both halves of an exhausting 24 hours accounted for and tended.

body: Thou tellest my wanderings: put thou my tears into thy bottle: are they not in thy book?
modernText: You count my wanderings. You put my tears into your container. Aren’t they in your book?
message: Your tears collected, kept, not wasted. For a worn-out, teary day, the tender idea that none of it goes unnoticed.

body: But thou, O LORD, art a shield for me; my glory, and the lifter up of mine head.
modernText: But you, Yahweh, are a shield around me, my glory, and the one who lifts up my head.
message: A shield around you and a hand lifting your head when it's hung low with tiredness. Both at once, on a day you're staring at the floor.

body: When thou passest through the waters, I will be with thee; and through the rivers, they shall not overflow thee: when thou walkest through the fire, thou shalt not be burned; neither shall the flame kindle upon thee.
modernText: When you pass through the waters, I will be with you, and through the rivers, they will not overflow you. When you walk through the fire, you will not be burned, and flame will not scorch you.
message: It doesn't promise you'll skip the deep, exhausting water. It promises you won't go under in it, and you won't go through it alone.

body: Like as a father pitieth his children, so the LORD pitieth them that fear him.
modernText: Like a father has compassion on his children, so Yahweh has compassion on those who fear him.
message: Not disappointed in you for being worn out. Looked at the way a parent looks at a tired kid, with tenderness, not judgment.

body: The LORD also will be a refuge for the oppressed, a refuge in times of trouble.
modernText: Yahweh will also be a high tower for the oppressed; a high tower in times of trouble.
message: A refuge specifically for the worn-down and oppressed, in the hard times. Built for exactly the kind of tired you're in.

body: For the needy shall not alway be forgotten: the expectation of the poor shall not perish for ever.
modernText: For the needy shall not always be forgotten, nor the hope of the poor perish forever.
message: A promise to the overlooked and depleted: you won't be forgotten forever. On a tired day, the hope isn't lost, just delayed.

body: For he hath not despised nor abhorred the affliction of the afflicted; neither hath he hid his face from him; but when he cried unto him, he heard.
modernText: For he has not despised nor abhorred the affliction of the afflicted, Neither has he hidden his face from him; but when he cried to him, he heard.
message: Your worn-out, afflicted state isn't held against you. The verse insists it's not despised, just seen, and heard when you cry.

body: The LORD is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear? the LORD is the strength of my life; of whom shall I be afraid?
modernText: Yahweh is my light and my salvation. Whom shall I fear? Yahweh is the strength of my life. Of whom shall I be afraid?
message: Light and salvation for a day you feel dim and spent. Something steady to lean the whole tired weight of your fear against.

body: O LORD my God, I cried unto thee, and thou hast healed me.
modernText: Yahweh my God, I cried to you, and you have healed me.
message: A simple testimony for a worn-out day: I cried, and I was healed. The crying was enough to start the mending.

body: Thou art my hiding place; thou shalt preserve me from trouble; thou shalt compass me about with songs of deliverance. Selah.
modernText: You are my hiding place. You will preserve me from trouble. You will surround me with songs of deliverance.
message: A hiding place to disappear into for a minute. On a tired day, somewhere to be surrounded by something other than the trouble.

body: The righteous cry, and the LORD heareth, and delivereth them out of all their troubles.
modernText: The righteous cry, and Yahweh hears, and delivers them out of all their troubles.
message: The crying out gets heard, no composure required. Just the tired cry, and it reaches someone who answers.

body: Many are the afflictions of the righteous: but the LORD delivereth him out of them all.
modernText: Many are the afflictions of the righteous, but Yahweh delivers him out of them all.
message: It doesn't lowball the many afflictions, the layered tiredness. And it doesn't lowball the other side: out of them all.

body: The LORD will strengthen him upon the bed of languishing: thou wilt make all his bed in his sickness.
modernText: Yahweh will sustain him on his sickbed, and restore him from his bed of illness.
message: For the days you can barely get out of bed, this meets you right there, in the languishing. Strength brought to where you lie.

body: And call upon me in the day of trouble: I will deliver thee, and thou shalt glorify me.
modernText: Call on me in the day of trouble. I will deliver you, and you will honor me.”
message: An open invitation with your name on it: call, even worn out, and be answered. You don't have to earn the right to.

body: And I said, Oh that I had wings like a dove! for then would I fly away, and be at rest.
modernText: I said, “Oh that I had wings like a dove! Then I would fly away, and be at rest.
message: That exact fantasy of just flying away somewhere quiet to rest. The Bible has it too. You're not weak for wishing you could escape for a while.

body: Trust in him at all times; ye people, pour out your heart before him: God is a refuge for us. Selah.
modernText: Trust in him at all times, you people. Pour out your heart before him. God is a refuge for us.
message: Pour out your worn-out heart, it says, not tidy it up first. On a tired day, you can bring the unfiltered, depleted version here.

body: A father of the fatherless, and a judge of the widows, is God in his holy habitation.
modernText: A father of the fatherless, and a defender of the widows, is God in his holy habitation.
message: A tender image for a day you feel unparented and on your own: cared for like family by someone who takes that role seriously.

body: God setteth the solitary in families: he bringeth out those which are bound with chains: but the rebellious dwell in a dry land.
modernText: God sets the lonely in families. He brings out the prisoners with singing, but the rebellious dwell in a sun-scorched land.
message: For the lonely kind of tired, this says you're meant to be placed, belonging, not left solitary. You're not as alone as the exhaustion suggests.

body: For the LORD heareth the poor, and despiseth not his prisoners.
modernText: For Yahweh hears the needy, and doesn’t despise his captive people.
message: The poor, the stuck, the depleted, heard and not despised. On a tired day, being at a low point doesn't disqualify your cry.

body: But I am poor and needy: make haste unto me, O God: thou art my help and my deliverer; O LORD, make no tarrying.
modernText: But I am poor and needy. Come to me quickly, God. You are my help and my deliverer. Yahweh, don’t delay.
message: Permission to ask God to hurry. On a worn-out day, urgency isn't irreverent, it's just honest about how empty you feel.

body: Shew me a token for good; that they which hate me may see it, and be ashamed: because thou, LORD, hast holpen me, and comforted me.
modernText: Show me a sign of your goodness, that those who hate me may see it, and be shamed, because you, Yahweh, have helped me, and comforted me.
message: Helped and comforted, both, in the past tense. On a tired day, a reminder that it's been done for you before, and can be again.

body: Then they cried unto the LORD in their trouble, and he delivered them out of their distresses.
modernText: Then they cried to Yahweh in their trouble, and he delivered them out of their distresses,
message: A refrain repeated all through this psalm: they cried, and were delivered. The pattern holds, even on a worn-out day.

body: Then they cried unto the LORD in their trouble, and he saved them out of their distresses.
modernText: Then they cried to Yahweh in their trouble, and he saved them out of their distresses.
message: Again, the same quiet pattern: the cry, the saving. Said more than once because you probably need to hear it more than once.

body: He brought them out of darkness and the shadow of death, and brake their bands in sunder.
modernText: He brought them out of darkness and the shadow of death, and broke away their chains.
message: Brought out of the dark, the chains broken. For a stuck, exhausted stretch, a picture of being freed, not just comforted.

body: Then they cry unto the LORD in their trouble, and he saveth them out of their distresses.
modernText: Then they cry to Yahweh in their trouble, he saves them out of their distresses.
message: The crying and the saving, once more. The verse keeps circling back to it, like it wants the tired to really believe it.

body: He sent his word, and healed them, and delivered them from their destructions.
modernText: He sends his word, and heals them, and delivers them from their graves.
message: Healed by a word sent, gently. On a worn-out day, a picture of being mended from a distance, without having to do anything.

body: Unto the upright there ariseth light in the darkness: he is gracious, and full of compassion, and righteous.
modernText: Light dawns in the darkness for the upright, gracious, merciful, and righteous.
message: Light rising in the dark, not blazing, just rising. For a tired, dim stretch, the quiet promise that it won't stay dark.

body: He raiseth up the poor out of the dust, and lifteth the needy out of the dunghill;
modernText: He raises up the poor out of the dust. Lifts up the needy from the ash heap,
message: Raised up out of the dust, the lowest, most depleted place. On a tired day, being at the bottom is exactly where the lifting starts.

body: Unless thy law had been my delights, I should then have perished in mine affliction.
modernText: Unless your law had been my delight, I would have perished in my affliction.
message: An honest admission: I'd have gone under in the affliction, if I hadn't had something to hold. On a tired day, the one thing you cling to matters.

body: I am afflicted very much: quicken me, O LORD, according unto thy word.
modernText: I am afflicted very much. Revive me, Yahweh, according to your word.
message: A plain, worn-out prayer: I'm really afflicted, please revive me. No pretending it's a little, just asking for life back.

body: The LORD shall preserve thy going out and thy coming in from this time forth, and even for evermore.
modernText: Yahweh will keep your going out and your coming in, from this time forward, and forever more.
message: The ordinary, tiring comings and goings, the commute, the errands, all of it watched over. The worn-out routine isn't unguarded.

body: I wait for the LORD, my soul doth wait, and in his word do I hope.
modernText: I wait for Yahweh. My soul waits. I hope in his word.
message: Waiting said twice, because waiting is the hard part when you're tired. The verse sits in it with you instead of rushing you.

body: And in that day thou shalt say, O LORD, I will praise thee: though thou wast angry with me, thine anger is turned away, and thou comfortedst me.
modernText: In that day you will say, “I will give thanks to you, Yahweh; for though you were angry with me, your anger has turned away and you comfort me.
message: Comfort after a hard stretch, the storm passed. For a tired day, a picture of the turn from strain to being soothed.

body: For the people shall dwell in Zion at Jerusalem: thou shalt weep no more: he will be very gracious unto thee at the voice of thy cry; when he shall hear it, he will answer thee.
modernText: For the people will dwell in Zion at Jerusalem. You will weep no more. He will surely be gracious to you at the voice of your cry. When he hears you, he will answer you.
message: Grace that comes the moment you cry out, not after you've composed yourself. On a worn-out day, the cry is all it takes.

body: Like a crane or a swallow, so did I chatter: I did mourn as a dove: mine eyes fail with looking upward: O LORD, I am oppressed; undertake for me.
modernText: I chattered like a swallow or a crane. I moaned like a dove. My eyes weaken looking upward. Lord, I am oppressed. Be my security.”
message: A short, tired prayer: I'm weighed down, take this over for me. Permission to hand the whole thing off when you've got nothing left.

body: I will open rivers in high places, and fountains in the midst of the valleys: I will make the wilderness a pool of water, and the dry land springs of water.
modernText: I will open rivers on the bare heights, and springs in the middle of the valleys. I will make the wilderness a pool of water, and the dry land springs of water.
message: Water in the dry, barren places, rivers where there were none. A picture of being flooded and refreshed exactly where you'd gone empty.

body: I have blotted out, as a thick cloud, thy transgressions, and, as a cloud, thy sins: return unto me; for I have redeemed thee.
modernText: I have blotted out, as a thick cloud, your transgressions, and, as a cloud, your sins. Return to me, for I have redeemed you.
message: A clean slate and an open door. On a tired day carrying guilt too, this says just come back, you're already redeemed.

body: Can a woman forget her sucking child, that she should not have compassion on the son of her womb? yea, they may forget, yet will I not forget thee.
modernText: “Can a woman forget her nursing child, that she should not have compassion on the son of her womb? Yes, these may forget, yet I will not forget you!
message: A mother forgetting her baby is unthinkable, and the verse says being forgotten by God is even more so. On a worn-out day, you are not slipping anyone's mind.

body: I, even I, am he that comforteth you: who art thou, that thou shouldest be afraid of a man that shall die, and of the son of man which shall be made as grass;
modernText: “I, even I, am he who comforts you. Who are you, that you are afraid of man who shall die, and of the son of man who will be made as grass?
message: The comfort is personal and repeated, I, even I. Not a system, someone, leaning in to steady your tired heart.

body: Thy sun shall no more go down; neither shall thy moon withdraw itself: for the LORD shall be thine everlasting light, and the days of thy mourning shall be ended.
modernText: Your sun will not go down any more, nor will your moon withdraw itself; for Yahweh will be your everlasting light, and the days of your mourning will end.
message: A promise that the long, draining stretch has an end date. For a tired day, a reminder that this isn't the permanent state of things.

body: For the LORD will not cast off for ever:
modernText: For the Lord will not cast off forever.
message: Not forever, the verse insists. However long the hard, tiring stretch feels, it's not the final word, and you're not cast off for good.

body: But though he cause grief, yet will he have compassion according to the multitude of his mercies.
modernText: For though he causes grief, yet he will have compassion according to the multitude of his loving kindnesses.
message: Even the hard stretches come with compassion on the other side. On a tired day, the mercies are described as a multitude, not a trickle.

body: But when he saw the multitudes, he was moved with compassion on them, because they fainted, and were scattered abroad, as sheep having no shepherd.
modernText: But when he saw the multitudes, he was moved with compassion for them, because they were harassed and scattered, like sheep without a shepherd.
message: He looked at worn-out, fainting people and felt compassion, not frustration. On a tired day, the response to your exhaustion is tenderness.

body: For as the sufferings of Christ abound in us, so our consolation also aboundeth by Christ.
modernText: For as the sufferings of Christ abound to us, even so our comfort also abounds through Christ.
message: The comfort keeps pace with the hardship, abounding to match it. On a tired day, the consolation is sized to the exhaustion.

body: Now our Lord Jesus Christ himself, and God, even our Father, which hath loved us, and hath given us everlasting consolation and good hope through grace,
modernText: Now our Lord Jesus Christ himself, and God our Father, who loved us and gave us eternal comfort and good hope through grace,
message: Everlasting comfort and good hope, already given through grace. Not earned by holding it together, just given, even to the worn-out.

body: Comfort your hearts, and stablish you in every good word and work.
modernText: comfort your hearts and establish you in every good work and word.
message: Comfort your heart and steady you, the two things a tired day has been quietly chipping at, named and tended.

body: They shall hunger no more, neither thirst any more; neither shall the sun light on them, nor any heat.
modernText: They will never be hungry or thirsty any more. The sun won’t beat on them, nor any heat;
message: A glimpse of a day with no more hunger, no more thirst, no more running on empty. For a tired day, a picture of the exhaustion finally ending.

body: For the Lamb which is in the midst of the throne shall feed them, and shall lead them unto living fountains of waters: and God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes.
modernText: for the Lamb who is in the middle of the throne shepherds them and leads them to springs of life-giving waters. And God will wipe away every tear from their eyes.”
message: A tender future image: every tear personally wiped away. For a worn-out, teary day, a reminder of where it's all ultimately heading.

body: I will be glad and rejoice in thy mercy: for thou hast considered my trouble; thou hast known my soul in adversities;
modernText: I will be glad and rejoice in your loving kindness, for you have seen my affliction. You have known my soul in adversities.
message: Your trouble, considered, actually looked at and weighed. On a tired day, the comfort of knowing your struggle wasn't overlooked.

body: The LORD of hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our refuge. Selah.
modernText: Yahweh of Armies is with us. The God of Jacob is our refuge.
message: With us, and a refuge. A steady refrain to lean on when you're worn out, worth repeating until it lands.

body: The LORD is on my side; I will not fear: what can man do unto me?
modernText: Yahweh is on my side. I will not be afraid. What can man do to me?
message: Someone on your side changes the math on a tired, fearful day. You can say 'I will not fear' and actually mean it.

body: The LORD is nigh unto all them that call upon him, to all that call upon him in truth.
modernText: Yahweh is near to all those who call on him, to all who call on him in truth.
message: Near, specifically, to everyone who calls, worn out or not. The calling is the only requirement, and nearness is the response.

body: Because he hath inclined his ear unto me, therefore will I call upon him as long as I live.
modernText: Because he has turned his ear to me, therefore I will call on him as long as I live.
message: Because he listened once, a decision to keep coming back. The relief of knowing the line stays open, even on the tired days.

body: But the salvation of the righteous is of the LORD: he is their strength in the time of trouble.
modernText: But the salvation of the righteous is from Yahweh. He is their stronghold in the time of trouble.
message: Strength that shows up on schedule, in the time of trouble, not a general reserve but a specific delivery for the worn-out now.

body: Shew thy marvellous lovingkindness, O thou that savest by thy right hand them which put their trust in thee from those that rise up against them.
modernText: Show your marvelous loving kindness, you who save those who take refuge by your right hand from their enemies.
message: A plea for the kindness to show up, from someone worn out and in need of saving. On a tired day, asking plainly for tenderness is allowed.

body: Unto thee, O LORD, do I lift up my soul.
modernText: To you, Yahweh, I lift up my soul.
message: Lifting up the tired soul, handing it over. On an empty day, even that lifting is enough of an offering.

body: Bow down thine ear to me; deliver me speedily: be thou my strong rock, for an house of defence to save me.
modernText: Bow down your ear to me. Deliver me speedily. Be to me a strong rock, a house of defense to save me.
message: A worn-out ask: lean in, hurry, be my steady place. For a tired day, permission to want help, and want it soon.

body: Into thine hand I commit my spirit: thou hast redeemed me, O LORD God of truth.
modernText: Into your hand I commend my spirit. You redeem me, Yahweh, God of truth.
message: Handing over your whole spirit, trusting someone else to hold it for the night. On a tired day, permission to stop gripping and just let go.

body: Let thy mercy, O LORD, be upon us, according as we hope in thee.
modernText: Let your loving kindness be on us, Yahweh, since we have hoped in you.
message: Mercy sized to your hope, resting over you. On a worn-out day, you don't have to hope big, just enough to let the mercy land.

body: This poor man cried, and the LORD heard him, and saved him out of all his troubles.
modernText: This poor man cried, and Yahweh heard him, and saved him out of all his troubles.
message: The poor, depleted man cried, and was heard and saved. On a tired day, being at a low point is exactly where the rescue starts.

body: Thy mercy, O LORD, is in the heavens; and thy faithfulness reacheth unto the clouds.
modernText: Your loving kindness, Yahweh, is in the heavens. Your faithfulness reaches to the skies.
message: Mercy as big as the sky, faithfulness past the clouds. For a tired day, a reminder that the supply is far larger than your empty feels.

body: Withhold not thou thy tender mercies from me, O LORD: let thy lovingkindness and thy truth continually preserve me.
modernText: Don’t withhold your tender mercies from me, Yahweh. Let your loving kindness and your truth continually preserve me.
message: A plain, worn-out ask: don't hold back the tenderness. On an empty day, you're allowed to want to be handled gently.

body: For thou hast delivered my soul from death: wilt not thou deliver my feet from falling, that I may walk before God in the light of the living?
modernText: For you have delivered my soul from death, and prevented my feet from falling, that I may walk before God in the light of the living.
message: Already rescued once, now asking to be kept from stumbling. On a tired day, the one who caught you before can keep your footing now.

body: I will cry unto God most high; unto God that performeth all things for me.
modernText: I cry out to God Most High, to God who accomplishes my requests for me.
message: The one who handles things for you, so you don't have to carry it all. On an empty day, permission to let some of it be done on your behalf.

body: Hear my cry, O God; attend unto my prayer.
modernText: Hear my cry, God. Listen to my prayer.
message: A short, tired cry: just hear me. On a worn-out day, the prayer doesn't have to be eloquent, only heard.

body: In God is my salvation and my glory: the rock of my strength, and my refuge, is in God.
modernText: My salvation and my honor is with God. The rock of my strength, and my refuge, is in God.
message: A rock of strength to lean the whole tired weight on. On an empty day, the sturdiness is somewhere other than your own legs.

body: Iniquities prevail against me: as for our transgressions, thou shalt purge them away.
modernText: Sins overwhelmed me, but you atoned for our transgressions.
message: A clean slate, the weight of what you've carried wiped off. On a tired day also heavy with guilt, this quietly lightens the second load.

body: But as for me, my prayer is unto thee, O LORD, in an acceptable time: O God, in the multitude of thy mercy hear me, in the truth of thy salvation.
modernText: But as for me, my prayer is to you, Yahweh, in an acceptable time. God, in the abundance of your loving kindness, answer me in the truth of your salvation.
message: Your prayer arriving at an acceptable time, heard in the mercy. On a worn-out day, the timing of your reaching out isn't off, it's welcome.

body: I will go in the strength of the Lord GOD: I will make mention of thy righteousness, even of thine only.
modernText: I will come with the mighty acts of the Lord Yahweh. I will make mention of your righteousness, even of yours alone.
message: Going in borrowed strength, not your own. On an empty day, permission to move on a power that isn't coming from your drained reserves.

body: They go from strength to strength, every one of them in Zion appeareth before God.
modernText: They go from strength to strength. Every one of them appears before God in Zion.
message: Not strength running out, but strength to strength, replenished along the way. For a tired stretch, a picture of being refilled as you go.

body: Be merciful unto me, O Lord: for I cry unto thee daily.
modernText: Be merciful to me, Lord, for I call to you all day long.
message: Crying out daily, worn down, and asking plainly for mercy. On a tired day, the repeated reaching is honest, not weak.

body: Mine eye mourneth by reason of affliction: LORD, I have called daily upon thee, I have stretched out my hands unto thee.
modernText: My eyes are dim from grief. I have called on you daily, Yahweh. I have spread out my hands to you.
message: From the darkest psalm in the book, hands stretched out daily in exhaustion. The verse honors the long, tired reaching, even when it feels unanswered.

body: For he shall give his angels charge over thee, to keep thee in all thy ways.
modernText: For he will put his angels in charge of you, to guard you in all your ways.
message: Guarded, watched over, even on the days you're too tired to watch yourself. Someone keeping you in all your worn-out ways.

body: They shall bear thee up in their hands, lest thou dash thy foot against a stone.
modernText: They will bear you up in their hands, so that you won’t dash your foot against a stone.
message: Borne up in hands, caught before you stumble. On a tired day, a picture of being carried past the thing that would've tripped you.

body: Unless the LORD had been my help, my soul had almost dwelt in silence.
modernText: Unless Yahweh had been my help, my soul would have soon lived in silence.
message: An honest admission: without that help, I'd have gone silent, gone under. On a tired day, naming how close the edge felt, and what kept you from it.

body: My soul cleaveth unto the dust: quicken thou me according to thy word.
modernText: My soul is laid low in the dust. Revive me according to your word!
message: A soul flat in the dust, asking only to be revived. For a worn-out day, the plainest prayer: just bring me back to life a little.

body: Thou hast beset me behind and before, and laid thine hand upon me.
modernText: You hem me in behind and before. You laid your hand on me.
message: Surrounded, front and back, a hand laid on you. On a tired day, a picture of being completely encircled and held, nothing exposed.

body: Yea, the darkness hideth not from thee; but the night shineth as the day: the darkness and the light are both alike to thee.
modernText: even the darkness doesn’t hide from you, but the night shines as the day. The darkness is like light to you.
message: Even the dark, exhausted stretch isn't dark to the one holding you. On a tired day, you're seen and accompanied even where you can't see.

body: I cried unto thee, O LORD: I said, Thou art my refuge and my portion in the land of the living.
modernText: I cried to you, Yahweh. I said, “You are my refuge, my portion in the land of the living.”
message: A refuge and a portion, on a day you feel you have little else. On a worn-out day, your share isn't tied to how much you have left.

body: Hear me speedily, O LORD: my spirit faileth: hide not thy face from me, lest I be like unto them that go down into the pit.
modernText: Hurry to answer me, Yahweh. My spirit fails. Don’t hide your face from me, so that I don’t become like those who go down into the pit.
message: My spirit faileth, the verse says plainly, and asks for a quick answer. On an empty day, you're allowed to say you're running out, and ask for haste.

body: Deliver me, O LORD, from mine enemies: I flee unto thee to hide me.
modernText: Deliver me, Yahweh, from my enemies. I flee to you to hide me.
message: Fleeing to hide, worn out, needing cover. On a tired day, a picture of running for shelter rather than toughing it out in the open.

body: And a man shall be as an hiding place from the wind, and a covert from the tempest; as rivers of water in a dry place, as the shadow of a great rock in a weary land.
modernText: A man shall be as a hiding place from the wind, and a covert from the storm, as streams of water in a dry place, as the shade of a large rock in a weary land.
message: Water in a dry place, shade in a weary land, the exact images for exhaustion. The verse meets the tired right where they are.

body: Speak ye comfortably to Jerusalem, and cry unto her, that her warfare is accomplished, that her iniquity is pardoned: for she hath received of the LORD’s hand double for all her sins.
modernText: “Speak comfortably to Jerusalem; and call out to her that her warfare is accomplished, that her iniquity is pardoned, that she has received of Yahweh’s hand double for all her sins.”
message: Comfort, and news that the hard, draining stretch is finished. For a tired day, the gentle word that the long fight is winding down.

body: Since thou wast precious in my sight, thou hast been honourable, and I have loved thee: therefore will I give men for thee, and people for thy life.
modernText: Since you have been precious and honored in my sight, and I have loved you, therefore I will give people in your place, and nations instead of your life.
message: Called precious and loved, on a day you feel like a worn-out burden. Your worth isn't tied to your energy, it was there before you were tired.

body: I, even I, am he that blotteth out thy transgressions for mine own sake, and will not remember thy sins.
modernText: I, even I, am he who blots out your transgressions for my own sake; and I will not remember your sins.
message: A clean slate, the past wiped and not held against you. On a tired day carrying old weight, this says you can set that part down for good.

body: Hearken unto me, O house of Jacob, and all the remnant of the house of Israel, which are borne by me from the belly, which are carried from the womb:
modernText: “Listen to me, house of Jacob, and all the remnant of the house of Israel, that have been carried from their birth, that have been carried from the womb.
message: Carried your whole life, from the very beginning. On a day you feel like you're dragging yourself, this says you've always been the one being carried.

body: O thou afflicted, tossed with tempest, and not comforted, behold, I will lay thy stones with fair colours, and lay thy foundations with sapphires.
modernText: “You afflicted, tossed with storms, and not comforted, behold, I will set your stones in beautiful colors, and lay your foundations with sapphires.
message: It names the exact feeling, tossed by storm and not comforted, and then turns to rebuild. The verse sees the uncomforted tiredness before it offers anything.

body: And he said unto her, Daughter, thy faith hath made thee whole; go in peace, and be whole of thy plague.
modernText: He said to her, “Daughter, your faith has made you well. Go in peace, and be cured of your disease.”
message: Called daughter, tenderly, told to go in peace, made whole. For a worn-out day, a picture of being gently restored and sent off lighter.

body: And he said to the woman, Thy faith hath saved thee; go in peace.
modernText: He said to the woman, “Your faith has saved you. Go in peace.”
message: Not a lecture, just: you're saved, go in peace. On a tired day, permission to stop striving and simply walk away carried.

body: Now we exhort you, brethren, warn them that are unruly, comfort the feebleminded, support the weak, be patient toward all men.
modernText: We exhort you, brothers: Admonish the disorderly; encourage the faint-hearted; support the weak; be patient toward all.
message: A verse that assumes some people are worn thin and need supporting, not scolding. On a tired day, being the weak one who needs holding up is accounted for.

body: For in that he himself hath suffered being tempted, he is able to succour them that are tempted.
modernText: For in that he himself has suffered being tempted, he is able to help those who are tempted.
message: Able to help, because he's been in the hard place himself. On a tired day, the help comes from someone who actually knows what worn-out feels like.

body: For we have not an high priest which cannot be touched with the feeling of our infirmities; but was in all points tempted like as we are, yet without sin.
modernText: For we don’t have a high priest who can’t be touched with the feeling of our infirmities, but one who has been in all points tempted like we are, yet without sin.
message: Not distant from your exhaustion, but able to feel it, having felt it too. On a tired day, you're understood from the inside, not just observed.

body: Mercy unto you, and peace, and love, be multiplied.
modernText: Mercy to you and peace and love be multiplied.
message: Mercy, peace, and love, not just given but multiplied. On a worn-out day, a blessing of more than enough of the gentle things.

body: And hast borne, and hast patience, and for my name’s sake hast laboured, and hast not fainted.
modernText: You have perseverance and have endured for my name’s sake, and have not grown weary.
message: A direct acknowledgment of your tired, patient labor, and that you haven't given out. On an empty day, being seen for how long you've held on.

body: And I heard a voice from heaven saying unto me, Write, Blessed are the dead which die in the Lord from henceforth: Yea, saith the Spirit, that they may rest from their labours; and their works do follow them.
modernText: I heard a voice from heaven saying, “Write, ‘Blessed are the dead who die in the Lord from now on.’ ” “Yes,” says the Spirit, “that they may rest from their labors; for their works follow with them.”
message: Rest from labors named as a blessing. For a worn-out day, scripture itself honoring rest as something good and longed for, not lazy.

body: LORD, I have loved the habitation of thy house, and the place where thine honour dwelleth.
modernText: Yahweh, I love the habitation of your house, the place where your glory dwells.
message: A longing for a place that feels like home and rest. On a tired day, the ache for somewhere settled to just be.

body: I will abide in thy tabernacle for ever: I will trust in the covert of thy wings. Selah.
modernText: I will dwell in your tent forever. I will take refuge in the shelter of your wings.
message: Abiding, settling in under a wing, for the long haul. On a tired day, a picture of a permanent place to rest, not just a quick break.

body: By thee have I been holden up from the womb: thou art he that took me out of my mother’s bowels: my praise shall be continually of thee.
modernText: I have relied on you from the womb. You are he who took me out of my mother’s womb. I will always praise you.
message: Held up your whole life, from before you can remember. On a worn-out day, a reminder that being carried isn't new, it's been the whole story.

body: But it is good for me to draw near to God: I have put my trust in the Lord GOD, that I may declare all thy works.
modernText: But it is good for me to come close to God. I have made the Lord Yahweh my refuge, that I may tell of all your works.
message: Simply: it is good to be near. On a tired day, you don't have to do anything impressive, just drawing close is the good thing.

body: He will regard the prayer of the destitute, and not despise their prayer.
modernText: He has responded to the prayer of the destitute, and has not despised their prayer.
message: The prayer of the empty-handed, the depleted, regarded and not despised. On a tired day, having nothing to offer is exactly the point.

body: For great is thy mercy toward me: and thou hast delivered my soul from the lowest hell.
modernText: For your loving kindness is great toward me. You have delivered my soul from the lowest Sheol.
message: Delivered from the lowest place, by a mercy called great. On a worn-out day, a reminder that you've been pulled up from the bottom before.

body: I will mention the lovingkindnesses of the LORD, and the praises of the LORD, according to all that the LORD hath bestowed on us, and the great goodness toward the house of Israel, which he hath bestowed on them according to his mercies, and according to the multitude of his lovingkindnesses.
modernText: I will tell of the loving kindnesses of Yahweh and the praises of Yahweh, according to all that Yahweh has given to us, and the great goodness toward the house of Israel, which he has given to them according to his mercies, and according to the multitude of his loving kindnesses.
message: On a day you can't feel much, a practice: just recount the kindnesses. The remembering is its own quiet way of being held up.

body: Though the LORD be high, yet hath he respect unto the lowly: but the proud he knoweth afar off.
modernText: For though Yahweh is high, yet he looks after the lowly; but he knows the proud from afar.
message: The high one paying attention to the lowly, the worn-down. On a tired day, being at a low point is exactly what draws the gaze near.

body: The LORD redeemeth the soul of his servants: and none of them that trust in him shall be desolate.
modernText: Yahweh redeems the soul of his servants. None of those who take refuge in him shall be condemned.
message: The soul redeemed, and a promise: none who trust will be left desolate. On a tired day, a quiet assurance that you won't be abandoned to the emptiness.

body: The LORD is nigh unto them that are of a broken heart; and saveth such as be of a contrite spirit.
modernText: Yahweh is near to those who have a broken heart, and saves those who have a crushed spirit.
message: It doesn't say the brokenness gets fixed or explained. It says you're not alone in it, that something draws near precisely because your heart is broken.

body: He healeth the broken in heart, and bindeth up their wounds.
modernText: He heals the broken in heart, and binds up their wounds.
