message: Not a quick patch, the slow tending of wounds. The verse treats your heartbreak as a real injury that deserves careful binding, not a brush-off.

body: Blessed are they that mourn: for they shall be comforted.
modernText: Blessed are those who mourn, for they shall be comforted.
message: Mourning called blessed, not weakness. The sadness isn't something to hurry past, and the comfort comes to you in it, not instead of it.

body: And God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes; and there shall be no more death, neither sorrow, nor crying, neither shall there be any more pain: for the former things are passed away.
modernText: He will wipe away every tear from their eyes. Death will be no more; neither will there be mourning, nor crying, nor pain, any more. The first things have passed away.”
message: Not yet, but one day, every tear personally wiped. For now, the verse doesn't rush you, it just holds a far-off promise that the crying ends.

body: Jesus wept.
modernText: Jesus wept.
message: The shortest verse in the Bible, and it's him crying at a grave. Even knowing how it ends, he wept. Your tears are in very good company.

body: For his anger endureth but a moment; in his favour is life: weeping may endure for a night, but joy cometh in the morning.
modernText: For his anger is but for a moment. His favor is for a lifetime. Weeping may stay for the night, but joy comes in the morning.
message: It doesn't deny the night of weeping, or how long a night can feel. It just sits with you in it, without pretending the morning is already here.

body: Thou tellest my wanderings: put thou my tears into thy bottle: are they not in thy book?
modernText: You count my wanderings. You put my tears into your container. Aren’t they in your book?
message: Your tears collected and kept, not wasted, not ignored. The tender idea that every one of them is counted and held, nothing lost.

body: To appoint unto them that mourn in Zion, to give unto them beauty for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning, the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness; that they might be called trees of righteousness, the planting of the LORD, that he might be glorified.
modernText: to provide for those who mourn in Zion, to give to them a garland for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning, the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness, that they may be called trees of righteousness, the planting of Yahweh, that he may be glorified.
message: An exchange someday, not a dismissal now. The ashes are real and named first. The beauty comes later, and doesn't erase that they were ashes.

body: Blessed be God, even the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies, and the God of all comfort;
modernText: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies and God of all comfort;
message: Called the God of all comfort, which only matters because the sorrow is real. The verse meets grief by being present to it, not solving it.

body: Who comforteth us in all our tribulation, that we may be able to comfort them which are in any trouble, by the comfort wherewith we ourselves are comforted of God.
modernText: who comforts us in all our affliction, that we may be able to comfort those who are in any affliction, through the comfort with which we ourselves are comforted by God.
message: Comfort in all of it, no grief too deep or too small to qualify. And later, the comfort you receive becomes something you can give.

body: The LORD also will be a refuge for the oppressed, a refuge in times of trouble.
modernText: Yahweh will also be a high tower for the oppressed; a high tower in times of trouble.
message: A refuge in the trouble, not a way around it. Somewhere to be held while it's still hard, not a promise that it stops being hard.

body: God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble.
modernText: God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble.
message: Present, right now, in the trouble, not waiting on the other side of it. On a heavy day, somewhere to sink into that's already here.

body: He is despised and rejected of men; a man of sorrows, and acquainted with grief: and we hid as it were our faces from him; he was despised, and we esteemed him not.
modernText: He was despised and rejected by men, a man of suffering and acquainted with disease. He was despised as one from whom men hide their face; and we didn’t respect him.
message: The verse describes someone who knew sorrow intimately, not from a distance. Your grief is understood by someone who's been inside it.

body: Likewise the Spirit also helpeth our infirmities: for we know not what we should pray for as we ought: but the Spirit itself maketh intercession for us with groanings which cannot be uttered.
modernText: In the same way, the Spirit also helps our weaknesses, for we don’t know how to pray as we ought. But the Spirit himself makes intercession for us with groanings which can’t be uttered.
message: When sadness has no words, when all you can do is groan, this says that wordless ache is itself heard. You don't have to explain it to be understood.

body: And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose.
modernText: We know that all things work together for good for those who love God, for those who are called according to his purpose.
message: Not that the sad thing is good, or that it feels good. Just that it isn't the final, meaningless word. Held gently, not used to rush you.

body: For he hath not despised nor abhorred the affliction of the afflicted; neither hath he hid his face from him; but when he cried unto him, he heard.
modernText: For he has not despised nor abhorred the affliction of the afflicted, Neither has he hidden his face from him; but when he cried to him, he heard.
message: Your grief isn't despised or looked down on. The verse insists it's seen, taken seriously, and heard when you cry out from inside it.

body: I waited patiently for the LORD; and he inclined unto me, and heard my cry.
modernText: I waited patiently for Yahweh. He turned to me, and heard my cry.
message: Waiting in the sadness, and being heard. The crying wasn't ignored. Something leaned down toward it, even while the waiting lasted.

body: He brought me up also out of an horrible pit, out of the miry clay, and set my feet upon a rock, and established my goings.
modernText: He brought me up also out of a horrible pit, out of the miry clay. He set my feet on a rock, and gave me a firm place to stand.
message: An honest name for grief: a horrible pit, miry clay. The verse doesn't pretend it's less than that. It just says you won't be left there forever.

body: But now thus saith the LORD that created thee, O Jacob, and he that formed thee, O Israel, Fear not: for I have redeemed thee, I have called thee by thy name; thou art mine.
modernText: But now Yahweh who created you, Jacob, and he who formed you, Israel, says: “Don’t be afraid, for I have redeemed you. I have called you by your name. You are mine.
message: On a day you feel lost in the sadness, this says you're still claimed, still belong. Your grief doesn't un-name you.

body: When thou passest through the waters, I will be with thee; and through the rivers, they shall not overflow thee: when thou walkest through the fire, thou shalt not be burned; neither shall the flame kindle upon thee.
modernText: When you pass through the waters, I will be with you, and through the rivers, they will not overflow you. When you walk through the fire, you will not be burned, and flame will not scorch you.
message: It doesn't promise you'll skip the deep water of grief. It promises you won't drown in it, and you won't go through it alone.

body: It is of the LORD’s mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not.
modernText: It is because of Yahweh’s loving kindnesses that we are not consumed, because his compassion doesn’t fail.
message: From the Bible's rawest book of grief, a thin thread: you haven't been consumed. Even in the depths, something is quietly keeping you.

body: They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness.
modernText: They are new every morning. Great is your faithfulness.
message: From inside real lament, a quiet anchor: the mercy resets each morning. Not that the grief is gone, just that you don't face it empty-handed.

body: Thou, which hast shewed me great and sore troubles, shalt quicken me again, and shalt bring me up again from the depths of the earth.
modernText: You, who have shown us many and bitter troubles, you will let me live. You will bring us up again from the depths of the earth.
message: It names the troubles as great and sore, doesn't minimize them. And it trusts, quietly, that life comes back, without rushing you there.

body: And I will restore to you the years that the locust hath eaten, the cankerworm, and the caterpiller, and the palmerworm, my great army which I sent among you.
modernText: I will restore to you the years that the swarming locust has eaten, the great locust, the grasshopper, and the caterpillar, my great army, which I sent among you.
message: For the grief of lost time, lost things. A promise of restoration someday, offered gently, without pretending the loss didn't happen.

body: I will be glad and rejoice in thy mercy: for thou hast considered my trouble; thou hast known my soul in adversities;
modernText: I will be glad and rejoice in your loving kindness, for you have seen my affliction. You have known my soul in adversities.
message: Your trouble considered, your soul known in the hard times. On a grieving day, the comfort of being seen all the way down, not just observed.

body: For I know the thoughts that I think toward you, saith the LORD, thoughts of peace, and not of evil, to give you an expected end.
modernText: For I know the thoughts that I think toward you,” says Yahweh, “thoughts of peace, and not of evil, to give you hope and a future.
message: Held loosely on a sad day. Not a demand to feel hopeful, just a quiet whisper that there's more to the story than this grief, when you're ready.

body: But they that wait upon the LORD shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles; they shall run, and not be weary; and they shall walk, and not faint.
modernText: but those who wait for Yahweh will renew their strength. They will mount up with wings like eagles. They will run, and not be weary. They will walk, and not faint.
message: On a day you have no strength left to grieve, the renewing comes to the ones who wait. You don't have to manufacture it, just wait, even sadly.

body: I sought the LORD, and he heard me, and delivered me from all my fears.
modernText: I sought Yahweh, and he answered me, and delivered me from all my fears.
message: The seeking, even through tears, got heard. On a sad day, the reaching out counts, and it reaches someone who answers.

body: This poor man cried, and the LORD heard him, and saved him out of all his troubles.
modernText: This poor man cried, and Yahweh heard him, and saved him out of all his troubles.
message: The poor, grieving man cried, and was heard. On a heavy day, being at a low point is exactly where the hearing happens.

body: Now the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing, that ye may abound in hope, through the power of the Holy Ghost.
modernText: Now may the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing, that you may abound in hope, in the power of the Holy Spirit.
message: Held gently. Not asking you to feel joyful now, just naming that hope has a source outside your grief, for whenever you can reach for it.

body: My flesh and my heart faileth: but God is the strength of my heart, and my portion for ever.
modernText: My flesh and my heart fails, but God is the strength of my heart and my portion forever.
message: Honest about the failing heart, the grief that's worn you through. And steady about a strength underneath it that isn't yours to lose.

body: Let your conversation be without covetousness; and be content with such things as ye have: for he hath said, I will never leave thee, nor forsake thee.
modernText: Be free from the love of money, content with such things as you have, for he has said, “I will in no way leave you, neither will I in any way forsake you.”
message: On a day grief makes you feel utterly alone, this says you're not left, not forsaken. A presence that stays even when it feels like everyone's gone.

body: And the LORD, he it is that doth go before thee; he will be with thee, he will not fail thee, neither forsake thee: fear not, neither be dismayed.
modernText: Yahweh himself is who goes before you. He will be with you. He will not fail you nor forsake you. Don’t be afraid. Don’t be discouraged.”
message: He goes ahead and stays with you, through the hard stretch. On a grieving day, a quiet promise that you're accompanied, not abandoned to it.

body: Thou hast seen it; for thou beholdest mischief and spite, to requite it with thy hand: the poor committeth himself unto thee; thou art the helper of the fatherless.
modernText: But you do see trouble and grief. You consider it to take it into your hand. You help the victim and the fatherless.
message: A tender word for the ones who've lost, who feel unparented by grief. Seen, specifically, in the losing, and not left to carry it alone.

body: Thine eyes did see my substance, yet being unperfect; and in thy book all my members were written, which in continuance were fashioned, when as yet there was none of them.
modernText: Your eyes saw my body. In your book they were all written, the days that were ordained for me, when as yet there were none of them.
message: Known completely, from before you were fully formed. On a grieving day, a reminder that you're held by someone who's seen all of you, even the broken parts.

body: How precious also are thy thoughts unto me, O God! how great is the sum of them!
modernText: How precious to me are your thoughts, God! How vast is their sum!
message: The thoughts toward you called precious, even now, even in the sadness. You haven't dropped off anyone's mind because you're grieving.

body: For I know that my redeemer liveth, and that he shall stand at the latter day upon the earth:
modernText: But as for me, I know that my Redeemer lives. In the end, he will stand upon the earth.
message: Said by a man who'd lost nearly everything. Not a cheerful line, a stubborn one, clung to from the bottom of grief. Sometimes faith is just this, held in the dark.

body: Casting all your care upon him; for he careth for you.
modernText: casting all your worries on him, because he cares for you.
message: All the care, all the grief, handed over to someone who actually cares. On a sad day, permission to set the weight down with someone who wants it.

body: Draw nigh to God, and he will draw nigh to you. Cleanse your hands, ye sinners; and purify your hearts, ye double minded.
modernText: Draw near to God, and he will draw near to you. Cleanse your hands, you sinners. Purify your hearts, you double-minded.
message: The drawing-near goes both ways. On a grieving day, even a small, tired step toward isn't met with distance, but with nearness coming back.

body: He shall cover thee with his feathers, and under his wings shalt thou trust: his truth shall be thy shield and buckler.
modernText: He will cover you with his feathers. Under his wings you will take refuge. His faithfulness is your shield and rampart.
message: A soft, sheltering image for a day you feel raw. Covered, tucked in, somewhere gentle to grieve that doesn't ask you to stop.

body: Come, and let us return unto the LORD: for he hath torn, and he will heal us; he hath smitten, and he will bind us up.
modernText: “Come! Let’s return to Yahweh; for he has torn us to pieces, and he will heal us; he has injured us, and he will bind up our wounds.
message: It doesn't pretend the wound isn't real, or deny it hurt. It just holds, alongside the pain, the quiet hope of being bound up again, in time.

body: They that sow in tears shall reap in joy.
modernText: Those who sow in tears will reap in joy.
message: The tears are named, honored as a kind of sowing, not wasted. The joy is promised for later, gently, without rushing you out of the weeping now.

body: Fear thou not; for I am with thee: be not dismayed; for I am thy God: I will strengthen thee; yea, I will help thee; yea, I will uphold thee with the right hand of my righteousness.
modernText: Don’t you be afraid, for I am with you. Don’t be dismayed, for I am your God. I will strengthen you. Yes, I will help you. Yes, I will uphold you with the right hand of my righteousness.
message: When grief makes everything feel like it's tilting, this is a hand under your arm. Upheld, held steady, not lectured about standing up straighter.

body: For I am persuaded, that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor powers, nor things present, nor things to come,
modernText: For I am persuaded that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor things present, nor things to come, nor powers,
message: For the grief that comes with loss, even death, this says not one thing can cut you off from the love holding you. Not even this.

body: Nor height, nor depth, nor any other creature, shall be able to separate us from the love of God, which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.
modernText: nor height, nor depth, nor any other created thing will be able to separate us from God’s love which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.
message: The verse runs through every category and finds none that can separate you from love. On a day of loss, a stubborn insistence that love outlasts it.

body: Precious in the sight of the LORD is the death of his saints.
modernText: Precious in Yahweh’s sight is the death of his saints.
message: For the grief of losing someone. Their life, and their death, called precious, held as something that mattered deeply. Not a loss that went unnoticed.

body: A time to weep, and a time to laugh; a time to mourn, and a time to dance;
modernText: a time to weep, and a time to laugh; a time to mourn, and a time to dance;
message: Permission for this to be a time to weep, a season to mourn. Grief isn't a failure to be happy, it's a real and rightful time of its own.

body: For the LORD heareth the poor, and despiseth not his prisoners.
modernText: For Yahweh hears the needy, and doesn’t despise his captive people.
message: The grieving, the stuck, the ones who feel imprisoned by sadness, heard and not despised. Being low doesn't disqualify your cry.

body: As one whom his mother comforteth, so will I comfort you; and ye shall be comforted in Jerusalem.
modernText: As one whom his mother comforts, so I will comfort you. You will be comforted in Jerusalem.”
message: The gentlest image in scripture for grief: comforted the way a mother comforts a crying child. Held close, no conditions, nothing to fix first.

body: The LORD thy God in the midst of thee is mighty; he will save, he will rejoice over thee with joy; he will rest in his love, he will joy over thee with singing.
modernText: Yahweh, your God, is among you, a mighty one who will save. He will rejoice over you with joy. He will calm you in his love. He will rejoice over you with singing.
message: Hard to imagine being sung over when you feel this heavy. But the verse says you are, even now, even grieving. Not for fixing yourself first, just for being you.

body: I am weary with my groaning; all the night make I my bed to swim; I water my couch with my tears.
modernText: I am weary with my groaning. Every night I flood my bed. I drench my couch with my tears.
message: It describes crying so hard the bed is soaked, and doesn't apologize for it. On a grieving night, the verse just keeps you company in it, no cleanup required.

body: Depart from me, all ye workers of iniquity; for the LORD hath heard the voice of my weeping.
modernText: Depart from me, all you workers of iniquity, for Yahweh has heard the voice of my weeping.
message: Your weeping has a voice, and it was heard. Not the words, the weeping itself. Even the crying you can't explain reaches someone.

body: The LORD hath heard my supplication; the LORD will receive my prayer.
modernText: Yahweh has heard my supplication. Yahweh accepts my prayer.
message: After all the tears, a quiet certainty: it was heard, it was received. The grieving prayer didn't fall into silence.

body: How long wilt thou forget me, O LORD? for ever? how long wilt thou hide thy face from me?
modernText: How long, Yahweh? Will you forget me forever? How long will you hide your face from me?
message: A raw, unedited lament, right in the Bible. On a day you feel forgotten, this says you're allowed to ask that out loud, no faith-face required.

body: How long shall I take counsel in my soul, having sorrow in my heart daily? how long shall mine enemy be exalted over me?
modernText: How long shall I take counsel in my soul, having sorrow in my heart every day? How long shall my enemy triumph over me?
message: It names sorrow that shows up every single day, not an occasional dip. The verse honors the kind of grief that just keeps coming back.

body: In my distress I called upon the LORD, and cried unto my God: he heard my voice out of his temple, and my cry came before him, even into his ears.
modernText: In my distress I called on Yahweh, and cried to my God. He heard my voice out of his temple. My cry before him came into his ears.
message: From the distress, not after it, the call went up and was heard. On a grieving day, the crying out from the bottom still reaches.

body: Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil: for thou art with me; thy rod and thy staff they comfort me.
modernText: Even though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for you are with me. Your rod and your staff, they comfort me.
message: The valley of the shadow of death, named plainly. The verse doesn't rush you out of it, it just promises you're not walking it alone.

body: Turn thee unto me, and have mercy upon me; for I am desolate and afflicted.
modernText: Turn to me, and have mercy on me, for I am desolate and afflicted.
message: It uses the word desolate and doesn't soften it. On a day grief leaves you empty, a verse that just names it and asks to be turned toward.

body: The troubles of my heart are enlarged: O bring thou me out of my distresses.
modernText: The troubles of my heart are enlarged. Oh bring me out of my distresses.
message: Honest that the heartache feels bigger than usual, swelling. It doesn't argue, it just asks to be brought through, trusting that it can be.

body: Have mercy upon me, O LORD, for I am in trouble: mine eye is consumed with grief, yea, my soul and my belly.
modernText: Have mercy on me, Yahweh, for I am in distress. My eye, my soul, and my body waste away with grief.
message: Grief that's reached the eyes, the soul, the gut, the whole body. The verse takes the full inventory of sadness without tidying any of it.

body: For my life is spent with grief, and my years with sighing: my strength faileth because of mine iniquity, and my bones are consumed.
modernText: For my life is spent with sorrow, my years with sighing. My strength fails because of my iniquity. My bones are wasted away.
message: An unflinching line about grief that's gone on for years, sighing as a way of life. For a long sorrow, a verse that doesn't pretend it's brief.

body: Lord, all my desire is before thee; and my groaning is not hid from thee.
modernText: Lord, all my desire is before you. My groaning is not hidden from you.
message: Even the wordless groaning of grief is seen, not hidden. You don't have to make your sadness presentable for it to be known.

body: My tears have been my meat day and night, while they continually say unto me, Where is thy God?
modernText: My tears have been my food day and night, while they continually ask me, “Where is your God?”
message: Tears described as your food, day and night, how all-consuming grief can be. The verse sits in that, doesn't rush you to a meal.

body: Why art thou cast down, O my soul? and why art thou disquieted in me? hope thou in God: for I shall yet praise him for the help of his countenance.
modernText: Why are you in despair, my soul? Why are you disturbed within me? Hope in God! For I shall still praise him for the saving help of his presence.
message: Talking honestly to your own grieving soul: why so heavy, so restless? Not scolding, just asking, which is sometimes all you can do.

body: Deep calleth unto deep at the noise of thy waterspouts: all thy waves and thy billows are gone over me.
modernText: Deep calls to deep at the noise of your waterfalls. All your waves and your billows have swept over me.
message: The feeling of being completely underwater in grief, wave after wave. The verse names the drowning sensation without pretending you're on dry land.

body: Why art thou cast down, O my soul? and why art thou disquieted within me? hope thou in God: for I shall yet praise him, who is the health of my countenance, and my God.
modernText: Why are you in despair, my soul? Why are you disturbed within me? Hope in God! For I shall still praise him, the saving help of my countenance, and my God.
message: The word 'yet' doing the quiet work. Not 'I'm fine now,' but 'someday, not yet.' Held loosely, offered without rushing the grief.

body: Why art thou cast down, O my soul? and why art thou disquieted within me? hope in God: for I shall yet praise him, who is the health of my countenance, and my God.
modernText: Why are you in despair, my soul? Why are you disturbed within me? Hope in God! For I shall still praise him: my Savior, my helper, and my God.
message: The same honest question to a heavy soul, asked a third time across the psalms. Grief that circles back, and a hope held out gently each time.

body: The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit: a broken and a contrite heart, O God, thou wilt not despise.
modernText: The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit. O God, you will not despise a broken and contrite heart.
message: Your broken heart isn't a problem to hide, it's described as something God won't turn away from. The brokenness itself is welcome here.

body: My heart is sore pained within me: and the terrors of death are fallen upon me.
modernText: My heart is severely pained within me. The terrors of death have fallen on me.
message: It names heart-pain so sharp it feels like dread. The verse doesn't minimize how physical and frightening grief can be.

body: From the end of the earth will I cry unto thee, when my heart is overwhelmed: lead me to the rock that is higher than I.
modernText: From the end of the earth, I will call to you when my heart is overwhelmed. Lead me to the rock that is higher than I.
message: When your heart is overwhelmed with sorrow, this just asks to be led somewhere steadier. You don't have to climb out of the grief alone.

body: I sink in deep mire, where there is no standing: I am come into deep waters, where the floods overflow me.
modernText: I sink in deep mire, where there is no foothold. I have come into deep waters, where the floods overflow me.
message: No footing, going under, in over your head, the verse describes grief exactly. It doesn't offer a ledge, it just names the sinking honestly.

body: Reproach hath broken my heart; and I am full of heaviness: and I looked for some to take pity, but there was none; and for comforters, but I found none.
modernText: Reproach has broken my heart, and I am full of heaviness. I looked for some to take pity, but there was none; for comforters, but I found none.
message: A broken heart and a fullness of heaviness, named plainly. The verse lets grief be as heavy as it actually is, no lightening.

body: In the day of my trouble I sought the Lord: my sore ran in the night, and ceased not: my soul refused to be comforted.
modernText: In the day of my trouble I sought the Lord. My hand was stretched out in the night, and didn’t get tired. My soul refused to be comforted.
message: The most honest line for deep grief: my soul refused to be comforted. The verse doesn't force comfort on you, it sits with the ache that won't be soothed yet.

body: But thou, O Lord, art a God full of compassion, and gracious, longsuffering, and plenteous in mercy and truth.
modernText: But you, Lord, are a merciful and gracious God, slow to anger, and abundant in loving kindness and truth.
message: Patient with you, not rushing your grief. On a sad day, the one you're reaching for is longsuffering, in no hurry for you to be over it.

body: O lord God of my salvation, I have cried day and night before thee:
modernText: Yahweh, the God of my salvation, I have cried day and night before you.
message: From the darkest psalm in the Bible, one that never resolves. Even unanswered, crying day and night, the reaching is honored. Grief doesn't need a tidy ending to be heard.

body: In the multitude of my thoughts within me thy comforts delight my soul.
modernText: In the multitude of my thoughts within me, your comforts delight my soul.
message: When grief multiplies the thoughts, this is the comfort that shows up in the middle of them. Not clearing the thoughts, just soothing the soul inside them.

body: My soul melteth for heaviness: strengthen thou me according unto thy word.
modernText: My soul is weary with sorrow: strengthen me according to your word.
message: A soul melting under the weight of sadness, named exactly. The verse doesn't pretend you're strong, it just asks for strength while you're not.

body: This is my comfort in my affliction: for thy word hath quickened me.
modernText: This is my comfort in my affliction, for your word has revived me.
message: Comfort found inside the affliction, not after it lifts. Something to hold while the grief is still here, not just a promise for later.

body: Let, I pray thee, thy merciful kindness be for my comfort, according to thy word unto thy servant.
modernText: Please let your loving kindness be for my comfort, according to your word to your servant.
message: A simple, grieving ask: let the kindness be what comforts me. Permission to want comfort, and to ask for it plainly, in the middle of the sadness.

body: When my spirit was overwhelmed within me, then thou knewest my path. In the way wherein I walked have they privily laid a snare for me.
modernText: When my spirit was overwhelmed within me, you knew my route. On the path in which I walk, they have hidden a snare for me.
message: Right when your spirit is overwhelmed with grief, the path is still known, by someone who isn't overwhelmed with you. Seen even when you're lost in it.

body: Therefore is my spirit overwhelmed within me; my heart within me is desolate.
modernText: Therefore my spirit is overwhelmed within me. My heart within me is desolate.
message: Overwhelmed, desolate, the verse uses the heaviest words and doesn't flinch. On a grieving day, a verse that matches the actual weight of it.

body: The LORD upholdeth all that fall, and raiseth up all those that be bowed down.
modernText: Yahweh upholds all who fall, and raises up all those who are bowed down.
message: For everyone bent under the weight of grief. Upheld and raised, gently, specifically the ones who feel like they're going down.

body: He will swallow up death in victory; and the Lord GOD will wipe away tears from off all faces; and the rebuke of his people shall he take away from off all the earth: for the LORD hath spoken it.
modernText: He has swallowed up death forever! The Lord Yahweh will wipe away tears from off all faces. He will take the reproach of his people away from off all the earth, for Yahweh has spoken it.
message: A far-off promise for the grief of loss: death itself undone, every tear wiped. Not yet, and it doesn't rush you, but it's held out as true.

body: Sing, O heavens; and be joyful, O earth; and break forth into singing, O mountains: for the LORD hath comforted his people, and will have mercy upon his afflicted.
modernText: Sing, heavens, and be joyful, earth! Break out into singing, mountains, for Yahweh has comforted his people, and will have compassion on his afflicted.
message: Comfort and mercy aimed at the afflicted, the grieving. On a sad day, you're not outside the care, you're exactly who it's for.

body: Therefore the redeemed of the LORD shall return, and come with singing unto Zion; and everlasting joy shall be upon their head: they shall obtain gladness and joy; and sorrow and mourning shall flee away.
modernText: Those ransomed by Yahweh will return, and come with singing to Zion. Everlasting joy shall be on their heads. They will obtain gladness and joy. Sorrow and sighing shall flee away.
message: A picture of a day the sorrow finally lifts and leaves. Held gently, not as a demand to feel it now, just a reminder of where it's heading.

body: I, even I, am he that comforteth you: who art thou, that thou shouldest be afraid of a man that shall die, and of the son of man which shall be made as grass;
modernText: “I, even I, am he who comforts you. Who are you, that you are afraid of man who shall die, and of the son of man who will be made as grass?
message: The comfort is personal and repeated, I, even I. Not a system, someone, leaning in to sit with your grief.

body: For thus saith the high and lofty One that inhabiteth eternity, whose name is Holy; I dwell in the high and holy place, with him also that is of a contrite and humble spirit, to revive the spirit of the humble, and to revive the heart of the contrite ones.
modernText: For the high and lofty One who inhabits eternity, whose name is Holy, says: “I dwell in the high and holy place, with him also who is of a contrite and humble spirit, to revive the spirit of the humble, and to revive the heart of the contrite.
message: Reviving the crushed, the heartbroken. The verse goes looking specifically for the ones at the lowest, grieving place, to breathe life back in.

body: I have seen his ways, and will heal him: I will lead him also, and restore comforts unto him and to his mourners.
modernText: I have seen his ways, and will heal him. I will lead him also, and restore comforts to him and to his mourners.
message: Comforts restored, specifically to the mourners. Grief isn't overlooked here, it's the exact thing being tended to and gently made whole.

body: Thy sun shall no more go down; neither shall thy moon withdraw itself: for the LORD shall be thine everlasting light, and the days of thy mourning shall be ended.
modernText: Your sun will not go down any more, nor will your moon withdraw itself; for Yahweh will be your everlasting light, and the days of your mourning will end.
message: A promise that the long season of grief has an end, even if you can't see it. Held gently, no rushing, just a quiet 'this won't be forever.'

body: The Spirit of the Lord GOD is upon me; because the LORD hath anointed me to preach good tidings unto the meek; he hath sent me to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives, and the opening of the prison to them that are bound;
modernText: The Lord Yahweh’s Spirit is on me, because Yahweh has anointed me to preach good news to the humble. He has sent me to bind up the broken hearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives and release to those who are bound,
message: The stated mission is to bind up broken hearts. On a grieving day, your heartbreak isn't incidental, it's exactly what this came to tend.

body: To proclaim the acceptable year of the LORD, and the day of vengeance of our God; to comfort all that mourn;
modernText: to proclaim the year of Yahweh’s favor and the day of vengeance of our God, to comfort all who mourn,
message: To comfort all that mourn, no exceptions. Whatever your grief is, however private, it's included in the 'all' this came for.

body: Then shall the virgin rejoice in the dance, both young men and old together: for I will turn their mourning into joy, and will comfort them, and make them rejoice from their sorrow.
modernText: Then the virgin will rejoice in the dance; the young men and the old together; for I will turn their mourning into joy, and will comfort them, and make them rejoice from their sorrow.
message: Mourning turned to joy, someday, and comfort for now. The verse holds both, without using the future to dismiss the present grief.

body: But though he cause grief, yet will he have compassion according to the multitude of his mercies.
modernText: For though he causes grief, yet he will have compassion according to the multitude of his loving kindnesses.
message: It doesn't deny the grief, even names it honestly. And it holds, alongside it, compassion described as a multitude, not a trickle.

body: Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.
modernText: “Come to me, all you who labor and are heavily burdened, and I will give you rest.
message: Come heavy laden, grief and all, exactly as weighed down as you are. The invitation isn't to arrive okay, just to come, and set the weight down.

body: Let not your heart be troubled: ye believe in God, believe also in me.
modernText: “Don’t let your heart be troubled. Believe in God. Believe also in me.
message: Said the night before the worst day, to people about to grieve. Not 'don't be sad,' but 'don't let the trouble be the only thing holding your heart.'

body: I will not leave you comfortless: I will come to you.
modernText: I will not leave you orphans. I will come to you.
message: A promise not to be left comfortless, alone in the grief. Comfort coming to you, personally, not something you have to go find.

body: Verily, verily, I say unto you, That ye shall weep and lament, but the world shall rejoice: and ye shall be sorrowful, but your sorrow shall be turned into joy.
modernText: Most certainly I tell you that you will weep and lament, but the world will rejoice. You will be sorrowful, but your sorrow will be turned into joy.
message: It flatly acknowledges you'll weep and grieve, no sugarcoating. The turn to joy comes later, and it doesn't erase that the weeping was real.

body: And ye now therefore have sorrow: but I will see you again, and your heart shall rejoice, and your joy no man taketh from you.
modernText: Therefore you now have sorrow, but I will see you again, and your heart will rejoice, and no one will take your joy away from you.
message: It names the sorrow as real, present, now. The rejoicing is promised, but gently, on the far side of a grief that's honored first.

body: Nevertheless God, that comforteth those that are cast down, comforted us by the coming of Titus;
modernText: Nevertheless, he who comforts the lowly, God, comforted us by the coming of Titus,
message: Comfort aimed specifically at the cast-down, the grieving. Not the thriving, the ones at the bottom are exactly who it finds.

body: O satisfy us early with thy mercy; that we may rejoice and be glad all our days.
modernText: Satisfy us in the morning with your loving kindness, that we may rejoice and be glad all our days.
message: A prayer, from inside a hard season, for mercy to come and gladness to return. Not a denial of the grief, a gentle reaching toward the other side of it.

body: Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.
modernText: “Come to me, all you who labor and are heavily burdened, and I will give you rest.
message: When your mind is stacking tabs faster than you can close them, this lands as a strange kind of invitation: come as you are, overloaded and all, and set it down for a second.

body: Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God.
modernText: In nothing be anxious, but in everything, by prayer and petition with thanksgiving, let your requests be made known to God.
message: It doesn't say flip the anxiety off like a switch. It says you don't have to carry the running list alone, you can hand it over piece by piece.

body: And the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.
modernText: And the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, will guard your hearts and your thoughts in Christ Jesus.
message: The kind of calm that doesn't quite make sense when everything says you should be panicking. That's the one being offered here.

body: Casting all your care upon him; for he careth for you.
modernText: casting all your worries on him, because he cares for you.
message: All of it, not just the parts that seem reasonable to be stressed about. The whole pile gets to be set down somewhere steadier than you.

body: Thou wilt keep him in perfect peace, whose mind is stayed on thee: because he trusteth in thee.
modernText: You will keep whoever’s mind is steadfast in perfect peace, because he trusts in you.
message: Peace here isn't the absence of the noise. It's something to lean your mind against while the noise keeps going.

body: God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble.
modernText: God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble.
message: Not a refuge for later, when things calm down. A refuge for right now, in the middle of it, while it's still loud.

body: Be still, and know that I am God: I will be exalted among the heathen, I will be exalted in the earth.
modernText: “Be still, and know that I am God. I will be exalted among the nations. I will be exalted in the earth.”
message: Be still is a lot to ask when your brain is sprinting. Read it less like an order and more like permission to stop for one breath.

body: Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you: not as the world giveth, give I unto you. Let not your heart be troubled, neither let it be afraid.
modernText: Peace I leave with you. My peace I give to you; not as the world gives, I give to you. Don’t let your heart be troubled, neither let it be fearful.
message: The world's version of calm depends on everything going right. This is a different kind, the kind that can show up even when it isn't.

body: And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose.
modernText: We know that all things work together for good for those who love God, for those who are called according to his purpose.
message: You don't have to see how any of this works out from where you're standing. The verse isn't asking you to, just to not carry the outcome alone.

body: For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.
modernText: For God didn’t give us a spirit of fear, but of power, love, and self-control.
message: The racing, spiraling feeling isn't the truest thing about you. Underneath it there's something steadier that the pressure didn't give and can't take.

body: Have not I commanded thee? Be strong and of a good courage; be not afraid, neither be thou dismayed: for the LORD thy God is with thee whithersoever thou goest.
modernText: Haven’t I commanded you? Be strong and courageous. Don’t be afraid. Don’t be dismayed, for Yahweh your God is with you wherever you go.”
message: Courage here isn't pretending you're fine. It's moving through the heavy thing without being alone in it.

body: Fear thou not; for I am with thee: be not dismayed; for I am thy God: I will strengthen thee; yea, I will help thee; yea, I will uphold thee with the right hand of my righteousness.
modernText: Don’t you be afraid, for I am with you. Don’t be dismayed, for I am your God. I will strengthen you. Yes, I will help you. Yes, I will uphold you with the right hand of my righteousness.
message: When everything feels like it's tilting, this is a hand under your arm, not a lecture about staying upright.

body: Cast thy burden upon the LORD, and he shall sustain thee: he shall never suffer the righteous to be moved.
modernText: Cast your burden on Yahweh and he will sustain you. He will never allow the righteous to be moved.
message: Burden is the right word for it, and this doesn't tell you to carry it better. It tells you where to put it down.

body: Take therefore no thought for the morrow: for the morrow shall take thought for the things of itself. Sufficient unto the day is the evil thereof.
modernText: Therefore don’t be anxious for tomorrow, for tomorrow will be anxious for itself. Each day’s own evil is sufficient.
message: Tomorrow keeps borrowing panic from today. This is permission to only carry the day you're actually in.

body: And which of you with taking thought can add to his stature one cubit?
modernText: Which of you by being anxious can add a cubit to his height?
message: All that worrying, and it never once added an hour or fixed a thing. Strange relief in realizing the spinning was never the part that helped.

body: Trust in the LORD with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding.
modernText: Trust in Yahweh with all your heart, and don’t lean on your own understanding.
message: You've been trying to think your way out of every angle at once. This is the exhale of not having to have it all figured out.

body: In all thy ways acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy paths.
modernText: In all your ways acknowledge him, and he will make your paths straight.
message: You don't have to map the whole path from here. The next step is enough, and you're not plotting it alone.

body: In the multitude of my thoughts within me thy comforts delight my soul.
modernText: In the multitude of my thoughts within me, your comforts delight my soul.
message: When the thoughts multiply at 2am, this is the quiet company that shows up in the middle of them, not after they stop.

body: Now the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing, that ye may abound in hope, through the power of the Holy Ghost.
modernText: Now may the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing, that you may abound in hope, in the power of the Holy Spirit.
message: Hope here isn't forced optimism. It's something filling back in slowly, in the exact places the stress emptied out.

body: Now the Lord of peace himself give you peace always by all means. The Lord be with you all.
modernText: Now may the Lord of peace himself give you peace at all times in all ways. The Lord be with you all.
message: Peace at all times and in every way, which includes this time, this way, this specific kind of overwhelmed.

body: The LORD lift up his countenance upon thee, and give thee peace.
modernText: Yahweh lift up his face toward you, and give you peace.’
message: An old blessing for a tired face. Someone turning toward you with steadiness when you can't find your own.

body: The LORD will give strength unto his people; the LORD will bless his people with peace.
modernText: Yahweh will give strength to his people. Yahweh will bless his people with peace.
message: Strength first, then peace. As if the quiet can't really land until there's something solid holding you up underneath it.

body: For thus saith the Lord GOD, the Holy One of Israel; In returning and rest shall ye be saved; in quietness and in confidence shall be your strength: and ye would not.
modernText: For thus said the Lord Yahweh, the Holy One of Israel, “You will be saved in returning and rest. Your strength will be in quietness and in confidence.” You refused,
message: Quietness and trust as actual strength, not as giving up. The opposite of white-knuckling your way through.

body: Let us therefore come boldly unto the throne of grace, that we may obtain mercy, and find grace to help in time of need.
modernText: Let’s therefore draw near with boldness to the throne of grace, that we may receive mercy and may find grace for help in time of need.
message: You don't have to arrive composed. You can come to this exactly as frazzled as you are and still be met with grace.

body: The LORD shall fight for you, and ye shall hold your peace.
modernText: Yahweh will fight for you, and you shall be still.”
message: Sometimes the bravest thing in the chaos is to stop fighting every front at once and let something else hold the line for a minute.

body: Which of you by taking thought can add one cubit unto his stature?
modernText: “Which of you, by being anxious, can add one moment to his lifespan?
message: The math never works out. All that height of worry, and not a single inch of it ever came back as help.

body: And take heed to yourselves, lest at any time your hearts be overcharged with surfeiting, and drunkenness, and cares of this life, and so that day come upon you unawares.
modernText: “So be careful, or your hearts will be loaded down with carousing, drunkenness, and cares of this life, and that day will come on you suddenly.
message: A gentle nudge to notice when the weight of it all is quietly flattening you, before it becomes the whole day.

body: And let the peace of God rule in your hearts, to the which also ye are called in one body; and be ye thankful.
modernText: And let the peace of God rule in your hearts, to which also you were called in one body, and be thankful.
message: Let peace be the thing that referees the noise, the voice that gets the final call when everything is shouting at once.

body: Commit thy way unto the LORD; trust also in him; and he shall bring it to pass.
modernText: Commit your way to Yahweh. Trust also in him, and he will do this:
message: Committing the way doesn't mean controlling it. It's loosening the grip on the parts that were never yours to hold anyway.

body: Rest in the LORD, and wait patiently for him: fret not thyself because of him who prospereth in his way, because of the man who bringeth wicked devices to pass.
modernText: Rest in Yahweh, and wait patiently for him. Don’t fret because of him who prospers in his way, because of the man who makes wicked plots happen.
message: Rest and wait are hard verbs when you're wired to fix. This is permission to stop performing calm and actually have some.

body: When thou passest through the waters, I will be with thee; and through the rivers, they shall not overflow thee: when thou walkest through the fire, thou shalt not be burned; neither shall the flame kindle upon thee.
modernText: When you pass through the waters, I will be with you, and through the rivers, they will not overflow you. When you walk through the fire, you will not be burned, and flame will not scorch you.
message: It doesn't say you'll skip the hard water. It says you won't go under in it, and you won't go through it alone.

body: The LORD is good, a strong hold in the day of trouble; and he knoweth them that trust in him.
modernText: Yahweh is good, a stronghold in the day of trouble; and he knows those who take refuge in him.
message: On a day this heavy, this is the quiet reminder that you're known, not just by the stress but by something that holds you in it.

body: The LORD thy God in the midst of thee is mighty; he will save, he will rejoice over thee with joy; he will rest in his love, he will joy over thee with singing.
modernText: Yahweh, your God, is among you, a mighty one who will save. He will rejoice over you with joy. He will calm you in his love. He will rejoice over you with singing.
message: Hard to imagine being delighted in when you feel like a mess. This says you are, exactly as frayed as you are right now.

body: He that dwelleth in the secret place of the most High shall abide under the shadow of the Almighty.
modernText: He who dwells in the secret place of the Most High will rest in the shadow of the Almighty.
message: A place to sit down in the middle of the storm. Not a fix for the weather, a shelter while it passes.

body: I will say of the LORD, He is my refuge and my fortress: my God; in him will I trust.
modernText: I will say of Yahweh, “He is my refuge and my fortress; my God, in whom I trust.”
message: Saying it out loud, refuge, even when it doesn't feel true yet. Sometimes steadiness starts as something you choose to lean on.

body: Be strong and of a good courage, fear not, nor be afraid of them: for the LORD thy God, he it is that doth go with thee; he will not fail thee, nor forsake thee.
modernText: Be strong and courageous. Don’t be afraid or scared of them; for Yahweh your God himself is who goes with you. He will not fail you nor forsake you.”
message: Strong and courageous, and then the real reason: not because you've got it, but because you're not facing it by yourself.

body: And David said to Solomon his son, Be strong and of good courage, and do it: fear not, nor be dismayed: for the LORD God, even my God, will be with thee; he will not fail thee, nor forsake thee, until thou hast finished all the work for the service of the house of the LORD.
modernText: David said to Solomon his son, “Be strong and courageous, and do it. Don’t be afraid, nor be dismayed; for Yahweh God, even my God, is with you. He will not fail you, nor forsake you, until all the work for the service of Yahweh’s house is finished.
message: A big task, a tired person, and the same quiet promise underneath it: you won't be left to finish it alone.

body: The LORD is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear? the LORD is the strength of my life; of whom shall I be afraid?
modernText: Yahweh is my light and my salvation. Whom shall I fear? Yahweh is the strength of my life. Of whom shall I be afraid?
message: When the fear has a dozen faces today, this asks a steadying question back: if you're held, then of what, exactly, are you afraid?

body: Wait on the LORD: be of good courage, and he shall strengthen thine heart: wait, I say, on the LORD.
modernText: Wait for Yahweh. Be strong, and let your heart take courage. Yes, wait for Yahweh.
message: Wait is the hardest instruction when you're wired to act. This makes waiting itself an act of strength, not a failure to move.

body: Truly my soul waiteth upon God: from him cometh my salvation.
modernText: My soul rests in God alone. My salvation is from him.
message: The soul quietly waiting, not because nothing's wrong, but because it's found something steadier than solving everything to rest on.

body: It is good that a man should both hope and quietly wait for the salvation of the LORD.
modernText: It is good that a man should hope and quietly wait for the salvation of Yahweh.
message: Even hoping quietly counts as doing something. Sometimes the steadiest move is to wait without forcing the fix.

body: The LORD God is my strength, and he will make my feet like hinds’ feet, and he will make me to walk upon mine high places. To the chief singer on my stringed instruments.
modernText: Yahweh, the Lord, is my strength. He makes my feet like deer’s feet, and enables me to go in high places. For the music director, on my stringed instruments.
message: Steady feet on uneven ground. Not the terrain getting easier, just a surer footing given for the climb.

body: Draw nigh to God, and he will draw nigh to you. Cleanse your hands, ye sinners; and purify your hearts, ye double minded.
modernText: Draw near to God, and he will draw near to you. Cleanse your hands, you sinners. Purify your hearts, you double-minded.
message: The drawing-near goes both ways. Take one small step toward steadier ground and find it was already moving toward you.

body: I have set the LORD always before me: because he is at my right hand, I shall not be moved.
modernText: I have set Yahweh always before me. Because he is at my right hand, I shall not be moved.
message: Keeping something steady in your line of sight so the shaking doesn't get the last word on how the day goes.

body: Trust ye in the LORD for ever: for in the LORD JEHOVAH is everlasting strength:
modernText: Trust in Yahweh forever; for in Yah, Yahweh, is an everlasting Rock.
message: Everlasting strength, the kind that doesn't run out mid-week. Something to lean the whole weight of a hard day against.

body: Therefore being justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ:
modernText: Being therefore justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ;
message: Peace as a settled fact, not a mood you have to manufacture. Something already true underneath however today feels.

body: And let us not be weary in well doing: for in due season we shall reap, if we faint not.
modernText: Let’s not be weary in doing good, for we will reap in due season, if we don’t give up.
message: For the kind of tired that comes from doing the right things with no payoff in sight. A quiet nudge to not give out just yet.

body: He giveth power to the faint; and to them that have no might he increaseth strength.
modernText: He gives power to the weak. He increases the strength of him who has no might.
message: Specifically for the empty tank. Strength offered to the exact people who feel like they have none left to give.

body: But they that wait upon the LORD shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles; they shall run, and not be weary; and they shall walk, and not faint.
modernText: but those who wait for Yahweh will renew their strength. They will mount up with wings like eagles. They will run, and not be weary. They will walk, and not faint.
message: Not a promise you'll stop being tired, but that the running won't be fueled by you alone. Something gets renewed that you didn't manufacture.

body: Blessed be God, even the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies, and the God of all comfort;
modernText: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies and God of all comfort;
message: Before anything gets fixed, there's comfort. The kind that meets you in the stress instead of waiting for you to be past it.

body: I will both lay me down in peace, and sleep: for thou, LORD, only makest me dwell in safety.
modernText: In peace I will both lay myself down and sleep, for you, Yahweh alone, make me live in safety.
message: The verse for when your body is in bed but your brain is still at the office. Rest offered not because everything's handled, but because you're held.

body: I laid me down and slept; I awaked; for the LORD sustained me.
modernText: I laid myself down and slept. I awakened; for Yahweh sustains me.
message: You made it to morning. Not because you white-knuckled through the night, but because something steadier than you kept watch.

body: Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil: for thou art with me; thy rod and thy staff they comfort me.
modernText: Even though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for you are with me. Your rod and your staff, they comfort me.
message: Even walking straight through the worst of it, the promise isn't 'no shadow.' It's 'not alone in the shadow.'

body: I sought the LORD, and he heard me, and delivered me from all my fears.
modernText: I sought Yahweh, and he answered me, and delivered me from all my fears.
message: Not just the big fears, all of them. The low-grade background dread you forgot you were even carrying.

body: What time I am afraid, I will trust in thee.
modernText: When I am afraid, I will put my trust in you.
message: It doesn't pretend you won't be afraid. It just gives you somewhere to put the fear when you are.

body: In God I will praise his word, in God I have put my trust; I will not fear what flesh can do unto me.
modernText: In God, I praise his word. In God, I put my trust. I will not be afraid. What can flesh do to me?
message: What can flesh really do next to the thing holding you. A quiet resizing of what felt enormous a second ago.

body: I called upon the LORD in distress: the LORD answered me, and set me in a large place.
modernText: Out of my distress, I called on Yah. Yah answered me with freedom.
message: Called out of the tight, pressed-in place and given room to breathe. Sometimes the answer to stress is just space.

body: The LORD is on my side; I will not fear: what can man do unto me?
modernText: Yahweh is on my side. I will not be afraid. What can man do to me?
message: If help is actually on your side, the list of things to brace against gets a lot shorter.

body: From the end of the earth will I cry unto thee, when my heart is overwhelmed: lead me to the rock that is higher than I.
modernText: From the end of the earth, I will call to you when my heart is overwhelmed. Lead me to the rock that is higher than I.
message: When your heart is overwhelmed is literally the condition this was written for. Led up to something higher and steadier than where you're standing.

body: Cause me to hear thy lovingkindness in the morning; for in thee do I trust: cause me to know the way wherein I should walk; for I lift up my soul unto thee.
modernText: Cause me to hear your loving kindness in the morning, for I trust in you. Cause me to know the way in which I should walk, for I lift up my soul to you.
message: A morning ask: let me hear something kind before the day starts talking. Point me somewhere before the noise does.

body: He shall not be afraid of evil tidings: his heart is fixed, trusting in the LORD.
modernText: He will not be afraid of evil news. His heart is steadfast, trusting in Yahweh.
message: For the person bracing for the next notification. A steadiness that doesn't flinch every time the phone buzzes.

body: Though I walk in the midst of trouble, thou wilt revive me: thou shalt stretch forth thine hand against the wrath of mine enemies, and thy right hand shall save me.
modernText: Though I walk in the middle of trouble, you will revive me. You will stretch out your hand against the wrath of my enemies. Your right hand will save me.
message: Not lifted out of the trouble, revived in the middle of walking through it. Kept moving when you thought you were out of gas.

body: Therefore will not we fear, though the earth be removed, and though the mountains be carried into the midst of the sea;
modernText: Therefore we won’t be afraid, though the earth changes, though the mountains are shaken into the heart of the seas;
message: Even if the ground itself moved, the verse says we won't fear. A stubborn calm that doesn't depend on things staying put.

body: Though the waters thereof roar and be troubled, though the mountains shake with the swelling thereof. Selah.
modernText: though its waters roar and are troubled, though the mountains tremble with their swelling.
message: Let the waters roar. The point isn't that it gets quiet, it's that something stays unmoved while it's loud.

body: When I said, My foot slippeth; thy mercy, O LORD, held me up.
modernText: When I said, “My foot is slipping!” Your loving kindness, Yahweh, held me up.
message: That moment you felt yourself going under, and something caught you. Mercy showing up right at the slip.

body: The LORD shall preserve thee from all evil: he shall preserve thy soul.
modernText: Yahweh will keep you from all evil. He will keep your soul.
message: Preserved, kept, watched. Steady words for a mind that's been running worst-case scenarios all day.

body: The LORD shall preserve thy going out and thy coming in from this time forth, and even for evermore.
modernText: Yahweh will keep your going out and your coming in, from this time forward, and forever more.
message: The ordinary comings and goings, the commute, the errands, the whole anxious day, all of it watched over.

body: For I the LORD thy God will hold thy right hand, saying unto thee, Fear not; I will help thee.
modernText: For I, Yahweh your God, will hold your right hand, saying to you, ‘Don’t be afraid. I will help you.’
message: A hand actually taking yours. Not a pep talk from across the room, closer than that.

body: But now thus saith the LORD that created thee, O Jacob, and he that formed thee, O Israel, Fear not: for I have redeemed thee, I have called thee by thy name; thou art mine.
modernText: But now Yahweh who created you, Jacob, and he who formed you, Israel, says: “Don’t be afraid, for I have redeemed you. I have called you by your name. You are mine.
message: Called by name, claimed. On a day you feel like a number on everyone's to-do list, you're known by yours.

body: For the mountains shall depart, and the hills be removed; but my kindness shall not depart from thee, neither shall the covenant of my peace be removed, saith the LORD that hath mercy on thee.
modernText: For the mountains may depart, and the hills be removed; but my loving kindness will not depart from you, and my covenant of peace will not be removed,” says Yahweh who has mercy on you.
message: Even if the solid things shift, the kindness doesn't. Something that outlasts what you thought was permanent.

body: And the work of righteousness shall be peace; and the effect of righteousness quietness and assurance for ever.
modernText: The work of righteousness will be peace, and the effect of righteousness, quietness and confidence forever.
message: Real peace isn't the loud kind that performs calm. It's quiet, and it just stays.

body: Behold, God is my salvation; I will trust, and not be afraid: for the LORD JEHOVAH is my strength and my song; he also is become my salvation.
modernText: Behold, God is my salvation. I will trust, and will not be afraid; for Yah, Yahweh, is my strength and song; and he has become my salvation.”
message: Saying it out loud, I will trust and not be afraid, even before the feeling catches up. Sometimes steadiness starts as a sentence.

body: For I know the thoughts that I think toward you, saith the LORD, thoughts of peace, and not of evil, to give you an expected end.
modernText: For I know the thoughts that I think toward you,” says Yahweh, “thoughts of peace, and not of evil, to give you hope and a future.
message: When your own head runs nothing but worst cases, this says the thoughts toward you are peace. A kinder narrator than the one you've been listening to.

body: Blessed is the man that trusteth in the LORD, and whose hope the LORD is.
modernText: “Blessed is the man who trusts in Yahweh, and whose confidence is in Yahweh.
message: Blessed is the one who leans their weight somewhere steadier than their own planning. Permission to stop being your own foundation.

body: For he shall be as a tree planted by the waters, and that spreadeth out her roots by the river, and shall not see when heat cometh, but her leaf shall be green; and shall not be careful in the year of drought, neither shall cease from yielding fruit.
modernText: For he will be as a tree planted by the waters, who spreads out its roots by the river, and will not fear when heat comes, but its leaf will be green, and will not be concerned in the year of drought. It won’t cease from yielding fruit.
message: Roots down by the water, so the heat comes and the leaf stays green. Steadiness that doesn't depend on the conditions being good.

body: Therefore I say unto you, Take no thought for your life, what ye shall eat, or what ye shall drink; nor yet for your body, what ye shall put on. Is not the life more than meat, and the body than raiment?
modernText: Therefore I tell you, don’t be anxious for your life: what you will eat, or what you will drink; nor yet for your body, what you will wear. Isn’t life more than food, and the body more than clothing?
message: An old way of saying stop borrowing tomorrow's panic. Your life is more than the list you're stressing over.

body: Behold the fowls of the air: for they sow not, neither do they reap, nor gather into barns; yet your heavenly Father feedeth them. Are ye not much better than they?
modernText: See the birds of the sky, that they don’t sow, neither do they reap, nor gather into barns. Your heavenly Father feeds them. Aren’t you of much more value than they?
message: The birds aren't out there spiraling about provision, and they're fine. A nudge that you might be more cared for than the anxiety suggests.

body: But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you.
modernText: But seek first God’s Kingdom, and his righteousness; and all these things will be given to you as well.
message: One thing to orient around instead of twenty. When everything feels urgent, this quietly reorders the pile.

body: And he saith unto them, Why are ye fearful, O ye of little faith? Then he arose, and rebuked the winds and the sea; and there was a great calm.
modernText: He said to them, “Why are you fearful, O you of little faith?” Then he got up, rebuked the wind and the sea, and there was a great calm.
message: Said to people in an actual sinking boat. Not a dismissal of the storm, a question about who's in it with them.

body: And he arose, and rebuked the wind, and said unto the sea, Peace, be still. And the wind ceased, and there was a great calm.
modernText: He awoke, and rebuked the wind, and said to the sea, “Peace! Be still!” The wind ceased, and there was a great calm.
message: Three words to a storm: peace, be still. For the internal weather too, not just the lake.

body: As soon as Jesus heard the word that was spoken, he saith unto the ruler of the synagogue, Be not afraid, only believe.
modernText: But Jesus, when he heard the message spoken, immediately said to the ruler of the synagogue, “Don’t be afraid, only believe.”
message: Right after the worst news, this. Not 'it's fine,' just 'don't do this part alone, and keep holding on.'

body: These things I have spoken unto you, that in me ye might have peace. In the world ye shall have tribulation: but be of good cheer; I have overcome the world.
modernText: I have told you these things, that in me you may have peace. In the world you have trouble; but cheer up! I have overcome the world.”
message: It's honest: in the world you'll have trouble. The peace isn't instead of the trouble, it's underneath it.

body: For to be carnally minded is death; but to be spiritually minded is life and peace.
modernText: For the mind of the flesh is death, but the mind of the Spirit is life and peace;
message: Where your mind lives changes how the day feels. A quiet suggestion about where to let it rest.

body: For I am persuaded, that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor powers, nor things present, nor things to come,
modernText: For I am persuaded that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor things present, nor things to come, nor powers,
message: Persuaded that not one thing on the whole list, not the future, not the 3am fear, can cut you off from the love holding you.

body: Nor height, nor depth, nor any other creature, shall be able to separate us from the love of God, which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.
modernText: nor height, nor depth, nor any other created thing will be able to separate us from God’s love which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.
message: Nothing in all creation. The verse runs out of categories before it finds one that can separate you from it.

body: There hath no temptation taken you but such as is common to man: but God is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able; but will with the temptation also make a way to escape, that ye may be able to bear it.
modernText: No temptation has taken you except what is common to man. God is faithful, who will not allow you to be tempted above what you are able, but will with the temptation also make the way of escape, that you may be able to endure it.
message: Whatever's pressing in isn't unprecedented, and it isn't a sealed room. There's always a door, even when you can't see it yet.

body: We are troubled on every side, yet not distressed; we are perplexed, but not in despair;
modernText: We are pressed on every side, yet not crushed; perplexed, yet not to despair;
message: Pressed on every side but not crushed. Honest about the pressure, stubborn about the not-crushed part.

body: And he said unto me, My grace is sufficient for thee: for my strength is made perfect in weakness. Most gladly therefore will I rather glory in my infirmities, that the power of Christ may rest upon me.
modernText: He has said to me, “My grace is sufficient for you, for my power is made perfect in weakness.” Most gladly therefore I will rather glory in my weaknesses, that the power of Christ may rest on me.
message: The grace doesn't wait for you to get strong. It shows up in the depleted, running-on-fumes version of you.

body: That he would grant you, according to the riches of his glory, to be strengthened with might by his Spirit in the inner man;
modernText: that he would grant you, according to the riches of his glory, that you may be strengthened with power through his Spirit in the inner person,
message: Strength on the inside, where the stress actually lives. Not just powering through, being reinforced underneath.

body: I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me.
modernText: I can do all things through Christ, who strengthens me.
message: Not a hype slogan. A quiet 'you're not drawing on your own tank for this' on a day the tank is empty.

body: But my God shall supply all your need according to his riches in glory by Christ Jesus.
modernText: My God will supply every need of yours according to his riches in glory in Christ Jesus.
message: Need, not every want. A promise sized to what the day actually requires, which is usually less than the anxiety insists.

body: Set your affection on things above, not on things on the earth.
modernText: Set your mind on the things that are above, not on the things that are on the earth.
message: When every small thing feels huge, this lifts your eyes for a second. Not to dismiss it, to resize it.

body: Now our Lord Jesus Christ himself, and God, even our Father, which hath loved us, and hath given us everlasting consolation and good hope through grace,
modernText: Now our Lord Jesus Christ himself, and God our Father, who loved us and gave us eternal comfort and good hope through grace,
message: Everlasting comfort and good hope, already given. Not earned by holding it together, just given.

body: Comfort your hearts, and stablish you in every good word and work.
modernText: comfort your hearts and establish you in every good work and word.
message: Comfort your heart and steady you. The two things the stress has been quietly chipping at, named and addressed.

body: Let your conversation be without covetousness; and be content with such things as ye have: for he hath said, I will never leave thee, nor forsake thee.
modernText: Be free from the love of money, content with such things as you have, for he has said, “I will in no way leave you, neither will I in any way forsake you.”
message: I will never leave thee. On a day everyone needs something and no one's got you, this says someone does, and isn't going anywhere.

body: So that we may boldly say, The Lord is my helper, and I will not fear what man shall do unto me.
modernText: So that with good courage we say, “The Lord is my helper. I will not fear. What can man do to me?”
message: A helper on your side changes the math on fear. You can say 'I will not fear' and actually mean it.

body: Wherefore seeing we also are compassed about with so great a cloud of witnesses, let us lay aside every weight, and the sin which doth so easily beset us, and let us run with patience the race that is set before us,
modernText: Therefore let’s also, seeing we are surrounded by so great a cloud of witnesses, lay aside every weight and the sin which so easily entangles us, and let’s run with perseverance the race that is set before us,
message: Lay aside the weight, the verse says, like it's a thing you're allowed to set down. Not every weight is yours to run with.

body: Looking unto Jesus the author and finisher of our faith; who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising the shame, and is set down at the right hand of the throne of God.
modernText: looking to Jesus, the author and perfecter of faith, who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising its shame, and has sat down at the right hand of the throne of God.
message: One steady thing to keep your eyes on while you run, so the chaos in your peripheral vision stops setting the pace.

body: Humble yourselves therefore under the mighty hand of God, that he may exalt you in due time:
modernText: Humble yourselves therefore under the mighty hand of God, that he may exalt you in due time,
message: Letting go of needing to force the outcome. Trusting the timing to something that isn't panicking the way you are.

body: But the God of all grace, who hath called us unto his eternal glory by Christ Jesus, after that ye have suffered a while, make you perfect, stablish, strengthen, settle you.
modernText: But may the God of all grace, who called you to his eternal glory by Christ Jesus, after you have suffered a little while, perfect, establish, strengthen, and settle you.
message: After the hard stretch, not a vague 'it gets better,' but settled, strengthened, steadied. The after is part of the promise.

body: Search me, O God, and know my heart: try me, and know my thoughts:
modernText: Search me, God, and know my heart. Try me, and know my thoughts.
message: The anxious thoughts you can't even organize, this invites them to be seen instead of hidden. Known all the way down, mess included.

body: And see if there be any wicked way in me, and lead me in the way everlasting.
modernText: See if there is any wicked way in me, and lead me in the everlasting way.
message: After the searching, a gentle leading. Not judged for what's in there, guided through it.

body: Cease from anger, and forsake wrath: fret not thyself in any wise to do evil.
modernText: Cease from anger, and forsake wrath. Don’t fret; it leads only to evildoing.
message: Fret not is a tall order, so read it as permission more than command. The fretting was never the thing holding your life together anyway.

body: And I said, Oh that I had wings like a dove! for then would I fly away, and be at rest.
modernText: I said, “Oh that I had wings like a dove! Then I would fly away, and be at rest.
message: That exact fantasy of just disappearing somewhere quiet, the Bible has it too. You're not weak for wishing you could fly away from it for a while.

body: He only is my rock and my salvation; he is my defence; I shall not be greatly moved.
modernText: He alone is my rock, my salvation, and my fortress. I will never be greatly shaken.
message: Not 'never moved,' just 'not greatly moved.' Room to be shaken without being toppled.

body: My soul, wait thou only upon God; for my expectation is from him.
modernText: My soul, wait in silence for God alone, for my expectation is from him.
message: Pointing your expectation at something steadier than outcomes you can't control. A quieter place to hang your hope.

body: Trust in him at all times; ye people, pour out your heart before him: God is a refuge for us. Selah.
modernText: Trust in him at all times, you people. Pour out your heart before him. God is a refuge for us.
message: Pour out your heart, it says, not tidy it up first. You can bring the unfiltered version here.

body: My flesh and my heart faileth: but God is the strength of my heart, and my portion for ever.
modernText: My flesh and my heart fails, but God is the strength of my heart and my portion forever.
message: Honest about the failing part, your body and your nerve giving out, and just as honest about the strength that isn't yours to run out of.

body: In the day of my trouble I will call upon thee: for thou wilt answer me.
